extraction_notes.note: The prompt gives proof sketches rigor semi_formal, while the finishing step warns that rigor belongs only on results; kept rigor on the two sketches per the prompt (PP2, a one-sentence 'similarly', has none).

Assumption 2-dagger uses an undeclared environment (assumpt) that the facts parser does not report; extracted as a prose assumption from 'Assume that' to the end of its display, so the mid-sentence start warning is a false alarm.
Theorem 4.1's parts (i) and (ii) are proved separately (Appendix C.4) and used separately, so each item is a nested claim and the proofs and sketches point to the parts.
Fact B.1 and Fact B.2 are uncited elementary properties stated without proof; retyped as claims (Hard rule 4).
Proposition 5.1 is called a direct generalization of Billingsley's Theorem 12.3 and is not proved; marked external rather than paper.

Most related-work citations (only four cited results stated in full were kept as external theorems), the concluding future-work directions (not mathematical open problems), the omitted proof-framework figures, and running commentary between results were not extracted.
The examples' update rules are displayed numbered equations; the algorithm steps reuse the equation rows as their verbatim statements, so each step has the same span as its nested equation node.

metadata.extraction_comment: In the proof of Theorem 4.1 (ii) the text applies 'Theorem 4.1' where the argument needs Corollary 5.1 (announced just before the proof); that \ref is kept as a mention and Corollary 5.1 is linked by name.

nodes.name: Root finding for two coupled operators
nodes.statement: We consider two unknown Lipschitz operators, $F:{\mathbb R}^{d_x}\times{\mathbb R}^{d_y}\rightarrow{\mathbb R}^{d_x}$ and $G:{\mathbb R}^{d_x}\times{\mathbb R}^{d_y}\rightarrow{\mathbb R}^{d_y}$, and aim to find a root pair $(x^{\star}, y^{\star})$ that satisfies \begin{equation} \left\{ \begin{aligned} &F(x^{\star},y^{\star}) = 0,\\ &G(x^{\star},y^{\star}) = 0. \end{aligned}\right. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Find a root pair $(x^\star,y^\star)$ with $F(x^\star,y^\star)=0$ and $G(x^\star,y^\star)=0$ for unknown Lipschitz operators $F,G$.

nodes.name: Coupled root equations (1)
nodes.statement: \left\{ \begin{aligned} &F(x^{\star},y^{\star}) = 0,\\ &G(x^{\star},y^{\star}) = 0. \end{aligned}\right.
nodes.label: prob:FG

nodes.name: Two-time-scale stochastic approximation
nodes.statement: Using this oracle, we iteratively update estimates $x_{n}$ and $y_{n}$ via \begin{subequations} \begin{align} x_{n+1} &= x_{n} - \alpha_{n}\left(F(x_{n},y_{n}) + \xi_{n}\right), \\ y_{n+1} &= y_{n} - \beta_{n}\left(G(x_{n},y_{n}) + \psi_{n}\right), \end{align} \end{subequations} where $x_{0}$ and $y_{0}$ are initialized arbitrarily, $\xi_n$ and $\psi_n$ are martingale difference noise, and $\alpha_{n}$, $\beta_{n}$ are step sizes satisfying $\beta_{n}\ll \alpha_{n}$, in ${\mathbb R}^{d_x}$ and ${\mathbb R}^{d_y}$.
nodes.statement_short: Two-time-scale SA: update fast iterate $x_n$ with step $\alpha_n$ and slow iterate $y_n$ with step $\beta_n \ll \alpha_n$ using noisy evaluations of $F,G$.

nodes.name: Fast-time-scale update (2a)
nodes.statement: x_{n+1} &= x_{n} - \alpha_{n}\left(F(x_{n},y_{n}) + \xi_{n}\right),
nodes.label: alg:x

nodes.name: Slow-time-scale update (2b)
nodes.statement: y_{n+1} &= y_{n} - \beta_{n}\left(G(x_{n},y_{n}) + \psi_{n}\right),
nodes.label: alg:y

nodes.name: Fast iterate and slow iterate
nodes.statement: Accordingly, $x_n$ and $y_n$ are termed the \textit{fast iterate} and \textit{slow iterate}, with their updates referred to as fast-time-scale and slow-time-scale updates, respectively.

nodes.name: Double-loop interpretation of two-time-scale SA (3)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} & \text{Inner loop: compute } x = H(y) , \text{ or equivalently, solve } F(x, y) = 0 \text{ for a fixed } y, \\ & \text{Outer loop: iteratively find the root of } G(H(y), y) = 0. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eq:two-loop-approx

nodes.name: Operator H
nodes.statement: Here $H(y)$ is the unique solution to $F(x,y) = 0$ for a given $y$, satisfying $x^\star = H(y^\star)$.

nodes.name: Decoupled convergence
nodes.statement: Previous studies have shown that the convergence rates of these error terms depend sorely on their respective step sizes \citep{konda2004convergence, mokkadem2006convergence, kaledin2020finite, han2024finite}, a property known as \textit{decoupled convergence}~\citep{han2024finite}.

nodes.name: Decoupled CLT and convergence rates for two-time-scale SA (prior work)
nodes.statement: In particular, under certain regular conditions, it holds that $ \beta_{n}^{-1/2} (y_{n} - y^\star)$ and $ \alpha_{n}^{-1/2} (x_{n} - H(y_{n}))$ both convergence weakly to Gaussian distributions, with non-asymptotic convergence rates ${\mathbb E} \| y_n - y^\star \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\beta_n) $ and ${\mathbb E} \| x_n - H(y_n) \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\alpha_n)$.
nodes.origin_citation: Konda & Tsitsiklis 2004; Mokkadem & Pelletier 2006; Kaledin et al. 2020; Han et al. 2024
conclusions: $ \beta_{n}^{-1/2} (y_{n} - y^\star)$ and $ \alpha_{n}^{-1/2} (x_{n} - H(y_{n}))$ both convergence weakly to Gaussian distributions
${\mathbb E} \| y_n - y^\star \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\beta_n) $ and ${\mathbb E} \| x_n - H(y_n) \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\alpha_n)$

nodes.name: CLT for linear two-time-scale SA (Konda-Tsitsiklis)
nodes.statement: For linear $F$ and $G$, \citep{konda2004convergence} showed that $\beta_n^{-1/2} (y_n - y^\star)$ weakly converges to a normal distribution under martingale difference noise.
conclusions: $\beta_n^{-1/2} (y_n - y^\star)$ weakly converges to a normal distribution

nodes.name: Finite-time decoupled rates for linear two-time-scale SA (Kaledin et al.)
nodes.statement: Inspired by this, \cite{kaledin2020finite} derived finite-time convergence rates, proving that ${\mathbb E} \| y_n - y^\star \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\beta_n)$ and ${\mathbb E} \| x_n - H(y_n) \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\alpha_n)$ for both the martingale noise and Markovian noise.
conclusions: ${\mathbb E} \| y_n - y^\star \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\beta_n)$ and ${\mathbb E} \| x_n - H(y_n) \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\alpha_n)$

nodes.name: High-probability rates for sparse projection two-time-scale SA (Dalal et al.)
nodes.statement: Fora sparse projection variant, \cite{dalal2020tale} showed that $\| y_n - y^\star \| = \widetilde{{\mathcal O}} (\sqrt{\beta_n})$ and $\| x_n - x^\star \| = \widetilde{{\mathcal O}} (\sqrt{\alpha_n})$ with high probability.

nodes.name: Joint weak convergence for nonlinear two-time-scale SA (Mokkadem-Pelletier)
nodes.statement: For the general nonlinear case, \cite{mokkadem2006convergence} established a joint weak convergence limit for $\alpha_n^{-1/2} (x_n - x^\star)$ and $\beta_n^{-1/2} (y_n - y^\star)$ under local linearity.

nodes.name: Euclidean and spectral norm
nodes.statement: For a vector $x$, $\| x \|$ denotes the Euclidean norm, while for a matrix $A$, $\| A \|$ denotes the spectral norm.

nodes.name: Asymptotic notation
nodes.statement: We use $o(\cdot)$, ${\mathcal O}(\cdot)$, $\Omega(\cdot)$, and $\Theta(\cdot)$ to hide universal constants and $\widetilde{{\mathcal O}}(\cdot)$ to hide both universal constants and log factors.

nodes.name: Stochastic order notation
nodes.statement: The notation $o_p(1)$ and ${\mathcal O}_p(1)$ indicate convergence in probability and stochastic boundedness, respectively.

nodes.name: Inequality up to constants
nodes.statement: For two non-negative numbers $a$ and $b$, $a \lesssim b$ indicates the existence of a positive number $C$ such that $a \le Cb$ with $C$ depending on parameters of no interest.

nodes.name: Asymptotic equivalence of sequences
nodes.statement: For two positive sequences $\{ a_n \}$ and $\{ b_n \}$, $a_n \sim b_n$ signifies $\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n / b_n = 1$.

nodes.name: Distribution notation
nodes.statement: For a random variable ${\textnormal{X}}$, ${\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi$ means ${\textnormal{X}}$ follows the distribution $\pi$.

nodes.name: Weak convergence and convergence in probability notation
nodes.statement: We use $\Rightarrow$ to denote weak convergence or convergence in distribution and $\overset{p}{\rightarrow}$ to signify convergence in probability.

nodes.name: Step-size ratio
nodes.statement: For the step size sequences $\{ \alpha_{n} \}_{n=0}^\infty$ and $\{ \beta_{n} \}_{n=0}^\infty$, their ratio is defined as $\kappa_{n} := \frac{\beta_{n}}{\alpha_{n}}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\kappa_n := \beta_n/\alpha_n$, the ratio of slow to fast step sizes.

nodes.name: Empty-sum convention
nodes.statement: For $m < n$ we stipulate $\sum_{i=n}^{m} \alpha_{i} = \sum_{i=n}^{m} \beta_{i} = 0 $.

nodes.name: Identity matrix
nodes.statement: The identity matrix is denoted by ${I}$, with an appropriate size.

nodes.name: Standard Brownian motion
nodes.statement: The standard $d$-dimensional Brownian motion is represented as ${\textnormal{W}}^d(t)$.

nodes.name: Space of continuous functions
nodes.statement: Given two metric spaces $(D, d_D)$ and $(E, d_E)$, $C(D; E)$ denotes the space of all $E$-valued continuous functions defined on the domain $D$.

nodes.name: Shorthand for real-valued continuous functions
nodes.statement: When $E=\mathbb{R}$, we use $C(D)$ in shorthand.

nodes.name: Bounded and compactly supported smooth function spaces
nodes.statement: Furthermore, we use $C_b(D)$ to denote the subspace of $C(D)$ consisting of all continuous bounded functions, and $C^m_c(D)$ for the subspace of $C(D)$ containing all functions with compact support and continuous $m$-th order derivatives.

nodes.name: Metric of uniform convergence on compact sets
nodes.statement: Following the approach in \cite{whitt1970weak}, we equip this space with the following metric: for any $f,g \in C([0, \infty); {\mathbb R}^d)$, \begin{equation*} \rho (f, g) := \ssum{j}{1}{\infty} 2^{-j} \frac{\rho_j(f,g)}{1+\rho_j(f,g)} \ \text{with} \ \rho_{j} (f, g) := \max_{0 \le t \le j} \| f(t) - g(t) \|. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Metric $\rho$ on $C([0,\infty);\mathbb{R}^d)$: weighted sum over $j$ of sup-distances on $[0,j]$.

nodes.name: Metric rho induces uniform convergence on compacts
nodes.statement: This metric induces the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets, i.e., $\rho(f,g) \to 0$ if and only if $\rho_j (f,g) \to 0$ for each positive integer $j$.
conclusions: This metric induces the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets

nodes.name: Completeness and separability of the continuous-path space
nodes.statement: Furthermore, $(C([0, \infty); {\mathbb R}^d), \rho) $ is a complete separable metric space~\citep[Theorem~1]{whitt1970weak}.
conclusions: $(C([0, \infty); {\mathbb R}^d), \rho) $ is a complete separable metric space

nodes.name: Random function
nodes.statement: A random element in this space can be interpreted as a stochastic process indexed by $[0, \infty)$, with the state space ${\mathbb R}^d$ and continuous sample paths. For brevity, we refer to such random elements as random functions in $C([0, \infty); {\mathbb R}^d)$.

nodes.name: Tightness of random functions
nodes.statement: Let $\{ {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=0}^\infty$ be a sequence of random functions in $C(D; E)$. The sequence $\{ {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=0}^\infty$ is \textit{tight}, if for any ${\varepsilon} > 0$, there exists a compact set $K \subset C(D; E)$ such that ${\mathbb P}( {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \in K ) \ge 1 - {\varepsilon}$ for any $n$.
nodes.genus: sequence of random functions in $C(D; E)$
differentia: for any ${\varepsilon} > 0$, there exists a compact set $K \subset C(D; E)$ such that ${\mathbb P}( {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \in K ) \ge 1 - {\varepsilon}$ for any $n$
nodes.label: defn:tight

nodes.name: Properties of tightness
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\{ {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=0}^\infty$ is a tight sequence of random functions in $C([0, \infty); {\mathbb R}^{d})$ and ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ is another random function in $C([0, \infty); {\mathbb R}^{d})$. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item If the finite-dimensional distributions of $ {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) $ converge weakly to the finite-dimensional distributions of ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$, i.e., for each positive integer $k$ and positive numbers $t_1, t_2, \dots, t_k > 0$, it holds that $({\textnormal{U}}_{n}(t_1), {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(t_2), \dots, {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(t_k)) \Rightarrow ({\textnormal{U}}(t_1), {\textnormal{U}}(t_2), \dots, {\textnormal{U}}(t_k))$, then ${\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \Rightarrow {\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ {\citep[Theorem~3]{whitt1970weak}}. \item Prokhorov's theorem {\citep[Theorem~5.1]{billingsley2013convergence}}: Each subsequence of $\{ {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=0}^\infty$ contains a further subsequence that converges weakly to some random function in $C([0, \infty); {\mathbb R}^{d})$. \item If each convergent subsequence of $\{ {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=0}^\infty$ converges weakly to ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$, then ${\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \Rightarrow {\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ \citep[Corollary on page~59]{billingsley2013convergence}. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: For tight random functions: fdd convergence implies weak convergence; Prokhorov subsequence extraction; common subsequential limit implies convergence.
assumptions: $\{ {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=0}^\infty$ is a tight sequence of random functions in $C([0, \infty); {\mathbb R}^{d})$
conclusions: ${\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \Rightarrow {\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$
Each subsequence of $\{ {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=0}^\infty$ contains a further subsequence that converges weakly to some random function in $C([0, \infty); {\mathbb R}^{d})$
nodes.label: prop:tight

nodes.name: The martingale problem
nodes.statement: Suppose ${\mathcal A}\colon \mathrm{dom}(A) \subseteq C_b({\mathbb R}^d) \rightarrow C_b({\mathbb R}^d) $ is a linear operator, $L \subseteq \mathrm{dom} ({\mathcal A})$ is the set of test functions, and ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ is a $({\mathcal F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$-adapted stochastic process. We say ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ solves the \textit{martingale problem} for $({\mathcal A}, L)$, if for any $f \in L$, the following process \begin{equation} f({\textnormal{U}}(t)) - f({\textnormal{U}}(0)) - \int_0^t {\mathcal A} f({\textnormal{U}}(s)) ds \end{equation} is a martingale w.r.t.\ to filtration $({\mathcal F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$.
nodes.statement_short: $U$ solves the martingale problem for $(\mathcal A, L)$ if $f(U(t))-f(U(0))-\int_0^t \mathcal A f(U(s))ds$ is a martingale for all $f\in L$.
nodes.label: def:mart_prob

nodes.name: Martingale problem process (4)
nodes.statement: f({\textnormal{U}}(t)) - f({\textnormal{U}}(0)) - \int_0^t {\mathcal A} f({\textnormal{U}}(s)) ds
nodes.label: eq:mart-prob

nodes.name: Multi-dimensional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
nodes.statement: In our context, the limiting process is a multi-dimensional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, defined as the () solution to the following stochastic differential equation (SDE) \footnote{In this paper we focus solely on the distribution of ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$, without specifying the probability space in which ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ resides. Consequently, when we refer to the solution of \eqref{eq:sde-general}, we mean the \textit{weak solution}, without explicitly detailing the probability space of the stochastic process.} \begin{equation} d {\textnormal{U}}(t) = - B {\textnormal{U}}(t) dt + \Sigma^{1/2} d {\textnormal{W}}^d(t), \end{equation} where $B, \Sigma \in {\mathbb R}^{d \times d}$ and $\Sigma$ is positive definite.
nodes.genus: solution to the following stochastic differential equation (SDE)

nodes.name: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck SDE (5)
nodes.statement: d {\textnormal{U}}(t) = - B {\textnormal{U}}(t) dt + \Sigma^{1/2} d {\textnormal{W}}^d(t),
nodes.label: eq:sde-general

nodes.name: Existence, uniqueness and Markov property of OU solution
nodes.statement: Given an initial distribution for ${\textnormal{U}}(0)$, the solution to~\eqref{eq:sde-general} exists uniquely. Furthermore, this solution is a time-homogeneous Markov process~\citep[Chapter 5, Section 3]{ethier2009markov}.
conclusions: the solution to~\eqref{eq:sde-general} exists uniquely
this solution is a time-homogeneous Markov process

nodes.name: Infinitesimal generator of the OU process
nodes.statement: To characterize this process, we let the operator ${\mathcal A}$ in Definition~\ref{def:mart_prob} be its \textit{infinitesimal generator}, namely \begin{equation} {\mathcal A} f(x) = - \inner{Bx}{\nabla f(x)} + \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{tr} ( \nabla^2 f(x) \Sigma ), \ \forall f \in C^2_c({\mathbb R}^d). \end{equation}

nodes.name: OU generator (6)
nodes.statement: {\mathcal A} f(x) = - \inner{Bx}{\nabla f(x)} + \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{tr} ( \nabla^2 f(x) \Sigma ), \ \forall f \in C^2_c({\mathbb R}^d).
nodes.label: eq:generator-general

nodes.name: Equivalence of SDE solutions and martingale problem solutions
nodes.statement: Suppose that the initial distribution ${\textnormal{U}}(0)$ is given and the generator ${\mathcal A}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:generator-general}. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item If ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ is a solution to the SDE in \eqref{eq:sde-general}, then ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ solves the martingale problem for $({\mathcal A}, C_c^2({\mathbb R}^d))$. \item If ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ solves the martingale problem for $({\mathcal A}, C_c^2({\mathbb R}^d))$, then ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ is a solution to the SDE in~\eqref{eq:sde-general}. \end{enumerate}
nodes.origin_citation: Ethier & Kurtz 2009, Ch. 5, Prop. 3.1 and Thm. 3.3
assumptions: the generator ${\mathcal A}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:generator-general}
${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ is a solution to the SDE in \eqref{eq:sde-general}
${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ solves the martingale problem for $({\mathcal A}, C_c^2({\mathbb R}^d))$
conclusions: ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ solves the martingale problem for $({\mathcal A}, C_c^2({\mathbb R}^d))$
${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ is a solution to the SDE in~\eqref{eq:sde-general}

assumptions: ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ is a solution to the SDE in \eqref{eq:sde-general}
conclusions: ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ solves the martingale problem for $({\mathcal A}, C_c^2({\mathbb R}^d))$

assumptions: ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ solves the martingale problem for $({\mathcal A}, C_c^2({\mathbb R}^d))$
conclusions: ${\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$ is a solution to the SDE in~\eqref{eq:sde-general}

nodes.name: Well-posedness of the OU martingale problem
nodes.statement: By this equivalence, the existence and uniqueness of the solution to \eqref{eq:sde-general} imply that the martingale problem for $({\mathcal A}, C_c^2({\mathbb R}^d))$ also has a unique solution, given the initial distribution of ${\textnormal{U}}(0)$.
conclusions: the martingale problem for $({\mathcal A}, C_c^2({\mathbb R}^d))$ also has a unique solution, given the initial distribution of ${\textnormal{U}}(0)$

nodes.name: Lipschitz conditions
nodes.statement:
There exists an operator $H\colon {\mathbb R}^{d_y}ightarrow{\mathbb R}^{d_x}$ such that for any fixed $y\in{\mathbb R}^{d_y}$, $x = H(y)$ is the unique solution of $F(x,y) = 0$. The operators $H$, $F$ and $G$ satisfy the following Lipschitz conditions: $ orall\, x \in {\mathbb R}^{d_x}, y_{1}, y_{2} \in{\mathbb R}^{d_y}$,  egin{align} \|H(y_{1}) - H(y_{2})\| & \leq L_{H}\|y_{1}-y_{2}\|,\ \|F(x,y_1) - F(H(y_1),y_1)\| & \leq L_{F} \|x - H(y_1) \|, 
onumber \ \|G(x,y_{1}) - G(H(y_{1}),y_{1})\| & \leq {L}_{G,x} \|x - H(y_{1})\|, 
onumber \ \| G(H(y_{1}),y_{1}) - G(H(y^\star), y^\star) \| & \leq {L}_{G,y} \| y - y^\star \|. 
onumber \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $x=H(y)$ uniquely solves $F(x,y)=0$; $H$, $F$, $G$ satisfy Lipschitz conditions with constants $L_H, L_F, L_{G,x}, L_{G,y}$.
nodes.label: assump:smooth

nodes.name: Uniform local linearity of H up to order 1+delta_H
nodes.statement: Assume that $H$ is differentiable and there exist constants $S_H \ge 0$ and ${\delta_H} \in [0.5, 1]$ such that $\forall\, y_1, y_2 \in {\mathbb R}^{d_y}$, \begin{equation*} \| H(y_1) - H(y_2) - \nabla H(y_2) (y_1-y_2) \| \le S_H \|y_1-y_2\|^{1+{\delta_H}}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: assump:smoothH

nodes.name: Nested local linearity of F and G
nodes.statement: There exist matrices $B_1, B_2, B_3$ with compatible dimensions, constants ${S}_{B,F}, {S}_{B,G} \ge 0$ and ${\delta_F}, {\delta_G} \in (0,1]$ such that \begin{align} \|F(x, y) - B_1(x {-} H(y))\| &\le {S}_{B,F} \left( \|x {-} H(y)\|^{1+{\delta_F}} + \|y {-} y^{\star}\|^{1+{\delta_F}} \right), \\ \|G(x, y) - B_2(x {-} H(y))- B_3(y {-} y^{\star}) )\| &\le {S}_{B,G} \left( \|x {-} H(y)\|^{1+{\delta_G}} + \|y {-} y^{\star}\|^{1+{\delta_G}} \right). \end{align} Furthermore, $\|B_1\| \le L_F$, $\| B_2\| \le {L}_{G,x}$, and $\|B_3\|\le {L}_{G,y}$.
nodes.statement_short: $F$ and $G$ are linear in $(x-H(y), y-y^\star)$ via matrices $B_1,B_2,B_3$ up to higher-order residuals of orders $1+\delta_F$, $1+\delta_G$.
nodes.label: assump:near-linear

nodes.name: Form of the linearization matrices
nodes.statement:
If $F$ and $G$ are differentiable at $(x^\star, y^\star)$, then we have  egin{align*} B_1 & = 
abla_x F(x^{\star}, y^{\star}), \quad B_2 = 
abla_x G(x^{\star}, y^{\star}), \ B_3 & = 
abla_y G(x^{\star}, y^{\star}) - 
abla_x G(x^{\star}, y^{\star}) [
abla_x F(x^{\star}, y^{\star})]^{-1} 
abla_y F(x^{\star}, y^{\star}). \end{align*}
nodes.label: remar:fclt:B-form

nodes.name: Conditions on step sizes
nodes.statement: The step sizes $\{ \alpha_{n} \}_{n=0}^\infty$ and $\{ \beta_{n} \}_{n=0}^\infty$ together with their ratios $\{ \kappa_{n} = \beta_{n} / \alpha_{n} \}_{n=0}^\infty$ satisfy the following conditions. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item As $n \to \infty$, $\alpha_{n}, \beta_{n}, \kappa_{n} \rightarrow 0$ and $\alpha_{n}$, $\beta_{n}$ are decreasing in $n$. \item $\frac{\beta_{n-1}}{\beta_{n}} = 1 + {\mathcal O}(\beta_{n})$ and $\tilde{\beta} := \lim_{n \to \infty} (\beta_{n+1}^{-1} - \beta_{n}^{-1} ) \ge 0 $. \item $\frac{\alpha_{n-1}}{\alpha_{n}} = 1 + {\mathcal O}(\beta_{n})$ and $\frac{\kappa_{n-1}}{\kappa_{n}} = 1 + {\mathcal O}\big(\beta_{n}\big)$. \item $n \alpha_{n}$ and $n \beta_{n}$ are increasing in $n$. \item $\beta_{n}^{(1+{\delta_H}) / 2 } = {\mathcal O}(\alpha_{n})$ and $ \alpha_{n}^{1+{\delta_G}}, \alpha_{n}^{1+{\delta_F}} = o(\beta_{n}) $, with ${\delta_H}$, ${\delta_F}$ and ${\delta_G}$ defined in Assumptions~\ref{assump:smoothH} and \ref{assump:near-linear}. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Step sizes and their ratio decrease to 0 regularly, $\tilde\beta=\lim(\beta_{n+1}^{-1}-\beta_n^{-1})$ exists, and the time-scale separation is within a range set by $\delta_H,\delta_F,\delta_G$.
nodes.label: assump:stepsize-twotime

nodes.name: Polynomially diminishing step sizes
nodes.statement: For $\alpha_{n} = \alpha_{0} (n+1)^{-a}$ and $\beta_{n} = \beta_{0} (n+1)^{-b}$ with $a, b \in (0, 1]$, we have $\tilde{\beta} = \beta_{0}^{-1}$ if $b = 1$ and $\tilde{\beta} = 0$ otherwise. Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime} requires $1 < \frac{b}{a} < 1 + \min\{ {\delta_F}, {\delta_G} \} $ and $\frac{b}{a} \ge \frac{2}{1+{\delta_H}} $. If ${\delta_H}=1$, $\frac{b}{a} \ge \frac{2}{1+{\delta_H}} $ naturally holds.
nodes.label: exmp:fclt-stepsize

nodes.name: Hurwitz matrices
nodes.statement: The matrices $B_1$ and $B_3$ defined in Assumption~\ref{assump:near-linear} and the parameter $\tilde{\beta}$ defined in Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime} satisfy that both $- B_1 $ and $- \left( B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta}}{2} {I} \right)$ are Hurwitz matrices, i.e, the real parts of their eigenvalues are negative.
nodes.label: assump:hurwitz

nodes.name: Hurwitz condition via symmetric parts
nodes.statement: Assumption~\ref{assump:hurwitz} is equivalent to requiring that both $\frac{B_1 + B_1^\top}{2}$ and $\frac{ B_3 + B_3^\top - \tilde{\beta} {I} }{2}$ are positive definite.
conclusions: Assumption~\ref{assump:hurwitz} is equivalent to requiring that both $\frac{B_1 + B_1^\top}{2}$ and $\frac{ B_3 + B_3^\top - \tilde{\beta} {I} }{2}$ are positive definite

nodes.name: Natural filtration of the iterates
nodes.statement: Define the filtration $( {\mathcal F}_{n} )_{n \ge 1}$ as \begin{equation*} {\mathcal F}_{n} = \sigma ( x_{0},y_{0},\xi_{0},\psi_{0},\xi_{1},\psi_{1},\ldots,\xi_{n-1},\psi_{n-1} ). \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Conditions on the noise
nodes.statement: The noise sequences $\{ \xi_{n} \}_{n=0}^\infty$ and $\{ \psi_{n} \}_{n=0}^\infty$ are martingale difference sequences satisfying ${\mathbb E}[ \xi_{n} \,|\, {\mathcal F}_{n}] = 0$ and ${\mathbb E} [ \psi_{n} \,|\, {\mathcal F}_{n}] = 0$. Their fourth moments are uniformly bounded, i.e., \begin{equation*} \sup_{n \ge 0} {\mathbb E} \| \xi_{n} \|^4 + \sup_{n \ge 0} {\mathbb E} \| \psi_{n} \|^{4} < \infty. \end{equation*} Moreover, as $n \to \infty$, \begin{equation*} {\mathbb E} \left[ \begin{pmatrix} \xi_{n} \xi_{n}^\top & \xi_{n} \psi_{n}^\top \\ \psi_{n} \xi_{n}^\top & \psi_{n} \psi_{n}^\top \end{pmatrix} \Bigg|\, {\mathcal F}_{n} \right] \overset{p}{\to} \begin{pmatrix} \Sigma_{\xi} & \Sigma_{\xi, \psi} \\ \Sigma_{\xi, \psi}^\top & \Sigma_{\psi} \end{pmatrix}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Martingale-difference noise with bounded fourth moments and conditional covariance converging in probability.
nodes.label: assump:noise-fclt

nodes.name: Error terms of two-time-scale SA
nodes.statement: Since two-time-scale SA can be viewed as an approximation of the procedure in \eqref{eq:two-loop-approx}, previous work studies the following error terms~\citep{kaledin2020finite, doan2022nonlinear, han2024finite} \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} {\hat{x}}_{n} = x_{n} - H(y_{n}), \quad {\hat{y}}_{n} = y_{n} - y^{\star}. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.origin_citation: Kaledin et al. 2020; Doan 2022; Han et al. 2024

nodes.name: Error terms (10)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} {\hat{x}}_{n} = x_{n} - H(y_{n}), \quad {\hat{y}}_{n} = y_{n} - y^{\star}. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: alg:xyhat

nodes.name: Error bound for the fast iterate
nodes.statement: Under Assumption~\ref{assump:smooth}, $\| x_{n} - x^\star \| = \| {\hat{x}}_{n} + H(y_{n}) - H(y^\star) \| \le \| {\hat{x}}_{n} \| + L_H \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \|$.

nodes.name: Non-asymptotic convergence rates (informal)
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions~\ref{assump:smooth} -- \ref{assump:noise-fclt} and some additional regular conditions, we have ${\mathbb E} \| {\hat{x}}_{n} \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\alpha_{n}) $, ${\mathbb E} \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\beta_{n})$ and ${\mathbb E} \| {\hat{x}}_{n} \|^4 + {\mathbb E} \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \|^4 = {\mathcal O} (\alpha_{n}^2)$.
assumptions: Assumptions~\ref{assump:smooth} -- \ref{assump:noise-fclt} and some additional regular conditions
conclusions: ${\mathbb E} \| {\hat{x}}_{n} \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\alpha_{n}) $, ${\mathbb E} \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\beta_{n})$ and ${\mathbb E} \| {\hat{x}}_{n} \|^4 + {\mathbb E} \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \|^4 = {\mathcal O} (\alpha_{n}^2)$
nodes.label: prop:mart-decouple-rate

nodes.name: Non-asymptotic decoupled convergence
nodes.statement: The convergence rates in Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-decouple-rate} hold.
nodes.label: assump:mart-decouple-rate

nodes.name: Rescaled iterates
nodes.statement: For $n \ge 1$, we define \begin{equation} {\check{x}}_{n} := \frac{{\hat{x}}_{n}}{ \sqrt{ \alpha_{n-1}} } = \frac{ {x}_n - H({y}_n) }{ \sqrt{\alpha_{n-1}} }, \quad {\check{y}}_{n} := \frac{ {\hat{y}}_{n} }{ \sqrt{\beta_{n-1}} } = \frac{ {y}_{n} - {y}^\star }{ \sqrt{ \beta_{n-1} } }. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Rescaled iterates (11)
nodes.statement: {\check{x}}_{n} := \frac{{\hat{x}}_{n}}{ \sqrt{ \alpha_{n-1}} } = \frac{ {x}_n - H({y}_n) }{ \sqrt{\alpha_{n-1}} }, \quad {\check{y}}_{n} := \frac{ {\hat{y}}_{n} }{ \sqrt{\beta_{n-1}} } = \frac{ {y}_{n} - {y}^\star }{ \sqrt{ \beta_{n-1} } }.
nodes.label: eq:xycheck-def

nodes.name: Rescaled iterates are stochastically bounded
nodes.statement: Assumption~\ref{assump:mart-decouple-rate} implies $ {\mathbb E} \| {\check{x}}_{n} \|^2 + {\mathbb E} \| {\check{y}}_{n} \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(1) $, indicating that ${\check{x}}_{n}, {\check{y}}_{n} = {\mathcal O}_p(1)$.
conclusions: ${\mathbb E} \| {\check{x}}_{n} \|^2 + {\mathbb E} \| {\check{y}}_{n} \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(1)$
${\check{x}}_{n}, {\check{y}}_{n} = {\mathcal O}_p(1)$

nodes.name: Continuous-time interpolated trajectories
nodes.statement: Now we construct the continuous trajectories $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=1}^\infty$ and $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=1}^\infty$ by linearly interpolating between the terms of the rescaled sequence $\{ {\check{x}}_{n} \}_{n=1}^\infty$ and $\{ {\check{y}}_{n} \}_{n=1}^\infty$: \begin{align} {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t) & = \begin{cases} {\check{x}}_{n}, & t = 0; \\ {\check{x}}_{m} + \frac{t - \sum_{i=n}^{m-1} \alpha_{i} }{\alpha_{m}} ({\check{x}}_{m+1} - {\check{x}}_{m}), & t \in \left( \sum_{i=n}^{m-1} \alpha_{i}, \sum_{i=n}^{m} \alpha_{i} \right] \text{ for } m \ge n; \end{cases} \\ {\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(t) & = \begin{cases} {\check{y}}_{n}, & t = 0; \\ {\check{y}}_{m} + \frac{t - \sum_{i=n}^{m-1} \beta_{i} }{\beta_{m}} ({\check{y}}_{m+1} - {\check{y}}_{m}), & t \in \left( \sum_{i=n}^{m-1} \beta_{i}, \sum_{i=n}^{m} \beta_{i} \right] \text{ for } m \ge n. \end{cases} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $\bar X_n$, $\bar Y_n$ linearly interpolate the rescaled iterates on time grids with spacings $\alpha_m$ and $\beta_m$.

nodes.name: Interpolated fast trajectory (12)
nodes.statement: {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t) & = \begin{cases} {\check{x}}_{n}, & t = 0; \\ {\check{x}}_{m} + \frac{t - \sum_{i=n}^{m-1} \alpha_{i} }{\alpha_{m}} ({\check{x}}_{m+1} - {\check{x}}_{m}), & t \in \left( \sum_{i=n}^{m-1} \alpha_{i}, \sum_{i=n}^{m} \alpha_{i} \right] \text{ for } m \ge n; \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq:xbar-short

nodes.name: Interpolated slow trajectory (13)
nodes.statement: {\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(t) & = \begin{cases} {\check{y}}_{n}, & t = 0; \\ {\check{y}}_{m} + \frac{t - \sum_{i=n}^{m-1} \beta_{i} }{\beta_{m}} ({\check{y}}_{m+1} - {\check{y}}_{m}), & t \in \left( \sum_{i=n}^{m-1} \beta_{i}, \sum_{i=n}^{m} \beta_{i} \right] \text{ for } m \ge n. \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq:ybar-short

nodes.name: Decoupled functional central limit theorems
nodes.statement: Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{assump:smooth} -- \ref{assump:noise-fclt} and \ref{assump:mart-decouple-rate} hold. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item The stochastic process ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ defined in \eqref{eq:xbar-short} converges weakly to the stationary solution of the following SDE \begin{equation} d {\textnormal{X}}(t) = - B_1 {\textnormal{X}}(t) dt + \Sigma_{\xi}^{1/2} d {\textnormal{W}}^{d_x}(t). \end{equation} The rescaled iterate $ {\check{x}}_{n} $ defined in \eqref{eq:xycheck-def} converges weakly to the invariant distribution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde}, i.e., ${\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_x)$, where $\Sigma_x$ satisfies the following Lyapunov equation \begin{equation} B_1 \Sigma_x + \Sigma_x B_1 = \Sigma_{\xi}. \end{equation} \item The stochastic process ${\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ defined in \eqref{eq:ybar-short} converges weakly to the stationary solution of the following SDE \begin{equation} d {\textnormal{Y}}(t) = - \left(B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \right) {\textnormal{Y}}(t) dt + \widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}^{1/2} d {\textnormal{W}}^{d_y}(t), \end{equation} where the matrix $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}$ is defined as \begin{equation} \widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi} := \Sigma_{\psi} - B_2 B_1^{-1} \Sigma_{\xi,\psi} - \Sigma_{\xi, \psi}^\top B_1^{-\top} B_2^\top + B_2 B_1^{-1} \Sigma_{\xi} B_1^{-\top} B_2^\top. \end{equation} The rescaled iterate $ {\check{y}}_{n}$ defined in \eqref{eq:xycheck-def} converges weakly to the invariant distribution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}, i.e., ${\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_y)$, where $\Sigma_y$ satisfies the following Lyapunov equation \begin{equation} \left(B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \right) \Sigma_y + \Sigma_y \left( B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \right) = \widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}. \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Under the assumptions, $\bar X_n$ and $\bar Y_n$ converge weakly to stationary OU processes with drifts $-B_1$ and $-(B_3-\tilde\beta I/2)$; rescaled iterates are asymptotically Gaussian.
conclusions: The stochastic process ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ defined in \eqref{eq:xbar-short} converges weakly to the stationary solution of the following SDE
The rescaled iterate $ {\check{x}}_{n} $ defined in \eqref{eq:xycheck-def} converges weakly to the invariant distribution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde}, i.e., ${\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_x)$
The stochastic process ${\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ defined in \eqref{eq:ybar-short} converges weakly to the stationary solution of the following SDE
The rescaled iterate $ {\check{y}}_{n}$ defined in \eqref{eq:xycheck-def} converges weakly to the invariant distribution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}, i.e., ${\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_y)$
nodes.label: thm:fclt-twotime

nodes.name: Decoupled FCLT for the fast iterate (Theorem 4.1 (i))
nodes.statement: The stochastic process ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ defined in \eqref{eq:xbar-short} converges weakly to the stationary solution of the following SDE \begin{equation} d {\textnormal{X}}(t) = - B_1 {\textnormal{X}}(t) dt + \Sigma_{\xi}^{1/2} d {\textnormal{W}}^{d_x}(t). \end{equation} The rescaled iterate $ {\check{x}}_{n} $ defined in \eqref{eq:xycheck-def} converges weakly to the invariant distribution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde}, i.e., ${\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_x)$, where $\Sigma_x$ satisfies the following Lyapunov equation \begin{equation} B_1 \Sigma_x + \Sigma_x B_1 = \Sigma_{\xi}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\bar X_n$ converges weakly to the stationary OU process $dX=-B_1Xdt+\Sigma_\xi^{1/2}dW$; $\check x_n \Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma_x)$ with Lyapunov covariance.
conclusions: The stochastic process ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ defined in \eqref{eq:xbar-short} converges weakly to the stationary solution of the following SDE
The rescaled iterate $ {\check{x}}_{n} $ defined in \eqref{eq:xycheck-def} converges weakly to the invariant distribution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde}, i.e., ${\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_x)$

nodes.name: Limiting SDE for the fast iterate (14)
nodes.statement: d {\textnormal{X}}(t) = - B_1 {\textnormal{X}}(t) dt + \Sigma_{\xi}^{1/2} d {\textnormal{W}}^{d_x}(t).
nodes.label: eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde

nodes.name: Lyapunov equation for fast covariance (15)
nodes.statement: B_1 \Sigma_x + \Sigma_x B_1 = \Sigma_{\xi}.
nodes.label: eq:fclt-twotime:x-var

nodes.name: Decoupled FCLT for the slow iterate (Theorem 4.1 (ii))
nodes.statement: The stochastic process ${\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ defined in \eqref{eq:ybar-short} converges weakly to the stationary solution of the following SDE \begin{equation} d {\textnormal{Y}}(t) = - \left(B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \right) {\textnormal{Y}}(t) dt + \widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}^{1/2} d {\textnormal{W}}^{d_y}(t), \end{equation} where the matrix $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}$ is defined as \begin{equation} \widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi} := \Sigma_{\psi} - B_2 B_1^{-1} \Sigma_{\xi,\psi} - \Sigma_{\xi, \psi}^\top B_1^{-\top} B_2^\top + B_2 B_1^{-1} \Sigma_{\xi} B_1^{-\top} B_2^\top. \end{equation} The rescaled iterate $ {\check{y}}_{n}$ defined in \eqref{eq:xycheck-def} converges weakly to the invariant distribution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}, i.e., ${\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_y)$, where $\Sigma_y$ satisfies the following Lyapunov equation \begin{equation} \left(B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \right) \Sigma_y + \Sigma_y \left( B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \right) = \widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\bar Y_n$ converges weakly to the stationary OU process with drift $-(B_3-\tilde\beta I/2)$ and diffusion $\widetilde\Sigma_\psi$; $\check y_n \Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma_y)$.
conclusions: The stochastic process ${\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ defined in \eqref{eq:ybar-short} converges weakly to the stationary solution of the following SDE
The rescaled iterate $ {\check{y}}_{n}$ defined in \eqref{eq:xycheck-def} converges weakly to the invariant distribution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}, i.e., ${\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_y)$

nodes.name: Limiting SDE for the slow iterate (16)
nodes.statement: d {\textnormal{Y}}(t) = - \left(B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \right) {\textnormal{Y}}(t) dt + \widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}^{1/2} d {\textnormal{W}}^{d_y}(t),
nodes.label: eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde

nodes.name: Effective slow-scale noise covariance (17)
nodes.statement: \widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi} := \Sigma_{\psi} - B_2 B_1^{-1} \Sigma_{\xi,\psi} - \Sigma_{\xi, \psi}^\top B_1^{-\top} B_2^\top + B_2 B_1^{-1} \Sigma_{\xi} B_1^{-\top} B_2^\top.
nodes.label: eq:cov-z

nodes.name: Lyapunov equation for slow covariance (18)
nodes.statement: \left(B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \right) \Sigma_y + \Sigma_y \left( B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \right) = \widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:fclt-twotime:y-var

nodes.name: Explanation of the decoupled FCLT
nodes.statement: For Theorem~\ref{thm:fclt-twotime}, we have the following explanations. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item \textbf{Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process}: The drift terms in the SDEs \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} and \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde} are linear, and the noise terms are constant. As a result, the solution to these SDEs is a multi-dimensional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. Assumption~\ref{assump:hurwitz} ensures the uniqueness of the invariant distribution for these processes, with covariance matrices given in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-var} and \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-var}~\citep[Section~6.5]{risken1996fokker}. \item \textbf{Stationary solution}: A ``stationary solution'' refers to a solution that is a stationary process. Specifically, this corresponds to a solution where the initial distribution matches the invariant distribution. \item \textbf{Interdependence}: The parameters $B_1$ and $\Sigma_{\xi}$ in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} are associated solely with the fast-time-scale updates, indicating that the asymptotic behavior of the fast iterate resembles standard SA and is nearly unaffected by the slow iterate. In contrast, both $B_3$ and $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}$ in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde} are influenced by the slow-time-scale update. Specifically, $B_3$ (as detailed in Remark~\ref{remar:fclt:B-form}) involves the gradient of $F$, and $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}$ represents the asymptotic covariance of $\psi_{n} - B_2 B_1^{-1} \xi_{n}$. Decoupling ensures that the convergence rates of different iterates depend only on their respective step sizes. However, the fast-time-scale update still influences the slow-time-scale update through the constant terms, such as the coefficients in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}. \item \textbf{Effect of step sizes}: The presence of $\tilde{\beta}$ in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde} highlights the impact of step sizes on asymptotic behavior. As illustrated in Example~\ref{exmp:fclt-stepsize}, for $\beta_{n} = \Theta(n^{-b})$ with $b \in (0,1]$, $\tilde{\beta} = \beta_{0}^{-1} \neq 0$ only when $b=1$, which requires the initial step size to be sufficiently large. This aligns with the convergence analysis for standard SA~\citep{moulines2011non}. Due to the assumption $\beta_{n} / \alpha_{n} = o(1)$, the choice of step sizes does not influence the asymptotic behavior in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} (see Remark~\ref{rema:step-size}). \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Limits are OU processes; stationary solution meaning; fast scale affects slow limit via constants; $\tilde\beta$ reflects step-size effect.
nodes.label: rema:fclt

nodes.name: Comparison with previous work
nodes.statement: Compared to the FCLT presented in~\cite{faizal2023functional}, which rescales the error terms ${\hat{x}}_{n}$ and ${\hat{y}}_{n}$ using the square root of the fast-time-scale step size, we apply distinct rescalings to ${\hat{x}}_{n}$ and ${\hat{y}}_{n}$ based on the square root of their respective step sizes. This refinement enables us to derive decoupled FCLTs under local linearity conditions, offering a more precise characterization of the asymptotic behavior in two-time-scale SA. Furthermore, our FCLTs can recover the classical CLTs from \cite{konda2004convergence, mokkadem2006convergence}, as demonstrated in Corollary~\ref{cor:clt}.

nodes.name: Central limit theorems
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:fclt-twotime}, we have $\alpha_{n}^{-1/2} ({x}_{n} - H({y}_{n})) \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_x)$, $ \beta_{n}^{-1/2} ({y}_{n} - {y}^\star) \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0,\Sigma_{y})$ and $ \alpha_{n}^{-1/2} ({x}_{n} - {x}^\star) \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_{x})$.
conclusions: $\alpha_{n}^{-1/2} ({x}_{n} - H({y}_{n})) \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_x)$
$ \beta_{n}^{-1/2} ({y}_{n} - {y}^\star) \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0,\Sigma_{y})$
$ \alpha_{n}^{-1/2} ({x}_{n} - {x}^\star) \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_{x})$
nodes.label: cor:clt

nodes.name: Strongly convex minimization with noisy gradients
nodes.statement: In the following two examples, we consider the problem of minimizing a strongly convex function $f$ with a unique minimizer $x_o^\star = \arg\min_{x} f(x)$, using noisy gradient observations.

abla^2 f(x_o^\star) ]^{-1} \Sigma_{\xi} [ 
abla^2 f(x_o^\star) ]^{-1} $. Thus, the solution to \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-var} is $\Sigma_{y} = \widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}$. We recover the CLT for the averaged iterate from \cite{polyak1992acceleration} and the FCLT for the original iterate from \cite[Section~II.4.5.3]{benveniste2012adaptive} and \cite[Section~8.4]{borkar2009stochastic}. Additionally, our results offer a trajectory-level characterization for the averaged iterate.
nodes.label: exmp:PRave

nodes.name: SGD with Polyak-Ruppert averaging
nodes.statement: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD), introduced by \citep{robbins1951stochastic}, iteratively updates the iterate $x_t$ by~\eqref{eq:SGD}. To improve the convergence of SGD, an additional averaging step~\eqref{eq:SGD-averaging} is often used~\citep{polyak1992acceleration,ruppert1988efficient} \begin{subequations} \begin{align} x_{n+1} &= x_{n} - \alpha_n(\nabla f(x_{n}) + \xi_{n})~\text{with}~\alpha_n = \frac{\alpha_0}{ (n+1)^a }~(0 < a < 1) , \\ y_{n+1} &= \frac{1}{n+1}\sum_{\tau=0}^n x_{\tau} = y_n - \beta_n(y_n-x_n)~\text{with}~\beta_n = \frac{1}{n+1}. \end{align} \end{subequations}
nodes.statement_short: SGD step on $x_n$ with step $\alpha_n\propto n^{-a}$ plus running average $y_n$ with step $1/(n+1)$.

nodes.name: SGD update (19a)
nodes.statement: x_{n+1} &= x_{n} - \alpha_n(\nabla f(x_{n}) + \xi_{n})~\text{with}~\alpha_n = \frac{\alpha_0}{ (n+1)^a }~(0 < a < 1) ,
nodes.label: eq:SGD

nodes.name: Polyak-Ruppert averaging step (19b)
nodes.statement: y_{n+1} &= \frac{1}{n+1}\sum_{\tau=0}^n x_{\tau} = y_n - \beta_n(y_n-x_n)~\text{with}~\beta_n = \frac{1}{n+1}.
nodes.label: eq:SGD-averaging

nodes.name: SGD with momentum
nodes.statement:
Stochastic heavy ball (SHB) is a variant of SGD based on momentum and adaptive step sizes and has been shown to be effective~\citep{gadat2018stochastic}. A ``normalized'' version of SHB~\citep{gupal1972stochastic,gitman2019understanding} iteratively runs  egin{equation}  egin{aligned} x_{n+1} &= x_{n} - \alpha_n (x_n - 
abla f(y_n) - \xi_n),\ y_{n+1} &= y_{n} -  eta_n x_{n}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} This update is a special case of \eqref{alg:xy} with $F(x, y) = x-
abla f(y), G(x, y) = x$, $H(y) = 
abla f(y)$, $y^{\star} = x_o^{\star}$ and $x^{\star} = 0$. Contextualizing this example in Theorem~ef{thm:fclt-twotime}, one can check $B_1 = {I}$, $B_3 -  rac{	ilde{ eta}}{2} {I} = 
abla^2 f(x^\star) -  rac{	ilde{ eta}}{2} {I}$ and $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi} = \Sigma_{\xi}$, implying that the asymptotic behavior is similar to that of standard SA. Consequently, for a strongly convex objective, the addition of momentum does not provide an asymptotic advantage over SGD. Furthermore, our result is not directly comparable to the FCLT in \cite{gadat2018stochastic}, as we consider distinct time scales, whereas their analysis focuses on a single-time-scale setting.
nodes.label: exmp:momentum

nodes.name: Normalized stochastic heavy ball
nodes.statement: A ``normalized'' version of SHB~\citep{gupal1972stochastic,gitman2019understanding} iteratively runs \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} x_{n+1} &= x_{n} - \alpha_n (x_n - \nabla f(y_n) - \xi_n),\\ y_{n+1} &= y_{n} - \beta_n x_{n}. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Momentum-SGD written as two-time-scale SA: $x_n$ tracks the gradient, $y_n$ moves along $-x_n$.

nodes.name: Normalized SHB updates (20)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} x_{n+1} &= x_{n} - \alpha_n (x_n - \nabla f(y_n) - \xi_n),\\ y_{n+1} &= y_{n} - \beta_n x_{n}. \end{aligned}

nodes.name: Gradient-based temporal-difference learning
nodes.statement: Gradient-based temporal-difference (TD) algorithms are widely used in off-policy reinforcement learning (RL), such as policy evaluation with function approximation~\citep{sutton2008convergent, sutton2009fast, maei2009convergent}. We consider two specific algorithms: GTD2 and TDC with linear function approximation~\citep{sutton2009fast}. These algorithms serve as typical examples of two-time-scale SA~\citep{dalal2018finite}. For clarity, we concentrate on the specific update rules while omitting the details of the RL setup. A more comprehensive explanation is provided in Appendix~\ref{append:exmp}. In this problem, the goal is to estimate the value function $V(s)$ for a given policy using a linear parameterization $V(s; y) = \phi(s)^\top y$, where $\phi(s)$ represents the feature vector of state $s$, and $y$ denotes the parameter vector. Given i.i.d.\ samples $\{ (s_n, r_n, s'_n) \}_{n=0}^\infty$~\citep{sutton2008convergent}, where $s_n$ is the current state, $r_n$ is the reward and $s'_n$ is the next state, the optimal parameter $y$ can be estimated iteratively via the following update rules\footnote{ Compared to the original formulation in \cite{sutton2009fast}, we incorporate an importance weight $\rho_{n}$, the explicit form of which is provided in Appendix~\ref{append:exmp}.} \begin{align} x_{n+1} &= x_{n} - \alpha_{n} \big( \phi(s_{n})^{\top} x_{n} - \rho_{n} \delta_{n} \big) \phi(s_{n}), \\ y_{n+1} &= y_{n} - \beta_{n} \rho_{n} \big( \gamma \phi(s'_{n}) - \phi(s_{n}) \big) \phi(s_{n})^\top x_{n}, \ \qquad \mathrm{ (GTD2) } \\ y_{n+1} &= y_{n} - \beta_{n} \rho_{n} \big( \gamma \phi(s'_n) \phi(s_n)^\top x_{n} - \delta_{n} \phi(s_{n}) \big), \ \quad \, \mathrm{ (TDC) } \end{align} where $\gamma$ is the discount factor, $\rho_{n}$ is the importance weight, and $\delta_{n}$ is the temporal-difference error defined as $ \delta_{n} = r_{n} + ( \gamma \phi(s'_{n}) - \phi(s_n) )^\top y_{n} $. Here, the fast iterate $x_{n}$ is an auxiliary variable. Both GTD2 and TDC share the same fast time-scale update but differ in their slow time-scale updates. To contextualize these methods within the two-time-scale SA~\eqref{alg:xy}, we define $A_n = \rho_{n} \phi(s_n) ( \phi(s_n) - \gamma \phi(s'_n) )^\top $, $b_n = \rho_{n} r_{n} \phi(s_n) $, $C_n = \phi(s_{n}) \phi(s_n)^\top $, $D_n = \gamma \rho_{n} \phi(s_n) \phi(s'_n)^\top$, and their expectations $A= {\mathbb E}[A_n]$, $b = {\mathbb E}[b_n]$, $C={\mathbb E}[C_n]$, and $D={\mathbb E}[D_n]$. It can be checked that \eqref{eq:gtd-x} -- \eqref{eq:tdc-y} are an instance of \eqref{alg:xy} with \begin{equation*} F(x,y) = Cx +Ay-b,\ \ G_{\mathrm{GTD2}}(x,y) = -A^\top x,\ \ G_{\mathrm{TDC}} (x,y) = D^\top x + Ay - b. \end{equation*} It follows that $H(y) = -C^{-1}(Ay-b)$, implying $G_{\mathrm{GTD2}}(H(y), y) = A^\top C^{-1} (Ay- b)$ and $G_{\mathrm{TDC}}(H(y), y) = (C - D^\top) C^{-1} (Ay - b)$. Although these expressions appear different, it can be verified that $C - D^\top = A^\top$ \citep[Equation~(68)]{li2024high}, leading to $G_{\mathrm{GTD2}} (H(y), y) \equiv G_{\mathrm{TDC}}(H(y),y)$. Therefore, GTD2 and TDC have the same optimal solution, $y^\star = A^{-1} b$ and $x^\star = H(y^\star) = 0$. Furthermore, the drift terms for both the methods in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} and \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde} are identical: $B_1 = C$ and $B_3 = A^\top C^{-1} A$. For the noise terms, both the methods share the same noise for the fast time scale $\xi_{n} = C_n x_{n} + A_n y_n - b_n - F(x_n, y_n) $. On the slow time scale, however, the noise differs slightly. For GTD2, the noise is expressed as $\psi^{\mathrm{GTD2}}_{n} = - A_{n}^\top x_n - G_{\mathrm{GTD2}}(x_n, y_n) $, whereas for TDC, it is given by $\psi^{\mathrm{TDC}}_{n} = D_n^\top x_{n} + A_n y_n - b_n - G_{\mathrm{TDC}}(x_n, y_n)$. Despite these differences, both the methods ultimately result in the same diffusion term $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}$ in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}. Additional details can be found in Appendix~\ref{append:exmp}. In summary, while GTD2 and TDC differ in form and may display distinct numerical behaviors~\citep{dann2014policy}, they share identical asymptotic properties, aligning with the results of~\citep{hu2024central}. Compared to their work, our results provide a more detailed characterization of trajectory properties for i.i.d.\ samples.
nodes.statement_short: GTD2 and TDC as two-time-scale SA: same drift $B_1=C$, $B_3=A^\top C^{-1}A$ and the same diffusion term, hence identical asymptotics.
nodes.label: exmp:gtd

nodes.name: GTD2 and TDC with linear function approximation
nodes.statement: Given i.i.d.\ samples $\{ (s_n, r_n, s'_n) \}_{n=0}^\infty$~\citep{sutton2008convergent}, where $s_n$ is the current state, $r_n$ is the reward and $s'_n$ is the next state, the optimal parameter $y$ can be estimated iteratively via the following update rules\footnote{ Compared to the original formulation in \cite{sutton2009fast}, we incorporate an importance weight $\rho_{n}$, the explicit form of which is provided in Appendix~\ref{append:exmp}.} \begin{align} x_{n+1} &= x_{n} - \alpha_{n} \big( \phi(s_{n})^{\top} x_{n} - \rho_{n} \delta_{n} \big) \phi(s_{n}), \\ y_{n+1} &= y_{n} - \beta_{n} \rho_{n} \big( \gamma \phi(s'_{n}) - \phi(s_{n}) \big) \phi(s_{n})^\top x_{n}, \ \qquad \mathrm{ (GTD2) } \\ y_{n+1} &= y_{n} - \beta_{n} \rho_{n} \big( \gamma \phi(s'_n) \phi(s_n)^\top x_{n} - \delta_{n} \phi(s_{n}) \big), \ \quad \, \mathrm{ (TDC) } \end{align} where $\gamma$ is the discount factor, $\rho_{n}$ is the importance weight, and $\delta_{n}$ is the temporal-difference error defined as $ \delta_{n} = r_{n} + ( \gamma \phi(s'_{n}) - \phi(s_n) )^\top y_{n} $.

nodes.statement: y_{n+1} &= y_{n} - \beta_{n} \rho_{n} \big( \gamma \phi(s'_{n}) - \phi(s_{n}) \big) \phi(s_{n})^\top x_{n}, \ \qquad \mathrm{ (GTD2) }

nodes.name: One-step recursions for the rescaled iterates
nodes.statement: Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{assump:smooth} -- \ref{assump:stepsize-twotime} and \ref{assump:mart-decouple-rate} hold. Define $\tilde{\xi}_{n} := \xi_{n} - \kappa_{n} H^\star \psi_{n}$. The rescaled sequences $\{ {\check{x}}_{n} \}_{n=0}^\infty$ and $\{ {\check{y}}_{n} \}_{n=0}^\infty$ defined in \eqref{eq:xycheck-def} satisfy the following relationships \begin{align} {\check{x}}_{n+1} & = ({I} - \alpha_{n} B_1) {\check{x}}_{n} - \sqrt{\alpha_{n}} \tilde{\xi}_{n} + R_{n}^x, \\ {\check{y}}_{n+1} & = \left( {I} - \beta_{n} B_3 + \frac{ \tilde{\beta} \beta_{n} }{2} {I} \right) {\check{y}}_{n} - \sqrt{\beta_{n} \alpha_{n} } B_2 {\check{x}}_{n} - \sqrt{\beta_n} \psi_{n} + R_{n}^y. \end{align} For any $2 < p \le \frac{4}{1 + ( {\delta_H} \vee {\delta_F} \vee {\delta_G} )/2} $, the residual terms $R_{n}^x$ and $R_{n}^y$ have the following properties: (i) ${\mathbb E} \| {\mathbb E} [ R_{n}^x | {\mathcal F}_n ] \| = o(\sqrt{\beta_{n} \alpha_{n}}) $, ${\mathbb E} \| R_{n}^x \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\beta_{n} \alpha_{n})$ and ${\mathbb E} \| R_{n}^x \|^p = o(\alpha_{n})$; (ii) ${\mathbb E} \| R_{n}^y \|^2 = o(\beta_{n}^2)$ and ${\mathbb E} \| R_{n}^y \|^p = o(\beta_{n})$.

nodes.name: Sufficient conditions for tightness
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\{ {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=0}^\infty$ is a sequence of random functions in $C([0, \infty); {\mathbb R}^{d})$. Then $\{ {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=0}^\infty$ is tight if the following two conditions hold: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For each positive $\eta$, there exist a positive $a$ and an integer $n_0$ such that \begin{equation*} {\mathbb P} \left( \| {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(0) \| \ge a \right) \le \eta, \quad \forall\, n \ge n_0. \end{equation*} \item For each positive $T$, there exist positive numbers $\gamma_1, \gamma_2, c_1, c_2, K$ such that \begin{equation} {\mathbb P} \left( \| {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(s) {-} {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(t) \| \ge {\varepsilon} \right) \le K \left( \frac{|s{-}t |^{1 {+} \gamma_1} }{{\varepsilon}^{c_1} } + \frac{ | s{-}t |^{1 {+} \gamma_2}}{{\varepsilon}^{c_2}} \right), \ \forall\, s,t \in [0, T], \forall \, n, \forall\, {\varepsilon} > 0. \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
assumptions: $\{ {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=0}^\infty$ is a sequence of random functions in $C([0, \infty); {\mathbb R}^{d})$
conclusions: $\{ {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=0}^\infty$ is tight
nodes.label: prop:tight-suff-slow

nodes.name: Modulus-of-continuity condition (29)
nodes.statement: {\mathbb P} \left( \| {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(s) {-} {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(t) \| \ge {\varepsilon} \right) \le K \left( \frac{|s{-}t |^{1 {+} \gamma_1} }{{\varepsilon}^{c_1} } + \frac{ | s{-}t |^{1 {+} \gamma_2}}{{\varepsilon}^{c_2}} \right), \ \forall\, s,t \in [0, T], \forall \, n, \forall\, {\varepsilon} > 0.

nodes.name: Generator for the fast-scale limit
nodes.statement: In this section, we demonstrate that the sequence $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=1}^\infty$ \textit{approximately solves} the martingale problem for $({\mathcal A}^x, C^2_c({\mathbb R}^{d_x}) )$, where ${\mathcal A}^x$ is the generator defined as \begin{equation} {\mathcal A}^x f({x}) = \inner{- B_1 {x} }{ \nabla f({x}) } + \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{tr}( \nabla^2 f({x})\, \Sigma_{\xi} ), \ \forall f \in C^2_c({\mathbb R}^{d_x}). \end{equation}

nodes.label: eq:generator-twotime:Lx

nodes.name: Generator for the slow-scale limit
nodes.statement: Meanwhile, the sequence $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=1}^\infty$ \textit{approximately solves} the martingale problem for $({\mathcal A}^y, C^2_c({\mathbb R}^{d_y}) )$, where \begin{equation} {\mathcal A}^y g({y}) = \inner{- \Big( B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \Big) {y} }{ \nabla g({y}) } + \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{tr}( \nabla^2 g({y})\, \tilde{\Sigma}_{\psi} ), \ \forall g \in C^2_c({\mathbb R}^{d_y}). \end{equation} Here the matrix $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:cov-z}.

nodes.name: Slow-scale generator (31)
nodes.statement: {\mathcal A}^y g({y}) = \inner{- \Big( B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \Big) {y} }{ \nabla g({y}) } + \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{tr}( \nabla^2 g({y})\, \tilde{\Sigma}_{\psi} ), \ \forall g \in C^2_c({\mathbb R}^{d_y}).
nodes.label: eq:generator-twotime:Ly

nodes.name: Generators of the limiting SDEs
nodes.statement: Clearly, ${\mathcal A}_x$ and ${\mathcal A}_y$ are the generators associated to the SDEs in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} and \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}, respectively.
conclusions: ${\mathcal A}_x$ and ${\mathcal A}_y$ are the generators associated to the SDEs in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} and \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}, respectively

nodes.name: Approximately solving of martingale problems
nodes.statement: Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{assump:smooth} -- \ref{assump:stepsize-twotime}, \ref{assump:noise-fclt} and \ref{assump:mart-decouple-rate} hold. For each $n$, define the following filtrations \begin{align} \begin{split} {\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,t} & = \begin{cases} {\mathcal F}_{n}, & t = 0; \\ {\mathcal F}_{m+1}, & t \in \left( \sum_{i=n}^{m-1} \alpha_{i}, \sum_{i=n}^{m} \alpha_{i} \right] \text{ for } m \ge n; \end{cases} \\ {\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n,t} & = \begin{cases} {\mathcal F}_{n}, & t = 0; \\ {\mathcal F}_{m+1}, & t \in \left( \sum_{i=n}^{m-1} \beta_{i}, \sum_{i=n}^{m} \beta_{i} \right] \text{ for } m \ge n. \end{cases} \end{split} \end{align} \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For any $f \in C^2_c({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$ and $t \ge 0$, with ${\mathcal A}^x$ defined in \eqref{eq:generator-twotime:Lx}, we have the following decomposition \begin{equation*} f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)) - f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(0)) - \int_0^{t} {\mathcal A}^x f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s))\, \mathrm{d} s = {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t) + {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t), \end{equation*} where for each $n$, ${\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t)$ is a martingale w.r.t. $({\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,t} )_{t \ge 0}$ and for each $t$, ${\mathbb E} | {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t) | \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. \item For any $g \in C^2_c({\mathbb R}^{d_y})$ and $t \ge 0$, with ${\mathcal A}^y$ defined in \eqref{eq:generator-twotime:Ly}, we have the following decomposition \begin{equation*} g({\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(t)) - g({\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(0)) - \int_0^{t} {\mathcal A}^y f({\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(s))\, \mathrm{d} s = {\mathcal M}_{n}^g(t) + {\mathcal R}_{n}^g(t), \end{equation*} where for each $n$, ${\mathcal M}_{n}^g(t)$ is a martingale w.r.t. $( {\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n,t})_{t \ge 0}$ and for each $t$, ${\mathbb E} | {\mathcal R}_{n}^g(t) | \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $f(\bar X_n(t))-f(\bar X_n(0))-\int_0^t\mathcal A^x f$ splits into a martingale plus an $L_1$-vanishing residual; same for $\bar Z_n$ with $\mathcal A^y$.
nodes.label: lem:mart-prob-twotime

nodes.name: Filtrations of the interpolated processes (32)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} {\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,t} & = \begin{cases} {\mathcal F}_{n}, & t = 0; \\ {\mathcal F}_{m+1}, & t \in \left( \sum_{i=n}^{m-1} \alpha_{i}, \sum_{i=n}^{m} \alpha_{i} \right] \text{ for } m \ge n; \end{cases} \\ {\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n,t} & = \begin{cases} {\mathcal F}_{n}, & t = 0; \\ {\mathcal F}_{m+1}, & t \in \left( \sum_{i=n}^{m-1} \beta_{i}, \sum_{i=n}^{m} \beta_{i} \right] \text{ for } m \ge n. \end{cases} \end{split}
nodes.label: eq:filtration-main

nodes.name: Adaptedness of the interpolated processes
nodes.statement: The definition of filtrations in \eqref{eq:filtration-main} ensures that each ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)$ is adapted to $({\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n.t})_{t \ge 0}$ and each ${\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(t)$ is adapted to $({\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n,t})_{t \ge 0}$.

nodes.name: Approximately solving a martingale problem
nodes.statement: The term \textit{approximately solving} indicates that the residual terms ${\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t)$ and ${\mathcal R}_{n}^g(t)$ converging to $0$ in the $L_1$ sense as $n \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Convergence via approximate martingale problems
nodes.statement: Suppose that the generator ${\mathcal A}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:generator-general} and the following conditions are met. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item Given the initial distribution, the martingale problem for $({\mathcal A}, C_c^2({\mathbb R}^d))$ has a unique solution. \item $\{ {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=0}^\infty$ is a tight sequence in $C([0, \infty); {\mathbb R}^d)$. \item ${\textnormal{U}}_{n}(0) \Rightarrow {\textnormal{U}}(0)$. \item For any $k \ge 1$, $0 \le t_1 < t_2 < \dots < t_k \le t \le t+s $, and $f, h_1, h_2, \dots, h_k \in C_c^2({\mathbb R}^d)$, \begin{equation} \lim_{n \to \infty} {\mathbb E} \bigg[ \Big( f({\textnormal{U}}_{n}(t+s)) - f({\textnormal{U}}_{n}(t)) - \int_t^{t+s} {\mathcal A} f({\textnormal{U}}_{n}(r)) \,\mathrm{d} r \Big) \prod_{i=1}^k h_i({\textnormal{U}}_{n}(t_i)) \bigg] = 0. \end{equation} Then we have ${\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \Rightarrow {\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: the generator ${\mathcal A}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:generator-general}
Given the initial distribution, the martingale problem for $({\mathcal A}, C_c^2({\mathbb R}^d))$ has a unique solution.
$\{ {\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=0}^\infty$ is a tight sequence in $C([0, \infty); {\mathbb R}^d)$.
conclusions: ${\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) \Rightarrow {\textnormal{U}}(\cdot)$
nodes.label: prop:mart-prob-approx

nodes.name: Approximate martingale-problem condition (33)
nodes.statement: \lim_{n \to \infty} {\mathbb E} \bigg[ \Big( f({\textnormal{U}}_{n}(t+s)) - f({\textnormal{U}}_{n}(t)) - \int_t^{t+s} {\mathcal A} f({\textnormal{U}}_{n}(r)) \,\mathrm{d} r \Big) \prod_{i=1}^k h_i({\textnormal{U}}_{n}(t_i)) \bigg] = 0.
nodes.label: eq:generator-condition

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Theorem 4.1 (i)
nodes.statement: We now briefly illustrate how Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx} is applied with ${\mathcal A} = {\mathcal A}_x$ and ${\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) = {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ to derive the FCLT for ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:fclt-twotime}. The process can be divided into three parts, corresponding to the cyan, red, and black arrows in Figure~\ref{fig:proof-intergrate}. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item \textbf{FCLT for convergent subsequences}: Conditions~\ref{prop:final:condition:unique}, \ref{prop:final:condition:tight}, and \ref{prop:final:condition:mart-prob} are verified in Section~\ref{sec:fclt:prelim}, Lemmas~\ref{lem:tight-twotime} and \ref{lem:mart-prob-twotime}, respectively. Tightness ensures the existence of a convergent subsequence, and applying Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx} shows that the subsequence converges to a solution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde}. \item \textbf{Convergence of initial distributions}: Assumption~\ref{assump:hurwitz} guarantees both the uniqueness of the invariant distribution $\pi^\star$ and the geometric ergodicity for \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} (see Proposition~\ref{prop:ergo}). These properties ensure that all convergent subsequences of ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(0)$ have the same limit $\pi^\star$, which implies the convergence of ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(0)$. \item \textbf{FCLT for the entire sequence}: Applying Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx} to the full sequence establishes the desired FCLT. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: tightness plus approximate martingale problem give subsequential FCLT; ergodicity fixes the initial law; apply Prop. 5.2 to the whole sequence.

nodes.name: Outline: apply Prop. 5.2 with $\mathcal A^x$ and $\bar X_n$
nodes.statement: We now briefly illustrate how Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx} is applied with ${\mathcal A} = {\mathcal A}_x$ and ${\textnormal{U}}_{n}(\cdot) = {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ to derive the FCLT for ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:fclt-twotime}. The process can be divided into three parts, corresponding to the cyan, red, and black arrows in Figure~\ref{fig:proof-intergrate}.
nodes.statement_short: Outline: apply Prop. 5.2 with $\mathcal A^x$ and $\bar X_n$ in three parts

nodes.name: Verify conditions via Sec. 2, Lemmas 5.3 and 5.4
nodes.statement: \textbf{FCLT for convergent subsequences}: Conditions~\ref{prop:final:condition:unique}, \ref{prop:final:condition:tight}, and \ref{prop:final:condition:mart-prob} are verified in Section~\ref{sec:fclt:prelim}, Lemmas~\ref{lem:tight-twotime} and \ref{lem:mart-prob-twotime}, respectively. Tightness ensures the existence of a convergent subsequence, and applying Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx} shows that the subsequence converges to a solution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde}.
nodes.statement_short: Verify conditions via Sec. 2, Lemmas 5.3 and 5.4; subsequences converge to SDE solutions

nodes.name: Hurwitz assumption gives unique invariant law and ergodicity
nodes.statement: \textbf{Convergence of initial distributions}: Assumption~\ref{assump:hurwitz} guarantees both the uniqueness of the invariant distribution $\pi^\star$ and the geometric ergodicity for \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} (see Proposition~\ref{prop:ergo}). These properties ensure that all convergent subsequences of ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(0)$ have the same limit $\pi^\star$, which implies the convergence of ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(0)$.
nodes.statement_short: Hurwitz assumption gives unique invariant law and ergodicity, so initial laws converge

nodes.name: Apply Prop. 5.2 to the whole sequence
nodes.statement: \textbf{FCLT for the entire sequence}: Applying Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx} to the full sequence establishes the desired FCLT.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Prop. 5.2 to the whole sequence

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Corollary 5.1
nodes.statement: Similarly, we could obtain the following FCLT for ${\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(\cdot)$.
nodes.statement_short: By the same argument as for the fast iterate.

nodes.name: FCLT for the auxiliary sequence
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:fclt-twotime}, the stochastic process ${\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ defined in \eqref{eq:zbar-short} converges weakly to the stationary solution of the SDE in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}.
conclusions: the stochastic process ${\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ defined in \eqref{eq:zbar-short} converges weakly to the stationary solution of the SDE in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}
nodes.label: cor:fclt-z

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Theorem 4.1 (ii)
nodes.statement: From the construction of ${\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ and ${\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ in \eqref{eq:ybar-short} and \eqref{eq:zbar-short}, it follows that their finite-dimensional distributions share the same weak convergence limits. Consequently, by Proposition~\ref{prop:tight}, ${\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ and ${\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ converge to the same limit.
nodes.statement_short: $\bar Y_n$ and $\bar Z_n$ share fdd limits, so by tightness they share the weak limit of Corollary 5.1.

nodes.name: Local linearity of H is Holder continuity of its gradient
nodes.statement: Assumption~\ref{assump:smoothH} is equivalent to the H\"older continuity of $\nabla H$.

nodes.name: Holder continuity of the gradient of H
nodes.statement: Assume that $H(\cdot)$ is differentiable and there exist constants ${\widetilde{S}_H} \ge 0$ and ${\delta_H} \in [0,1]$ such that $\forall \, y_1, y_2 \in {\mathbb R}^{d_y}$, \begin{equation} \| \nabla H(y_1) - \nabla H(y_2) \| \le {\widetilde{S}_H} \| y_1 - y_2 \|^{{\delta_H}}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Holder continuity of grad H (34)
nodes.statement: \| \nabla H(y_1) - \nabla H(y_2) \| \le {\widetilde{S}_H} \| y_1 - y_2 \|^{{\delta_H}}.
nodes.label: assump:H:holder

nodes.name: Equivalence of local linearity and Holder gradient
nodes.statement: Suppose ${\delta_H} \in [0,1]$. Under Assumption~\ref{assump:H:holder-assump}, Assumption~\ref{assump:smoothH} holds with $S_H = \frac{{\widetilde{S}_H}}{1+{\delta_H}} $; under Assumption~\ref{assump:smoothH}, Assumption~\ref{assump:H:holder-assump} holds with ${\widetilde{S}_H} = 2^{1-{\delta_H}} \sqrt{1+{\delta_H}} \left( \frac{1+{\delta_H}}{{\delta_H}} \right)^\frac{{\delta_H}}{2} S_H$ (we make the contention that $\left( \frac{1+{\delta_H}}{{\delta_H}} \right)^\frac{{\delta_H}}{2} = 1$ if ${\delta_H} = 0$).

conclusions: Assumption~\ref{assump:smoothH} holds with $S_H = \frac{{\widetilde{S}_H}}{1+{\delta_H}} $
Assumption~\ref{assump:H:holder-assump} holds with
Assumption~\ref{assump:smoothH} holds with $S_H = \frac{{\widetilde{S}_H}}{1+{\delta_H}} $
Assumption~\ref{assump:H:holder-assump} holds with
nodes.label: prop:holder-equiv

nodes.name: Lowering the order of local linearity of H
nodes.statement: Suppose that \eqref{assump:smooth:FH:ineqH} holds. If Assumption~\ref{assump:smoothH} holds up to order $1 + {\delta_H}$, then it also holds up to order $1+{\delta_H}'$ for any ${\delta_H}' \in [0, {\delta_H}] $.
conclusions: it also holds up to order $1+{\delta_H}'$ for any ${\delta_H}' \in [0, {\delta_H}] $
nodes.label: prop:H-reduce-order

nodes.name: Lowering the order of local linearity of F and G
nodes.statement: Suppose that Assumption~\ref{assump:smooth} holds. If Assumption~\ref{assump:near-linear} holds up to order $(1+{\delta_F}, 1+{\delta_G})$, then it also holds up to order $(1+{\delta_F}', 1+{\delta_G}')$ for any ${\delta_F}' \in (0, {\delta_F})$ and ${\delta_G}' \in (0, {\delta_G})$.
conclusions: it also holds up to order $(1+{\delta_F}', 1+{\delta_G}')$ for any ${\delta_F}' \in (0, {\delta_F})$ and ${\delta_G}' \in (0, {\delta_G})$
nodes.label: prop:FG-reduce-order

nodes.name: Operator decomposition
nodes.statement_short: $F$, $G$ and increments of $H$ split into linear parts ($B_1$, $B_2$, $B_3$, $H^\star$) plus higher-order residuals.
nodes.label: prop:operator-decom

nodes.name: Implications of the step-size assumption
nodes.statement: We can derive the following results from Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime}. \begin{itemize} \item Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime} implies $\beta_n = \Omega(1/n)$ and $\alpha_{n} / \beta_{n} = \omega(1)$. Then we have $\ssum{n}{0}{\infty} \alpha_{n} = \ssum{n}{0}{\infty} \beta_{n} = \infty$, which is a ubiquitous condition in the SA analysis to ensure convergence to the target solution \citep{konda2004convergence, doan2022nonlinear, faizal2023functional}. \item Note that $\alpha_{n+1}^{-1} - \alpha_{n}^{-1} = \beta_{n+1}^{-1} \kappa_{n+1} - \beta_{n}^{-1} \kappa_{n} = \beta_{n+1}^{-1} (\kappa_{n+1} - \kappa_{n}) + \kappa_{n} ( \beta_{n+1}^{-1} - \beta_{n}^{-1} ) = \beta_{n+1}^{-1} \kappa_{n+1} ( 1 - \kappa_{n} / \kappa_{n+1} ) + \kappa_{n} ( \beta_{n+1}^{-1} - \beta_{n}^{-1} ) $. If we define $\tilde{\alpha} := \lim_{n \to \infty} (\alpha_{n+1}^{-1} - \alpha_{n}^{-1} )$ then we have $\tilde{\alpha} = 0$. This is why the choice of step sizes does not affect the SDE in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde}. The parameters $\tilde{\beta}$ and $\tilde{\alpha}$ also frequently in previous analysis \citep{konda2004convergence, faizal2023functional}. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Step-size conditions give divergent step-size sums and $\tilde\alpha=0$, so step sizes do not affect the fast-scale SDE.
nodes.label: rema:step-size

nodes.name: Linear case
nodes.statement: If $F$ and $G$ are linear operators, implying $H$ is also linear. the residual terms in Proposition~\ref{prop:operator-decom} vanish. Under this scenario, for Lemmas~\ref{lem:check-twotime-xy} and \ref{lem:check-twotime-z}, as well as Theorem~\ref{thm:fclt-twotime}, to hold, Condition~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime-moreab} in Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime} is no longer necessary. Moreover, the requirement for the boundedness of fourth moments can be relaxed to $p$-th moments for any $p>2$. For polynomially diminishing step sizes $\alpha_{n} = \alpha_{0} (n+1)^{-a}$ and $\beta_{n} = \beta_{0} (n+1)^{-b}$ with $a, b \in (0, 1]$, it suffices to ensure $b / a > 1$.

nodes.statement:

nodes.name: Combine the two bounds into a min with $R_H$
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{assump:smooth:FH:ineqH} and Assumption~\ref{assump:smoothH}, we have \begin{equation*} \| H(y_1) - H(y_2) - \nabla H(y_2) (y_1-y_2) \| \le S_H \|y_1-y_2\| \cdot \min\left\{\|y_1-y_2\|^{\delta_H}, R_H \right\} \end{equation*} with $R_H = \frac{2L_H}{S_H}$.

nodes.statement: Thus, by replacing $S_H$ with $\max\left\{S_H R_H^{{\delta_H} - {\delta_H}'}, S_H R_H / R_H^{{\delta_H}'} \right\}$, Assumption~\ref{assump:smoothH} holds up to order $1+{\delta_H}'$.
nodes.statement_short: Enlarge $S_H$ to conclude

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition A.3
nodes.statement: For ease of exposition, we let ${\hat{x}} = {x} - H({y})$ and ${\hat{y}} = {y} - {y}^\star$. First, these assumptions imply \begin{align*} \|F({x}, {y}) - B_1 {\hat{x}} \| & = \|F({x}, {y}) - F(H({y}), {y}) - B_1 {\hat{x}} \| \le 2 L_F \| {\hat{x}} \| + {\varepsilon} \cdot \| {\hat{y}} \|, \\ \| G({x}, {y}) - B_2 {\hat{x}} - B_3 {\hat{y}} ) \| & = \| G({x}, {y}) - G(H({y}), {y}) + G(H({y}), {y}) - G(H({y}^\star), {y}^\star) {-} B_2 {\hat{x}} {-} B_3 {\hat{y}} \| \\ & \le 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| + 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \|, \end{align*} where ${\varepsilon}$ is an arbitrary positive constant. In the following, we only prove that \eqref{assump:near-linear-G} holds after replacing ${\delta_G}$ with ${\delta_G}' \in (0, {\delta_G})$. The proof for \eqref{assump:near-linear-F} is similar. If (i) $ {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{x}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} \le 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| $ and ${S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{y}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} \le 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| $ or (ii) $ {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{x}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} > 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| $ and ${S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{y}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} > 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| $, we have \begin{align*} \| G({x}, {y}) - B_2 {\hat{x}} - B_3 {\hat{y}} ) \| & \le \min \left\{ {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{x}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} + {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{y}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}}, 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| + 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| \right\} \\ & = \min \left\{ {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{x}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}}, 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| \right\} + \min \left\{ {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{y}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}}, 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| \right\} \\ & = {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{x}} \| \cdot \min\left\{ \| {\hat{x}} \|^{\delta_G}, \frac{2 {L}_{G,x}}{{S}_{B,G}} \right\} + {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{y}} \| \cdot \min \left\{ \| {\hat{y}} \|^{{\delta_G}}, \frac{2{L}_{G,y}}{{S}_{B,G}} \right\}. \end{align*} Then the remaining proof is similar to that of Proposition~\ref{prop:H-reduce-order}. If neither of (i) and (ii) holds, without loss of generality we assume $ {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{x}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} \le 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| $ and ${S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{y}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} > 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| $. This implies $ \| {\hat{x}} \| \le c_x := (2 {L}_{G,x} / {S}_{B,G})^{1/{\delta_G}} $ and $\| {\hat{y}} \| > c_y := ( 2 {L}_{G,y} / {S}_{B,G} )^{1/{\delta_G}}$. Then we have \begin{align*} \| G({x}, {y}) - B_2 {\hat{x}} - B_3 {\hat{y}} ) \| & \le \min \left\{ {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{x}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} + {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{y}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}}, 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| + 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| \right\} \\ & \le 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| + 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| \le 2 {L}_{G,x}\, c_x + 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| \\ & \le \left( \frac{2 {L}_{G,x} c_x}{ c_y^{1+{\delta_G}'} } + \frac{2 {L}_{G,y}}{c_y^{{\delta_G}'}} \right) \| {\hat{y}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}'}. \end{align*} Thus \eqref{assump:near-linear-G} holds with ${\delta_G}$ and ${S}_{B,G}$ replaced with ${\delta_G}'$ and $\frac{2 {L}_{G,x} c_x}{ c_y^{1+{\delta_G}'} } + \frac{2 {L}_{G,y}}{c_y^{{\delta_G}'}}$ respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Bound residuals by both the Lipschitz and local-linearity estimates; case analysis on which is smaller, reducing to the argument for Prop. A.2.

nodes.name: Introduce $\hat x,\hat y$ and derive Lipschitz-type bounds
nodes.statement: For ease of exposition, we let ${\hat{x}} = {x} - H({y})$ and ${\hat{y}} = {y} - {y}^\star$. First, these assumptions imply \begin{align*} \|F({x}, {y}) - B_1 {\hat{x}} \| & = \|F({x}, {y}) - F(H({y}), {y}) - B_1 {\hat{x}} \| \le 2 L_F \| {\hat{x}} \| + {\varepsilon} \cdot \| {\hat{y}} \|, \\ \| G({x}, {y}) - B_2 {\hat{x}} - B_3 {\hat{y}} ) \| & = \| G({x}, {y}) - G(H({y}), {y}) + G(H({y}), {y}) - G(H({y}^\star), {y}^\star) {-} B_2 {\hat{x}} {-} B_3 {\hat{y}} \| \\ & \le 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| + 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \|, \end{align*} where ${\varepsilon}$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $\hat x,\hat y$ and derive Lipschitz-type bounds

nodes.name: Reduce to the $G$ inequality
nodes.statement: In the following, we only prove that \eqref{assump:near-linear-G} holds after replacing ${\delta_G}$ with ${\delta_G}' \in (0, {\delta_G})$. The proof for \eqref{assump:near-linear-F} is similar.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the $G$ inequality

nodes.name: Cases (i)/(ii): split the min and argue as for Prop. A.2
nodes.statement: If (i) $ {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{x}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} \le 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| $ and ${S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{y}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} \le 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| $ or (ii) $ {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{x}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} > 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| $ and ${S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{y}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} > 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| $, we have \begin{align*} \| G({x}, {y}) - B_2 {\hat{x}} - B_3 {\hat{y}} ) \| & \le \min \left\{ {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{x}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} + {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{y}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}}, 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| + 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| \right\} \\ & = \min \left\{ {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{x}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}}, 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| \right\} + \min \left\{ {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{y}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}}, 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| \right\} \\ & = {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{x}} \| \cdot \min\left\{ \| {\hat{x}} \|^{\delta_G}, \frac{2 {L}_{G,x}}{{S}_{B,G}} \right\} + {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{y}} \| \cdot \min \left\{ \| {\hat{y}} \|^{{\delta_G}}, \frac{2{L}_{G,y}}{{S}_{B,G}} \right\}. \end{align*} Then the remaining proof is similar to that of Proposition~\ref{prop:H-reduce-order}.
nodes.statement_short: Cases (i)/(ii): split the min and argue as for Prop. A.2

nodes.name: Mixed case: bound by a multiple of $\|\hat y\|^{1+\delta_G'}
nodes.statement: If neither of (i) and (ii) holds, without loss of generality we assume $ {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{x}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} \le 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| $ and ${S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{y}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} > 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| $. This implies $ \| {\hat{x}} \| \le c_x := (2 {L}_{G,x} / {S}_{B,G})^{1/{\delta_G}} $ and $\| {\hat{y}} \| > c_y := ( 2 {L}_{G,y} / {S}_{B,G} )^{1/{\delta_G}}$. Then we have \begin{align*} \| G({x}, {y}) - B_2 {\hat{x}} - B_3 {\hat{y}} ) \| & \le \min \left\{ {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{x}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} + {S}_{B,G} \| {\hat{y}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}}, 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| + 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| \right\} \\ & \le 2 {L}_{G,x} \| {\hat{x}} \| + 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| \le 2 {L}_{G,x}\, c_x + 2 {L}_{G,y} \| {\hat{y}} \| \\ & \le \left( \frac{2 {L}_{G,x} c_x}{ c_y^{1+{\delta_G}'} } + \frac{2 {L}_{G,y}}{c_y^{{\delta_G}'}} \right) \| {\hat{y}} \|^{1+{\delta_G}'}. \end{align*} Thus \eqref{assump:near-linear-G} holds with ${\delta_G}$ and ${S}_{B,G}$ replaced with ${\delta_G}'$ and $\frac{2 {L}_{G,x} c_x}{ c_y^{1+{\delta_G}'} } + \frac{2 {L}_{G,y}}{c_y^{{\delta_G}'}}$ respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Mixed case: bound by a multiple of $\|\hat y\|^{1+\delta_G'}$

nodes.name: Non-asymptotic convergence rates (formal)
nodes.statement: Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{assump:smooth} -- \ref{assump:noise-fclt} and the following strong monotonicity conditions hold: (i) there exists a constant $\mu_{F} > 0$ such that for any $y \in {\mathbb R}^{d_y}$ and $x \in {\mathbb R}^{d_x}$, $\left\langle x - H(y), F(x,y) - F(H(y),y) \right\rangle \geq \mu_{F} \|x-H(y)\|^2$; (ii) there exists a constant $\mu_{G} > 0$ such that for any $ y\in{\mathbb R}^{d_y}$, $\left\langle y - y^{\star}, G(H(y),y) - G(H(y^\star), y^\star) \right\rangle \geq \mu_{G} \|y - y^{\star}\|^2$. Then we have ${\mathbb E} \| {\hat{x}}_{n} \|^4 + {\mathbb E} \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \|^4 = {\mathcal O} (\alpha_{n}^2)$. If we further assume $b/a \le 1 + {\delta_F}/2$ in the step size selection of Example~\ref{exmp:fclt-stepsize}, we have ${\mathbb E} \| {\hat{x}}_{n} \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\alpha_{n}) $ and ${\mathbb E} \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\beta_{n})$.
