nodes.name: Time interpolation
nodes.statement: For the step size sequences $\{ \alpha_{n} \}_{n=0}^\infty$ and $\{ \beta_{n} \}_{n=0}^\infty$, $n, n' \in {\mathbb N}$ with $n' > n$ and $t \ge 0$, we define \begin{align*} \Gamma^\alpha_{n, n'} := \ssum{k}{n}{n'-1} \alpha_{k},\ N^\alpha(n, t) := \max \left\{ m \ge n \colon \Gamma^\alpha_{n, m} \le t \right\}, \ \text{ and } \ \underline{t}^\alpha_{n} = \Gamma^\alpha_{n, N^\alpha(n,t)} , \\ \Gamma^\beta_{n, n'} := \ssum{k}{n}{n'-1} \beta_{k}, \ N^\beta(n, t) := \max \left\{ m \ge n \colon \Gamma^\beta_{n,m} \le t \right\}, \ \text{ and } \ \underline{t}^\beta_{n} = \Gamma^\beta_{n, N^\beta(n,t)}. \end{align*} For $n' \le n$, we stipulate $\Gamma^\alpha_{n,n'} = \Gamma^\beta_{n,n'} := 0 $.
nodes.statement_short: Cumulative step sizes $\Gamma_{n,n'}$, the last index $N(n,t)$ with $\Gamma_{n,N}\le t$, and the left grid point $\underline t_n$.
nodes.label: defn:time-inter

nodes.name: Properties of time interpolation
nodes.statement: Under Definition~\ref{defn:time-inter}, we have the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For $n_1 \le n_2 \le n_3$, $\Gamma^\alpha_{n_1, n_2} + \Gamma^\alpha_{n_2, n_3} = \Gamma^\alpha_{n_1, n_3}$. \item For $m \ge n$, $N^\alpha(n, \Gamma^\alpha_{n,m}) = m $. \item $\underline{t}^\alpha_{n} \le t < \underline{t}^\alpha_{n} + \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,t)} $. When $t = \Gamma^\alpha_{n, m}$ for some $m \ge n$, $t = \underline{t}^\alpha_{n} $. \item As $n \to \infty$, if $\alpha_{n} \to 0 $, then $\underline{t}^\alpha_{n} \uparrow t$. \end{enumerate} Similar properties hold if the superscript is replaced by $\beta$.

nodes.name: Magnitude of the interpolation index
nodes.statement: Suppose that Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime} holds. There exist two positive constants $c_\alpha$ and $c_\beta$ such that for any $t>0$ and $n \in {\mathbb N}$, \begin{equation*} n \le N^\alpha(n,t) \le 2^{ \left\lceil 2t/c_\alpha \right\rceil + 1} n \quad \text{ and } \quad n \le N^\beta(n,t) \le 2^{ \left\lceil 2t/c_\beta \right\rceil + 1} n. \end{equation*} As a corollary, $\frac{\alpha_{n}}{ \alpha_{N^\alpha (n, t) } } \le 2^{ \left\lceil 2t/c_\alpha \right\rceil + 1}$ and $\frac{\beta_{n}}{ \beta_{N^\beta (n, t) } } \le 2^{ \left\lceil 2t/c_\beta \right\rceil + 1}$.
conclusions: There exist two positive constants $c_\alpha$ and $c_\beta$ such that for any $t>0$ and $n \in {\mathbb N}$,
nodes.label: lem:aux:bounded

nodes.name: Equivalent expression of the interpolated trajectories
nodes.statement: With Definition~\ref{defn:time-inter}, the construction in \eqref{eq:xbar-short}, \eqref{eq:ybar-short} and \eqref{eq:zbar-short} can be equivalently expressed as follows \begin{align} \begin{split} {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t) & \overset{\eqref{eq:xbar-short}}{=} {\check{x}}_{ N^\alpha(n,t) } + \frac{t - \underline{t}^\alpha_{n}}{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,t)} } \big( {\check{x}}_{ N^\alpha(n,t) + 1} - {\check{x}}_{ N^\alpha(n,t) } \big) \\ & \overset{\eqref{eq:xcheck-twotime}}{=} {\check{x}}_{ N^\alpha(n,t) } + (t - \underline{t}^\alpha_{n} ) \left( - B_1 {\check{x}}_{N^\alpha(n,t)} + \frac{R_{N^\alpha(n,t)}^x}{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,t)} } \right) - \frac{t - \underline{t}^\alpha_{n}}{ \sqrt{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,t)} } } \tilde{\xi}_{N^\alpha(n,t)}. \end{split} \\ \begin{split} {\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(t) & \overset{\eqref{eq:ybar-short}}{=} {\check{y}}_{ N^\beta(n,t) } + \frac{t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}}{\beta_{N^\beta(n,t)}} \big( {\check{y}}_{ N^\beta(n,t)+1 } - {\check{y}}_{ N^\beta(n,t) } \big) \\ & \overset{\eqref{eq:ycheck-twotime}}{=} {\check{y}}_{ N^\beta(n,t) } + (t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n} ) \left[ \Big(- B_3 + \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \Big) {\check{y}}_{N^\beta(n,t)} + \frac{R_{N^\beta(n,t)}^y }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } \right] - \frac{t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}} {\sqrt{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } } \psi_{N^\beta(n,t)} \\ & \qquad - (t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}) \sqrt{ \frac{ \alpha_{N^\beta(n,t)} }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } } B_2 {\check{x}}_{N^\beta(n,t)}. \end{split}\\ \begin{split} {\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(t) & \overset{\eqref{eq:zbar-short}}{=} {\check{z}}_{ N^\beta(n,t) } + \frac{t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}}{\beta_{N^\beta(n,t)}} \big( {\check{z}}_{ N^\beta(n,t)+1 } - {\check{z}}_{ N^\beta(n,t) } \big) \\ & \overset{\eqref{eq:zcheck-twotime}}{=} {\check{z}}_{ N^\beta(n,t) } + (t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n} ) \left[ \Big(- B_3 + \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \Big) {\check{z}}_{N^\beta(n,t)} + \frac{R_{N^\beta(n,t)}^z }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } \right] - \frac{t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}}{ \sqrt{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)}} } \tilde{\psi}_{N^\beta(n,t)}. \end{split} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $\bar X_n$, $\bar Y_n$, $\bar Z_n$ via $N(n,t)$ and the one-step recursions.

nodes.name: Interpolated fast trajectory via recursion (35)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t) & \overset{\eqref{eq:xbar-short}}{=} {\check{x}}_{ N^\alpha(n,t) } + \frac{t - \underline{t}^\alpha_{n}}{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,t)} } \big( {\check{x}}_{ N^\alpha(n,t) + 1} - {\check{x}}_{ N^\alpha(n,t) } \big) \\ & \overset{\eqref{eq:xcheck-twotime}}{=} {\check{x}}_{ N^\alpha(n,t) } + (t - \underline{t}^\alpha_{n} ) \left( - B_1 {\check{x}}_{N^\alpha(n,t)} + \frac{R_{N^\alpha(n,t)}^x}{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,t)} } \right) - \frac{t - \underline{t}^\alpha_{n}}{ \sqrt{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,t)} } } \tilde{\xi}_{N^\alpha(n,t)}. \end{split}

nodes.statement: \begin{split} {\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(t) & \overset{\eqref{eq:ybar-short}}{=} {\check{y}}_{ N^\beta(n,t) } + \frac{t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}}{\beta_{N^\beta(n,t)}} \big( {\check{y}}_{ N^\beta(n,t)+1 } - {\check{y}}_{ N^\beta(n,t) } \big) \\ & \overset{\eqref{eq:ycheck-twotime}}{=} {\check{y}}_{ N^\beta(n,t) } + (t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n} ) \left[ \Big(- B_3 + \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \Big) {\check{y}}_{N^\beta(n,t)} + \frac{R_{N^\beta(n,t)}^y }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } \right] - \frac{t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}} {\sqrt{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } } \psi_{N^\beta(n,t)} \\ & \qquad - (t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}) \sqrt{ \frac{ \alpha_{N^\beta(n,t)} }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } } B_2 {\check{x}}_{N^\beta(n,t)}. \end{split}

nodes.statement: \begin{split} {\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(t) & \overset{\eqref{eq:zbar-short}}{=} {\check{z}}_{ N^\beta(n,t) } + \frac{t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}}{\beta_{N^\beta(n,t)}} \big( {\check{z}}_{ N^\beta(n,t)+1 } - {\check{z}}_{ N^\beta(n,t) } \big) \\ & \overset{\eqref{eq:zcheck-twotime}}{=} {\check{z}}_{ N^\beta(n,t) } + (t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n} ) \left[ \Big(- B_3 + \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2} \Big) {\check{z}}_{N^\beta(n,t)} + \frac{R_{N^\beta(n,t)}^z }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } \right] - \frac{t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}}{ \sqrt{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)}} } \tilde{\psi}_{N^\beta(n,t)}. \end{split}

nodes.name: Grid properties of the interpolated trajectory
nodes.statement: Under Definition~\ref{defn:time-inter}, ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ satisfies the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For $m \ge n$, $ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\Gamma^\alpha_{n, m} ) = {\check{x}}_{m}$. \item ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t) = {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{t}_n^\alpha ) + \frac{t - \underline{t}^\alpha_{n}}{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,t)} } \big( {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{t}_n^\alpha + \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,t)} ) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{t}_n^\alpha ) \big)$. \item For $m \ge n$ and $t \in [\Gamma^\alpha_{n,m}, \Gamma^\alpha_{n,m+1})$, ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\underline{t}^\alpha_{n}) = {\check{x}}_{m}$. \end{enumerate} Similar results also hold for ${\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ and ${\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(\cdot)$.
nodes.label: fact2

nodes.name: Discussion on the interpolation
nodes.statement: For the way of interpolation in our works, \cite{faizal2023functional} also adopts the linear interpolation while \cite{gadat2018stochastic, liang2023asymptotic, blanchet2024limit} uses two different interpolations for different parts. Since both $\alpha_{N^\alpha(n,t)}$ and $\beta_{N^\beta(n,t)}$ converge to $0$ as $n \to \infty$, different interpolation methods make no difference in the asymptotic sense in our setup. We choose simple linear interpolation for analytical simplicity such that each trajectory is continuous in time.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma B.1
nodes.statement: We first prove the result for the sequence $\{ \beta_{n} \}$. From the definition of $N^\beta(n,t)$ in Definition~\ref{defn:time-inter}, we must have $N^\beta(n,t) \ge n$. Then the monotonicity of $n \beta_{n}$ in Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime} implies $\frac{\beta_{n}}{ \beta_{ N^\beta(n,t) } } \le \frac{ N^\beta(n,t) }{n}$. It remains to derive the upper bound of $\frac{ N^\beta(n,t) }{n} $. From Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime}, we have $\frac{ \beta_{n-1} }{ \beta_{n} } = 1 + {\mathcal O} (\beta_{n}) = 1 + {\mathcal O} (\beta_{n-1}) $. It follows that $\frac{1}{\beta_{n}} = \frac{1}{\beta_{n-1}} + {\mathcal O}(1) = \dots = {\mathcal O}(n) $, implying $\beta_{n} = \Omega \big( \frac{1}{n} \big)$. Consequently, there exists $c_\beta$ such that $\beta_{n} \ge \frac{c_\beta}{n} $ for any $n \in {\mathbb N}$. Meanwhile, for a fixed $n$, there exists a unique integer $k(n)$ such that $ 2^{k(n) - 1} \le n < 2^{k(n)} $. Then we have that for any $k' \ge k(n)$, \begin{equation*} \beta_{2^{k'} + 1} + \dots + \beta_{ 2^{k' + 1} } \ge c_\beta \left( \frac{1}{ 2^{k'} + 1 } + \frac{1}{ 2^{k'} + 2 } + \dots \frac{1}{ 2^{k'+1} } \right) \ge \frac{ c_\beta }{2}. \end{equation*} It follows that with $m(n) := 2^{ k(n) + \left\lceil 2t/ c_\beta \right\rceil } $, \begin{equation*} \Gamma^\beta_{n, m(n)+1} = \ssum{l}{n}{m(n)} \beta_{l} > \ssum{l}{2^{k(n)}+1}{2^{k(n) + \left\lceil 2t/c_\beta \right\rceil } } \beta_{l} \ge \left\lceil \frac{2t}{c_\beta} \right\rceil \frac{c_\beta}{2} \ge t. \end{equation*} From Definition~\ref{defn:time-inter}, we have $N^\beta(n,t) \le m(n) = 2^{ k(n) + \left\lceil 2t/c_\beta \right\rceil }$. Recall that $n \ge 2^{k(n)-1}$. It follows that $\frac{ N^\beta(n,t) }{n} \le 2^{ \left\lceil 2t/c_\beta \right\rceil + 1 }$. For the sequence $\{ \alpha_{n} \}$, Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime} guarantees that $n \alpha_{n}$ is non-decreasing and $\frac{\alpha_{n-1}}{\alpha_{n}} = 1 + o(\beta_{n}) = 1 + {\mathcal O}(\alpha_{n})$. Then following similar procedure, we have that there exists $c_\alpha > 0$ such that $ \frac{ \alpha_{n} }{ \alpha_{ N^\alpha(n,t) } } \le \frac{ N^\alpha(n,t) }{n} \le 2^{ \left\lceil 2t/c_\alpha \right\rceil + 1 }$.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\beta_n\ge c_\beta/n$; sum step sizes over dyadic blocks to bound $N^\beta(n,t)/n$; same for $\alpha_n$.

nodes.statement_short: Conclude $N^\beta(n,t)/n$ bound

nodes.name: Same argument for $\alpha_n$
nodes.statement: For the sequence $\{ \alpha_{n} \}$, Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime} guarantees that $n \alpha_{n}$ is non-decreasing and $\frac{\alpha_{n-1}}{\alpha_{n}} = 1 + o(\beta_{n}) = 1 + {\mathcal O}(\alpha_{n})$. Then following similar procedure, we have that there exists $c_\alpha > 0$ such that $ \frac{ \alpha_{n} }{ \alpha_{ N^\alpha(n,t) } } \le \frac{ N^\alpha(n,t) }{n} \le 2^{ \left\lceil 2t/c_\alpha \right\rceil + 1 }$.
nodes.statement_short: Same argument for $\alpha_n$

nodes.name: Markov decision process
nodes.statement: Consider an infinite-horizon MDP ${\mathcal M}=({\mathcal S}, {\mathcal A}, {\mathcal P} ,r, \gamma)$ with discounted rewards, where ${\mathcal S}$ and ${\mathcal A}$ denote the (finite) state space and action space, respectively, and $\gamma \in [0,1)$ is the discount factor.

nodes.name: Transition kernel
nodes.statement: The transition kernel ${\mathcal P} \colon {\mathcal S} \times {\mathcal A} \rightarrow \Delta({\mathcal S})$ specifies the probability distribution over the next states for each state-action pair $(s,a) \in {\mathcal S} \times {\mathcal A}$, where ${\mathcal P}(\cdot | s,a) \in \Delta({\mathcal S}) $ denotes the distribution of transitions from state $s$ when action $a$ is executed.

nodes.name: Reward function
nodes.statement: The reward function $r\colon {\mathcal S} \times {\mathcal A} \rightarrow [0,1]$ represents the immediate reward received from state $s$ when action $a$ is taken.

nodes.name: Policy
nodes.statement: A policy $\pi\colon {\mathcal S} \rightarrow \Delta({\mathcal A})$ maps each state to a probability distribution over actions.

nodes.name: Value function
nodes.statement: Its quality is assessed via the value function $$V^\pi(s) := {\mathbb E} \bigg[ \sum_{t=0}^\infty \gamma^t r(s_t, a_t) \,|\, s_0 = s,\ a_t \sim \pi(\cdot|a_t),\ s_{t+1} \sim {\mathcal P}(\cdot|s_t,a_t) \bigg], $$ which gives the expected discounted cumulative reward for following policy $\pi$.

nodes.name: Policy evaluation
nodes.statement: The process of estimating $V^\pi$ for a fixed policy $\pi$ is known as \textit{policy evaluation}.

nodes.name: Off-policy evaluation
nodes.statement: When the data is generated under a different policy $\pi_b$ to establish the value function $V^\pi$ of $\pi$, the task is referred to as \textit{off-policy evaluation}~\citep{uehara2022review}.

nodes.name: Linear function approximation
nodes.statement: A straightforward approach is linear function approximation, where $V^\pi(s) \approx V(s;y) = \phi(s)^\top y$, with $\phi(s)$ representing the feature vector of state $s$~\citep{dann2014policy}.

nodes.name: Rewards and importance weights in GTD
nodes.statement: In Example~\ref{exmp:gtd}, given the following i.i.d. samples $\{ (s_n, a_n, r(s_n, a_n), s'_{n}) \}_{n=0}^\infty$ with $a_n \sim \pi_b(\cdot | s_n)$ and $s'_{n} \sim {\mathcal P}(\cdot|s_{n}, a_{n})$, we define $r_{n} = r(s_n, a_n)$, and $\rho_{n} = \frac{\pi(a_n|s_n)}{\pi_b(a_n|s_n)}$.

nodes.name: Derivation that GTD2 and TDC share the same diffusion term
nodes.statement: As discussed in Remark~\ref{rema:fclt}, deriving $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}$ in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde} requires analyzing the asymptotic covariance of $\psi_{n} - B_2 B_1^{-1} \xi_{n} $. Suppose $(x_n, y_n)$ converges to $(x^\star, y^\star)$ in probability, as guaranteed by the results in~\cite{maei2011gradient}. For GTD2, we have $B_1 = C$ and $B_2 = -A^\top$, leading to \begin{align*} \psi^{\mathrm{GTD2}}_{n} - B_2 B_1^{-1} \xi_{n} & = -(A_{n}^\top {-} A^\top) x_{n} + A^\top C^{-1} [ (C_n {-} C) x_{n} + (A_n {-} A)y_{n} - (b_{n} {-} b) ] \\ & = A^\top C^{-1} ( A_{n} A^{-1} b - b_{n} ) + o_p(1) \end{align*} For TDC, $B_1 = C$ and $B_2 = D^\top = C-A^\top$. Then \begin{align*} \psi^{\mathrm{TDC}}_{n} - B_2 B_1^{-1}\xi_{n} & = (D_n^\top {-} D^\top) x_{n} + (A_{n} {-} A ) y_{n} - (b_{n} {-} b) \\ & \quad \ - (C - A^\top) C^{-1} [ (C_n {-} C) x_{n} + (A_n {-} A)y_{n} - (b_{n} {-} b) ] \\ & = A^\top C^{-1} ( A_{n} A^{-1} b - b_{n} ) + o_p(1). \end{align*} Thus, both GTD2 and TDC share the same $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}$.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $\psi_n-B_2B_1^{-1}\xi_n$ for GTD2 and TDC; both equal $A^\top C^{-1}(A_nA^{-1}b-b_n)+o_p(1)$.

nodes.name: Reduce to the covariance of $\psi_n-B_2B_1^{-1}\xi_n$, assum
nodes.statement: As discussed in Remark~\ref{rema:fclt}, deriving $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}$ in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde} requires analyzing the asymptotic covariance of $\psi_{n} - B_2 B_1^{-1} \xi_{n} $. Suppose $(x_n, y_n)$ converges to $(x^\star, y^\star)$ in probability, as guaranteed by the results in~\cite{maei2011gradient}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the covariance of $\psi_n-B_2B_1^{-1}\xi_n$, assuming consistency

nodes.name: Expand for GTD2
nodes.statement: For GTD2, we have $B_1 = C$ and $B_2 = -A^\top$, leading to \begin{align*} \psi^{\mathrm{GTD2}}_{n} - B_2 B_1^{-1} \xi_{n} & = -(A_{n}^\top {-} A^\top) x_{n} + A^\top C^{-1} [ (C_n {-} C) x_{n} + (A_n {-} A)y_{n} - (b_{n} {-} b) ] \\ & = A^\top C^{-1} ( A_{n} A^{-1} b - b_{n} ) + o_p(1) \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand for GTD2

nodes.name: Expand for TDC
nodes.statement: For TDC, $B_1 = C$ and $B_2 = D^\top = C-A^\top$. Then \begin{align*} \psi^{\mathrm{TDC}}_{n} - B_2 B_1^{-1}\xi_{n} & = (D_n^\top {-} D^\top) x_{n} + (A_{n} {-} A ) y_{n} - (b_{n} {-} b) \\ & \quad \ - (C - A^\top) C^{-1} [ (C_n {-} C) x_{n} + (A_n {-} A)y_{n} - (b_{n} {-} b) ] \\ & = A^\top C^{-1} ( A_{n} A^{-1} b - b_{n} ) + o_p(1). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand for TDC

nodes.name: Same limiting expression, hence same covariance
nodes.statement: Thus, both GTD2 and TDC share the same $\widetilde{\Sigma}_{\psi}$.
nodes.statement_short: Same limiting expression, hence same covariance

nodes.name: Proof of Lemmas 5.1 and 5.2
nodes.statement_short: Linearize via operator decomposition, rescale the error recursions, and bound residuals with the step-size and rate assumptions; combine for $\check z_n$. Key step: expanding $\sqrt{\beta_{n-1}/\beta_n}=1+\tilde\beta\beta_n/2+o(\beta_n)$.

nodes.name: Plan and update rules for $\hat x_n$, $\hat y_n$
nodes.statement: The proof is structured into three parts: we derive the one-step recursion first for ${\check{y}}_{n}$, followed by ${\check{x}}_{n}$, and finally ${\check{z}}_{n}$. To begin, we take the update rules for ${\hat{x}}_{n}$ and ${\hat{y}}_{n}$, as outlined below. \begin{align} {\hat{x}}_{n+1} & = {\hat{x}}_n - \alpha_n F(x_n, y_n) - \alpha_n \xi_n + H(y_n) - H(y_{n+1}), \\ {\hat{y}}_{n+1} & = {\hat{y}}_n - \beta_n G(H(y_n), y_n) + \beta_n ( G(H(y_n), y_n) - G(x_n, y_n) ) - \beta_n \psi_n. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Plan and update rules for $\hat x_n$, $\hat y_n$

nodes.name: Part 1: recursion and residual bounds for $\check y_n$
nodes.statement:
extbf{Part 1: one-step recursion for ${\check{y}}_{n}$}. By Proposition~ef{prop:operator-decom}, we can rewrite the update rule of ${\hat{y}}_{n}$ in \eqref{eq:yhat} as  egin{align} {\hat{y}}_{n+1} = (I -  eta_{n} B_3) {\hat{y}}_{n} -  eta_{n} B_2 {\hat{x}}_{n} -  eta_n \psi_n -  eta_n R_n^G. \end{align} Then from the definition of ${\check{y}}_{n}$ and \eqref{eq:yhat-decom}, we have  egin{align} {\check{y}}_{n+1} & = \sqrt{  rac{  eta_{n-1} }{  eta_{n} } } ({I} -  eta_{n} B_3) {\check{y}}_{n} - \sqrt{  eta_{n} \alpha_{n-1} } B_2 {\check{x}}_{n} - \sqrt{ eta_{n}} \psi_{n} - \sqrt{ eta_{n}} R_{n}^G 
onumber \ & = \left( {I} -  eta_{n} B_3 +  rac{ 	ilde{ eta}  eta_{n} }{2} {I} ight) {\check{y}}_{n} - \sqrt{ eta_{n} \alpha_{n} } B_2 {\check{x}}_{n} - \sqrt{ eta_n} \psi_{n} + R_{n}^y, \end{align} where  egin{align}  egin{split} R_{n}^y & = \underbrace{ \left( \sqrt{  rac{  eta_{n-1} }{ eta_{n}} } - 1 -  rac{ 	ilde{ eta}  eta_{n} }{2} ight) {\check{y}}_{n} }_{=: R_{n,1}^y} + \underbrace{ (  eta_{n} - \sqrt{  eta_{n}  eta_{n-1} } ) B_3 {\check{y}}_{n} \vphantom{ \left( \sqrt{  rac{  eta_{n-1} }{ eta_{n}} } ight) } }_{ =:R_{n,2}^y } \ & \quad \ + \underbrace{ ( \sqrt{  eta_{n} \alpha_{n} } - \sqrt{  eta_{n} \alpha_{n-1} } ) B_2 {\check{x}}_{n} \vphantom{ \left( \sqrt{  rac{  eta_{n-1} }{ eta_{n}} } ight) } }_{=: R_{n,3}^y } - \underbrace{ \sqrt{ eta_{n}} R_{n}^G \vphantom{ \left( \sqrt{  rac{  eta_{n-1} }{ eta_{n}} } ight) } }_{ =: R_{n,4}^y }. \end{split} \end{align} By Assumption~ef{assump:stepsize-twotime}, we have  egin{align} \sqrt{  rac{  eta_{n-1} }{  eta_{n} } } & = \sqrt{ 1 +  eta_{n-1} (  eta_{n}^{-1} -  eta_{n-1}^{-1} ) } = \sqrt{1 + 	ilde{ eta}  eta_{n-1} + o( eta_{n-1}) } 
onumber \ & = \sqrt{1 + 	ilde{ eta}  eta_{n} + o( eta_{n}) } = 1 +  rac{ 	ilde{ eta}  eta_{n} }{2} + o( eta_{n}), 
onumber \ \sqrt{  rac{ \alpha_{n-1} }{\alpha_{n}} } & = 1 + {\mathcal O}( eta_n), \qquad \sqrt{  rac{ \kappa_{n-1} }{\kappa_{n}} } = 1 + {\mathcal O}( eta_n). \end{align} It follows that $\| R_{n,1}^y \| + \| R_{n,2}^y \| = o( eta_{n}) \| {\check{y}}_{n} \| = o( eta_{n}^{1/2}) \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \| $ and $\| R_{n,3}^y \| = {\mathcal O}( eta_{n}^{3/2} \alpha_{n}^{1/2}) \| {\check{x}}_{n} \| = o( eta_{n}^{3/2}) \| {\hat{x}}_{n} \| $. Meanwhile, by Proposition~ef{prop:operator-decom}, we have $ \| R_{n,4}^y \| = {\mathcal O}( eta_{n}^{1/2}) ( \| {\hat{x}}_{n} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} + \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} ) $. Note that in Assumption~ef{assump:stepsize-twotime}, we require $\alpha_{n}^{1+{\delta_G}} = o( eta_{n}) $. Then we have  egin{align} \| R_{n}^y \| = o( eta_{n}^{1/2}) \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \| + o( eta_{n}^{3/2}) \| {\hat{x}}_{n} \| + {\mathcal O}( eta_{n}) \,  rac{ \alpha_{n}^{ (1+{\delta_G}) / 2 } }{  eta_{n}^{1/2} } \cdot  rac{ \| {\hat{x}}_{n} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} + \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} } {\alpha_{n}^{(1+{\delta_G})/2} }. \end{align} By Assumption~ef{assump:mart-decouple-rate}, it follows that $ {\mathbb E} \| {\mathbb E}[ R_{n}^y | {\mathcal F}_{n} ] \| \le {\mathbb E} \| R_{n}^y \| = o( eta_{n})$ and ${\mathbb E} \| R_{n}^y \|^2 = o( eta_{n}^2)$. Moreover, by Proposition~ef{prop:FG-reduce-order}, we have that \eqref{eq:lem:check-twotime:Ry-upper} holds with ${\delta_G}$ replaced by ${\delta_G} / 2$. For $2 \le p \le  rac{4}{1+{\delta_G} / 2}$, it follows that  egin{align*} {\mathbb E} \| R_{n}^y \|^p = o( eta_{n}) + o(  eta_{n} \cdot  eta_{n}^{p-1} / \alpha_{n}^{ p {\delta_G} / 2} ) = o( eta_{n}), \end{align*} where the last step is due to $p-1 \ge p/2 \ge p {\delta_G} / 2$.
nodes.statement_short: Part 1: recursion and residual bounds for $\check y_n$

nodes.name: Part 2: recursion and residual bounds for $\check x_n$
nodes.statement_short: Part 2: recursion and residual bounds for $\check x_n$

nodes.name: Part 3: combine Parts 1-2 for $\check z_n$
nodes.statement: \textbf{Part 3: one-step recursion for ${\check{z}}_{n}$}. From the definition of ${\check{z}}_{n}$ and the update rules of ${\check{y}}_{n}$ and ${\check{x}}_{n}$ in \eqref{eq:lem:check-twotime:y-update} and \eqref{eq:lem:check-twotime:x-update} , we have \begin{align*} {\check{z}}_{n+1} & = {\check{y}}_{n+1} - \sqrt{\kappa_{n}} B_2 B_1^{-1} {\check{x}}_{n+1} \\ & = \left( {I} - \beta_{n} B_3 + \frac{\tilde{\beta} \beta_{n}}{2} {I} \right) ({\check{z}}_{n} + \sqrt{\kappa_{n-1}} B_2 B_1^{-1} {\check{x}}_{n}) - \sqrt{ \beta_{n} \alpha_{n} } B_2 {\check{x}}_{n} - \sqrt{ \beta_{n} } \psi_{n} + R_{n}^y \\ & \quad - \sqrt{\kappa_{n}} B_2 B_1^{-1} \left[ ({I} - \alpha_{n} B_1 ) {\check{x}}_{n} - \sqrt{\alpha_{n}} \tilde{\xi}_{n} + R_{n}^x \right] \\ & = \left( {I} - \beta_{n} B_3 + \frac{\tilde{\beta} \beta_{n}}{2} {I} \right) {\check{z}}_{n} - \sqrt{\beta_{n}} \tilde{\psi}_{n} + R_{n}^z, \end{align*} where $\tilde{\psi}_{n} := \psi_{n} - B_2 B_1^{-1} \tilde{\xi}_n = ({I} + \kappa_{n} B_2 B_1^{-1} H^\star) \psi_{n} - B_2 B_1^{-1} \xi_{n}$ and \begin{align*} R_{n}^z & = \underbrace{ (\sqrt{\kappa_{n-1}} {-} \sqrt{\kappa_{n}}) B_2 B_1^{-1} {\check{x}}_{n} }_{=: R_{n,1}^z} - \underbrace{ \sqrt{\kappa_{n-1}} \beta_{n} (B_3 {-} \tilde{\beta} {I} / 2) B_2 B_1^{-1} {\check{x}}_{n} }_{=: R_{n,2}^z} + R_{n}^{y} - \sqrt{\kappa_{n}} B_2 B_1^{-1} R_{n}^x. \end{align*} By \eqref{eq:lem:check-twotime:sqrtalpha}, we have $\| R_{n,1}^z \| + \| R_{n,2}^z \| = o(\beta_{n}) \| {\check{x}}_{n} \|$. Moreover, from the definitions of $R_{n}^y$ and $R_{n}^x$ in \eqref{eq:lem:check-twotime:Ry} and \eqref{eq:lem:check-twotime:Rx} and the analysis in Parts~1 and 2, we can obtain ${\mathbb E} \| {\mathbb E} [ R_{n}^z | {\mathcal F}_{n} ] \| = o(\beta_{n}) $, ${\mathbb E} \| R_{n}^z \|^2 = {\mathcal O} (\beta_{n}^2)$ and ${\mathbb E} \| R_{n}^z \|^p = o(\beta_{n})$ for $2 \le p \le \frac{4}{1 + ( {\delta_H} \vee {\delta_F} \vee {\delta_G} )/2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Part 3: combine Parts 1-2 for $\check z_n$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.3 (tightness)
nodes.statement_short: Verify the two sufficient conditions of Prop. 5.1 via Markov, Cauchy-Schwarz and Burkholder bounds for $\bar X_n$, $\bar Z_n$. Key step for $\bar Y_n$: expand $\hat x_k$ recursively to control the coupling term $B^{(2x,n)}$.

nodes.name: Order of the three tightness proofs
nodes.statement: We begin by proving the tightness of $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=1}^\infty$. The tightness of $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=1}^\infty$ can be established using a similar approach. Finally, we address the tightness of $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=1}^\infty$, which is the primary challenge in this proof.
nodes.statement_short: Order of the three tightness proofs

nodes.name: Part 1: tightness of $\bar X_n$ via Prop. 5.1
nodes.statement_short: Part 1: tightness of $\bar X_n$ via Prop. 5.1

nodes.name: Part 2: tightness of $\bar Z_n$ similarly
nodes.statement: \textbf{Part~2: the tightness of $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=1}^\infty$}. Note that in the proof of Part~1, the only place we employed Lemma~\ref{lem:check-twotime-xy} is \eqref{eq:lem:tight-twotime:l2bound-x} and in fact, we only require ${\mathbb E} \| R_{n}^x \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\alpha_{n}^2)$. Moreover, the dimension $d_x$ would not affect the proof. The tightness of $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=1}^\infty$ follows from a similar procedure by applying the residual bounds in Lemma~\ref{lem:check-twotime-z}.
nodes.statement_short: Part 2: tightness of $\bar Z_n$ similarly

nodes.name: Part 3: decompose $\bar Y_n$ increments and bound two terms
nodes.statement: \textbf{Part~3: the tightness of $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=1}^\infty$}. Note that Assumption~\ref{assump:mart-decouple-rate} implies ${\mathbb E} \| {\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(0) \|^2 = {\mathbb E} \| {\check{y}}_{n} \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(1)$. Then by Markov's inequality, the first condition in Proposition~\ref{prop:tight-suff-slow} holds. Now we verify the second condition. Without loss of generality, we assume $0 \le t < s \le T$. For ease of notation, we define $\widetilde{B}_3 := B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta} {I}}{2}$. From the definition of ${\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(t)$ in \eqref{eq:def:ybar}, we have \begin{align*} {\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(s) - {\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(t) & \overset{\eqref{eq:def:ybar}}{=} {\check{y}}_{N^\beta(n,s)} + (s - \underline{s}^\beta_{n} ) \left( - \widetilde{B}_3 {\check{y}}_{N^\beta(n,s)} + \frac{ R_{N^\beta(n,s)}^y }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,s)} } \right) - \frac{s - \underline{s}^\beta_{n}}{ \sqrt{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,s) } } } \psi_{N^\beta(n,s)} \\ & \qquad - {\check{y}}_{N^\beta(n,t)} - (t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n} ) \left( - \widetilde{B}_3 {\check{y}}_{N^\beta(n,t)} + \frac{ R_{N^\beta(n,t)}^y }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } \right) + \frac{t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}}{ \sqrt{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } } \psi_{N^\beta(n,t)} \\ & \qquad - (s - \underline{s}^\beta_{n}) \sqrt{ \frac{ \alpha_{N^\beta(n,s)} }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,s)} } } B_2 {\check{x}}_{N^\beta(n,s)} + (t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}) \sqrt{ \frac{ \alpha_{N^\beta(n,t)} }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } } B_2 {\check{x}}_{N^\beta(n,t)} \\ & \overset{\eqref{eq:ycheck-twotime}}{=} \Bigg\{ \ssum{k}{N^\beta(n,t)}{N^\beta(n,s)-1} \beta_{k} \left( - \widetilde{B}_3 {\check{y}}_{k} + \frac{R_{k}^y}{\beta_{k}} \right) - (t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n} ) \left( - \widetilde{B}_3 {\check{y}}_{N^\beta(n,t)} + \frac{ R_{N^\beta(n,t)}^y }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } \right) \\ & \qquad+ (s - \underline{s}^\beta_{n} ) \left( - \widetilde{B}_3 {\check{y}}_{N^\beta(n,s)} + \frac{ R_{N^\beta(n,s)}^y }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,s)} } \right) \Bigg\} - \Bigg\{ \ssum{k}{N^\beta(n,t)}{N^\beta(n,s)-1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \psi_{k} \\ & \qquad - \frac{t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}}{ \sqrt{\beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } } \psi_{N^\beta(n,t)} + \frac{s - \underline{s}^\beta_{n}}{ \sqrt{\beta_{N^\beta(n,s)} } } \psi_{N^\beta(n,s)} \Bigg\} - \Bigg\{ \ssum{k}{N^\beta(n,t)}{N^\beta(n,s)-1} \beta_{k} \sqrt{ \frac{\alpha_{k}}{\beta_{k}} } B_2 {\check{x}}_{k} \\ & \qquad - (t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}) \sqrt{ \frac{ \alpha_{N^\beta(n,t)} }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } } B_2 {\check{x}}_{N^\beta(n,t)} + (s - \underline{s}^\beta_{n}) \sqrt{ \frac{ \alpha_{N^\beta(n,s)} }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,s)} } } B_2 {\check{x}}_{N^\beta(n,s)} \Bigg\} \\ & =: {\bf B}^{(3y,n)}_{t,s} - \mbox{\boldmath$\Psi$\unboldmath}^{(n)}_{t,s} - {\bf B}^{(2x,n)}_{t,s}. \end{align*} For the first and second terms, similar to the derivation of \eqref{eq:lem:tight-twotime:B1x} and \eqref{eq:lem:tight-twotime:xii}, with $p \in \left(2, \frac{4}{1 + ( {\delta_H} \vee {\delta_F} \vee {\delta_G} )/2} \right]$, there exist $K_3, K_4$ such that for any $n$, \begin{align} {\mathbb E} \| {\bf B}^{(3y,n)}_{t,s} \|^2 \le K_3 (s-t)^2 \quad \text{ and } \quad {\mathbb E} \| \mbox{\boldmath$\Psi$\unboldmath}^{(n)}_{t,s} \|^p \le K_4 (s-t)^\frac{p}{2}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Part 3: decompose $\bar Y_n$ increments and bound two terms

nodes.name: Naive Cauchy-Schwarz fails for the coupling term
nodes.statement: \textbf{Main difficulty}. The main difficulty lies to how to deal with the last term $ {\bf B}^{(2x,n)}_{t,s}$. If we adopt a similar procedure of deriving \eqref{eq:lem:tight-twotime:B1x} by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we could only obtain \[{\mathbb E} \| {\bf B}^{(2x,n)}_{t,s} \|^2 \lesssim (s-t) \left( \ssum{k}{N^\beta(n,t)}{N^\beta(n,s)} \beta_{k} \frac{\alpha_{k} }{\beta_{k}} \right) \lesssim (s-t)^2 \max_{k \ge N^\beta(n,s)} \frac{\alpha_{k}}{\beta_{k}}. \] Since Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime}~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime-tozero} implies $\max_{k \ge N^\beta(n,s)} \alpha_{k} / \beta_{k} \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, this upper bound becomes ineffective.
nodes.statement_short: Naive Cauchy-Schwarz fails for the coupling term

nodes.name: Expand $\hat x_k$ recursively, bound via Lemma C.1, conclude
nodes.statement: \textbf{Solution approach}. To address this issue, we need to provide a more precise characterization of $ {\bf B}^{(2x,n)}_{t,s}$. A natural approach is to further expand each ${\check{x}}_{k}$. While this idea is feasible, it leads to more complex calculations, as each ${\check{x}}_{k}$ depends on both ${\check{x}}_{k-1}$ and ${\check{y}}_{k-1}$. Below, we outline the detailed process. To begin, we define another term ${\bf B}^{(2x)}_{n_0,n_1} := \ssum{k}{n_0}{n_1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} B_2 {\hat{x}}_{k}$. Here, we use the unrescaled iterate to simplify the subsequent calculations. Given that ${\check{x}}_{k} = {\hat{x}}_{k} / \sqrt{\alpha_{k-1} }$, it follows that ${\bf B}^{(2x)}_{n_0,n_1} = \ssum{k}{n_0}{n_1} \sqrt{ \beta_{k} \alpha_{k-1} } B_2 {\check{x}}_{k} $, which demonstrates that this term is closely related to ${\bf B}^{(2x,n)}_{t,s}$, as shown in the following equation \begin{align*} {\bf B}^{(2x,n)}_{t,s} & = {\bf B}^{(2x)}_{N^\beta(n,t), N^\beta(n,s)-1} - (t - \underline{t}^\beta_{n}) \sqrt{ \frac{ \alpha_{N^\beta(n,t)} }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,t)} } } B_2 {\check{x}}_{N^\beta(n,t)} \\ & \qquad + (s - \underline{s}^\beta_{n}) \sqrt{ \frac{ \alpha_{N^\beta(n,s)} }{ \beta_{N^\beta(n,s)} } } B_2 {\check{x}}_{N^\beta(n,s)} + \ssum{k}{N^\beta(n,t)}{N^\beta(n,s)-1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \left( \sqrt{ \frac{\alpha_{k}}{\alpha_{k-1}} } - 1 \right) B_2 {\hat{x}}_{k}. \end{align*} By the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have \begin{align*} & {\mathbb E} \left\| \ssum{k}{N^\beta(n,t)}{N^\beta(n,s)-1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \left( \sqrt{ \frac{\alpha_{k}}{\alpha_{k-1}} } - 1 \right) B_2 {\hat{x}}_{k} \right\|^2 \\ & \qquad \qquad \le \left( \ssum{k}{N^\beta(n,t)}{N^\beta(n,s)-1} \beta_{k} \right) \left[ \ssum{k} {N^\beta(n,t)}{N^\beta(n,s)-1} \Big( \sqrt{ \frac{\alpha_{k}}{\alpha_{k-1}} } - 1 \Big)^2 {\mathbb E} \| B_2 {\hat{x}}_{k} \|^2 \right]. \end{align*} In \eqref{eq:lem:check-twotime:sqrtalpha}, we have shown that $\sqrt{ \frac{\alpha_{k}}{\alpha_{k-1}} } - 1 = o(\beta_k)$. Assumption~\ref{assump:mart-decouple-rate} implies ${\mathbb E} \| B_2 {\hat{x}}_{k} \|^2 = o(1)$. Moreover, $t' - (\underline{t'})^\beta_{n} \le \beta_{N^\beta(n,t')}$ for $t'=t,s$. Summarizing the above results and following a similar procedure as \eqref{eq:lem:tight-twotime:B1x}, we can obtain that there exists $K_5$ such that \begin{align} {\mathbb E} \| {\bf B}^{(2x,n)}_{t,s} - {\bf B}^{(2x)}_{N^\beta(n,t), N^\beta(n,s)-1} \|^2 \le K_5 (s-t)^2 \end{align} for any $n$. This inequality controls the difference between ${\bf B}^{(2x,n)}_{t,s}$ and ${\bf B}^{(2x)}_{N^\beta(n,t), N^\beta(n,s)-1}$. \vspace{0.2cm} From now on, we always assume $n_0 = N^\beta(n,t)$ and $n_1 = N^\beta(n,s)-1$ and It remains to deal with the term ${\bf B}^{(2x)}_{n_0, n_1}$. Recall that the update rule of ${\hat{x}}_{n}$ is shown in \eqref{eq:xhat-decom}. For ease of notation, we define $A_{n}:= {I} - \alpha_{n} B_1 + \beta_{n} H^\star B_2$, $\tilde{\xi}_{n} := \xi_{n} - \beta_{n} H^\star \psi_{n} / \alpha_{n}$ and $\tilde{R}^x_{n} := R^{\nabla H}_{n} + R^H_{n} + \alpha_{n} R^F_{n} - \beta_{n} H^\star R^G_{n}$. Then the update rule of ${\hat{x}}_{n}$ can be rewritten as \begin{align*} {\hat{x}}_{n+1} = A_{n} {\hat{x}}_{n} + \beta_{n} H^\star B_3 {\hat{y}}_{n} - \alpha_{n} \tilde{\xi}_{n} - \tilde{R}^x_{n}. \end{align*} Applying this equation multiple times yields \begin{align*} {\hat{x}}_{n+m} = \bigg( \prod_{i=1}^{m} A_{n+m-i} \bigg) {\hat{x}}_{n} + \sum_{l=n}^{n+m-1} \bigg( \prod_{i=1}^{n+m-l-1} A_{n+m-i} \bigg) \big( \beta_{l} H^\star B_3 {\hat{y}}_{l} - \alpha_{l} \tilde{\xi}_{l} - \tilde{R}^x_{l} \big). \end{align*} It follows that \begin{align*} {\bf B}^{(2x)}_{n_0, n_1} & = \ssum{k}{n_0}{n_1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} B_2 \left[ \bigg( \prod_{i=1}^{k-n_{0}} A_{k-i} \bigg) {\hat{x}}_{n_0} + \ssum{l}{n_0}{k-1} \bigg( \prod_{i=1}^{k-l-1} A_{k-i} \bigg) \big( \beta_{l} H^\star B_3 {\hat{y}}_{l} - \alpha_{l} \tilde{\xi}_{l} - \tilde{R}^x_{l} \big) \right] \\ & = \ssum{k}{n_0}{n_1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} B_2 \bigg( \prod_{i=1}^{k-n_{0}} A_{k-i} \bigg) {\hat{x}}_{n_0} + \ssum{l}{n_0}{n_1-1} \ssum{k}{l+1}{n_1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} B_2 \bigg( \prod_{i=1}^{k-l-1} A_{k-i} \bigg) \big( \beta_{l} H^\star B_3 {\hat{y}}_{l} {-} \alpha_{l} \tilde{\xi}_{l} {-} \tilde{R}^x_{l} \big) \\ & = \underbrace{ B_2 \widetilde{\Gamma}_{n_0, n_1} {\hat{x}}_{n_0} + B_2 \ssum{l}{n_0}{n_1-1} \widetilde{\Gamma}_{l+1, n_1} \big( \beta_{l} H^\star B_3 {\hat{y}}_{l} - \tilde{R}^x_{l} \big) }_{:= {\bf B}^{(2x,1)}_{n_0,n_1} } - \underbrace{ B_2 \ssum{l}{n_0}{n_1-1} \widetilde{\Gamma}_{l+1, n_1} \alpha_{l} \tilde{\xi}_{l} }_{:= {\bf B}^{(2x,2)}_{n_0,n_1} }, \end{align*} where we define $\widetilde{\Gamma}_{m, j} := \ssum{k}{m}{j} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \bigg( \prod_{i=1}^{k-m} A_{k-i} \bigg)$ in the last step. The magnitude of $\widetilde{\Gamma}_{m, j}$ can be controlled by the following auxiliary lemma, whose proof is deferred to the end of this subsection. \begin{lem} Suppose that Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime} holds and the real parts of the eigenvalues of $B_1$ are no less than $\mu_1$. Define $A_{k}:= {I} - \alpha_{k} B_1 + \beta_{k} H^\star B_2$. If $t$ and $s$ are fixed positive numbers satisfying $s>t$ and $n$ is sufficiently large, then for any $N^\beta(n,t) \le l < N^\beta(n, s)$, we have \begin{align*} \left\| \sum_{k=l+1}^{N^\beta(n,s)-1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \prod_{i=1}^{k-l-1} A_{k-i} \right\| \le \frac{ 2^{ \left\lceil 2s/c_\alpha \right\rceil + 3} }{\mu_1} \cdot \frac{ \sqrt{\beta_{l}} }{ \alpha_{l} }. \end{align*} \end{lem} For the first term ${\bf B}^{(2x,1)}_{n_0,n_1}$, the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality implies \begin{align*} & \quad {\mathbb E} \| {\bf B}^{(2x,1)}_{n_0,n_1} \|^2 \\ & \le 2 {\mathbb E} \| B_2 \widetilde{\Gamma}_{n_0, n_1} {\hat{x}}_{n_0} \|^2 + 2 {\mathbb E} \left\| B_2 \ssum{l}{n_0}{n_1-1} \widetilde{\Gamma}_{l+1, n_1} (\beta_{l} H^\star B_3 {\hat{y}}_{l} - \tilde{R}^x_{l} ) \right\|^2 \\ & \le 2 (\| B_2 \| \|\widetilde{\Gamma}_{n_0, n_1} \|)^2 {\mathbb E} \| {\hat{x}}_{n_0} \|^2 + 2 \| B_2 \|^2 \left( \ssum{l}{n_0}{n_1-1} \beta_{l} \right) \! \left( \ssum{l}{n_0}{n_1-1} \beta_{l} \| \widetilde{\Gamma}_{l+1, n_1} \|^2 {\mathbb E} \left\| H^\star B_3 {\hat{y}}_{l} {-} \frac{\tilde{R}^x_{l}}{\beta_{l}} \right\|^2 \right). \end{align*} By Lemma~\ref{lem:slow:stepsize-aux}, when $n$ is sufficiently large, we $\| \widetilde{\Gamma}_{l+1,n_1} \| \le \frac{ 2^{ \left\lceil 2T/c_\alpha \right\rceil + 3} }{\mu_1} \frac{ \sqrt{\beta_{l}} }{ \alpha_{l} } $ for any $n_0 \le l < n_1$ and $\| \widetilde{\Gamma}_{n_0, n_1} \| \le \frac{ 2^{ \left\lceil 2T/c_\alpha \right\rceil + 3} }{\mu_1} \frac{ \sqrt{\beta}_{n_0} }{ \alpha_{n_0} } + \sqrt{\beta_{n_0}} $, with $\mu_1$ and $c_\alpha$ specified in Lemma~\ref{lem:slow:stepsize-aux}; Assumption~\ref{assump:mart-decouple-rate} implies ${\mathbb E} \| {\hat{x}}_{n_0} \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(\alpha_{n_0})$ and ${\mathbb E} \| {\hat{y}}_{l} \|^2 = {\mathcal O} (\beta_{l})$; the upper bounds in \eqref{eq:lem:check-twotime:Rx-upper} and the subsequent analysis therein imply that under Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime}, ${\mathbb E} \| \tilde{R}^x_{l} \|^2 = {\mathcal O}( \beta_{l}^2 \alpha_{l}^{1+{\delta_H}} + \beta_{l}^{2+{\delta_H}} + \alpha_{l}^{3+{\delta_F}} + \beta_{l}^2 \alpha_{l}^{1+{\delta_G}} ) = {\mathcal O}(\alpha_{l}^2 \beta_{l})$. Therefore, we have $\|\widetilde{\Gamma}_{n_0, n_1} \|^2 {\mathbb E} \| {\hat{x}}_{n_0} \|^2 = {\mathcal O} \left( \frac{\beta_{n_0} }{\alpha_{n_0}} \right) = o(1)$ and \begin{align*} \|\widetilde{\Gamma}_{l+1, n_1} \|^2 {\mathbb E} \left\| H^\star B_3 {\hat{y}}_{l} - \frac{ \tilde{R}^x_{l} }{\beta_{l}} \right\|^2 & = {\mathcal O} \left( \frac{\beta_{l}}{\alpha_{l}^2} \right) \left( {\mathbb E} \| {\hat{y}}_{l} \|^2 + \frac{ {\mathbb E} \| \tilde{R}^x_{l} \|^2 }{ \beta_{l}^2 } \right) = {\mathcal O}(1). \end{align*} Then similar to the derive of \eqref{eq:lem:tight-twotime:B1x}, there exist $K_6$ and $m_1$ such that \begin{align} {\mathbb E} \| {\bf B}^{(2x,1)}_{n_0,n_1} \|^2 \le K_6 (s-t)^2 \end{align} holds for any $n \ge m_1$. Modifying $K_6$, we could make \eqref{eq:lem:tight-slow:B2x-1} hold for any $n$. For the second term ${\bf B}^{(2x,2)}_{n_0,n_1}$, applying $\| \widetilde{\Gamma}_{l+1,n_1} \| \le C_T \frac{ \sqrt{\beta_{l}} }{ \alpha_{l} } $ with $C_T := \frac{ 2^{ \left\lceil 2T/c_\alpha \right\rceil + 3} }{\mu_1}$, we obtain that with $p \in \left(2, \frac{4}{1 + ( {\delta_H} \vee {\delta_F} \vee {\delta_G} )/2} \right]$ and sufficiently large $n$, \begin{align*} {\mathbb E} \| {\bf B}^{(2x,2)}_{n_0,n_1} \|^p & \overset{\eqref{eq:burk-jensen}}{\le} C^{ti}_p \left( n_1 - n_0 \right)^{\frac{p}{2}-1} \| B_2 \|^p \ssum{l}{ n_0 }{n_1-1 } \| \widetilde{\Gamma}_{l+1, n_1} \|^p \alpha_{l}^p {\mathbb E} \| \tilde{\xi}_{l} \|^p \\ & \le C^{ti}_p C_{T}^p \left( n_1 - n_0 \right)^{\frac{p}{2}-1} \| B_2 \|^p \ssum{l}{ n_0 }{n_1-1 } \beta_{l}^\frac{p}{2} {\mathbb E} \| \tilde{\xi}_{l} \|^p, \end{align*} where we have used Burkholder's inequality in Proposition~\ref{prop:burk} with $C^{ti}_p = \left[ (p-1) \vee \frac{1}{p-1} \right]^p$. Then following a similar procedure to \eqref{eq:lem:tight-twotime:xii}, we have that there exist $K_7$ and $m_2$ such that \begin{align} {\mathbb E} \| {\bf B}^{(2x,2)}_{n_0,n_1} \|^p \le K_7 (s-t)^\frac{p}{2} \end{align} for any $n \ge m_2$. Modifying $K_7$, we could make \eqref{eq:lem:tight-slow:B2x-2} hold for any $n$. The upper bounds in \eqref{eq:lem:tight-slow:Bdiff}, \eqref{eq:lem:tight-slow:B2x-1} and \eqref{eq:lem:tight-slow:B2x-2} collectively control the term ${\bf B}^{(2x,n)}_{t,s}$. Combining them with \eqref{eq:lem:tight-slow:BandPsi} and Markov's inequality yields the following upper bound \begin{align*} {\mathbb P} \left( \| {\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(s) - {\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(t) \| \ge {\varepsilon} \right) & \le {\mathbb P} \left( \| {\bf B}^{(3y,n)}_{t,s} \| \ge \frac{{\varepsilon}}{5} \right) + {\mathbb P} \left( \| \mbox{\boldmath$\Psi$\unboldmath}^{(n)}_{t,s} \| \ge \frac{{\varepsilon}}{5} \right) + {\mathbb P} \left( \| {\bf B}^{(2x,1)}_{n_0,n_1} \| \ge \frac{{\varepsilon}}{5} \right) \\ & \qquad + {\mathbb P} \left( \| {\bf B}^{(2x,2)}_{n_0,n_1} \| \ge \frac{{\varepsilon}}{5} \right) + {\mathbb P} \left( \| {\bf B}^{(2x,n)}_{t,s} - {\bf B}^{(2x)}_{n_0, n_1} \| \ge \frac{{\varepsilon}}{5} \right) \\ & \le \frac{25}{{\varepsilon}^2} \left( {\mathbb E} \| {\bf B}^{(3y,n)}_{t,s} \|^2 + {\mathbb E} \| {\bf B}^{(2x,1)}_{n_0,n_1} \|^2 + {\mathbb E} \| {\bf B}^{(2x,n)}_{t,s} - {\bf B}^{(2x)}_{n_0, n_1} \|^2 \right) \\ & \qquad + \frac{5^p}{{\varepsilon}^p} \left( {\mathbb E} \| \mbox{\boldmath$\Psi$\unboldmath}^{(n)}_{t,s} \|^p + {\mathbb E} \| {\bf B}^{(2x,2)}_{n_0,n_1} \|^p \right) \\ & \le 5^4 \left( \max_{3 \le i \le 7} K_i \right) \left[ \frac{ (s-t)^2 }{{\varepsilon}^2} + \frac{ (s-t)^\frac{p}{2} }{{\varepsilon}^p} \right]. \end{align*} This upper bound verifies the second condition in Proposition~\ref{prop:tight-suff-slow}, and hence $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(\cdot) \}_{n=1}^\infty$ is tight.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $\hat x_k$ recursively, bound via Lemma C.1, conclude tightness of $\bar Y_n$

nodes.name: Burkholder's inequality
nodes.statement: Fix any $p \ge 2$. Let $\{ X_k \}_{1 \le k \le n}$ be a finite ${\mathbb R}^d$-valued martingale difference sequence with $\sup_{1 \le k \le n} {\mathbb E} \| X_k \|^p < \infty$. Then we have \begin{align*} {\mathbb E} \left\| \ssum{k}{1}{n} X_k \right\|^p \le \left[ (p-1) \vee \frac{1}{p-1} \right]^p {\mathbb E} \left( \ssum{k}{1}{n} \| X_k \|^2 \right)^\frac{p}{2}, \end{align*} which together with Jensen's inequality imply \begin{align} {\mathbb E} \left\| \ssum{k}{1}{n} X_k \right\|^p \le \left[ (p-1) \vee \frac{1}{p-1} \right]^p n^{\frac{p}{2} - 1 } {\mathbb E} \ssum{k}{1}{n} \| X_k \|^p. \end{align}
assumptions: $\{ X_k \}_{1 \le k \le n}$ be a finite ${\mathbb R}^d$-valued martingale difference sequence with $\sup_{1 \le k \le n} {\mathbb E} \| X_k \|^p < \infty$
nodes.label: prop:burk

nodes.name: Burkholder-Jensen moment bound (52)
nodes.statement: {\mathbb E} \left\| \ssum{k}{1}{n} X_k \right\|^p \le \left[ (p-1) \vee \frac{1}{p-1} \right]^p n^{\frac{p}{2} - 1 } {\mathbb E} \ssum{k}{1}{n} \| X_k \|^p.
nodes.label: eq:burk-jensen

nodes.name: Auxiliary step-size product bound
nodes.statement: Suppose that Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime} holds and the real parts of the eigenvalues of $B_1$ are no less than $\mu_1$. Define $A_{k}:= {I} - \alpha_{k} B_1 + \beta_{k} H^\star B_2$. If $t$ and $s$ are fixed positive numbers satisfying $s>t$ and $n$ is sufficiently large, then for any $N^\beta(n,t) \le l < N^\beta(n, s)$, we have \begin{align*} \left\| \sum_{k=l+1}^{N^\beta(n,s)-1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \prod_{i=1}^{k-l-1} A_{k-i} \right\| \le \frac{ 2^{ \left\lceil 2s/c_\alpha \right\rceil + 3} }{\mu_1} \cdot \frac{ \sqrt{\beta_{l}} }{ \alpha_{l} }. \end{align*}
assumptions: the real parts of the eigenvalues of $B_1$ are no less than $\mu_1$
$t$ and $s$ are fixed positive numbers satisfying $s>t$ and $n$ is sufficiently large
nodes.label: lem:slow:stepsize-aux

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.1
nodes.statement: For ease of notation, we define $n_0 := N^\beta(n, t)$ and $n_1 := N^\beta(n, s)-1$. Since the real parts of the eigenvalues of $B_1$ are no less than $\mu_1$, $\beta_{j} = o(\alpha_{j})$ and $n$ is sufficiently large, we have $\| A_j \| \le \| {I} - \alpha_{j} B_1 \| + \beta_{j} \| H^\star B_2 \| \le 1 - \mu_1 \alpha_{j} / 2$ for any $j > l \ge n$. It follows that \begin{align*} \left\| \sum_{k=l+1}^{n_1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \prod_{i=1}^{k-l-1} A_{k-i} \right\| \le \sum_{k=l+1}^{n_1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \prod_{i=l+1}^{k-1} \left( 1 {-} \frac{ \mu_1 \alpha_{i} }{2} \right) \le \sum_{k=l+1}^{n_1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \exp \left( - \frac{\mu_1}{2} \sum_{i=l+1}^{k-1} \alpha_{i} \right). \end{align*} Moreover, by Lemma~\ref{lem:aux:bounded} and the monotonicity of the step sizes, we have $ \alpha_{k} \ge c_1 \alpha_{l} $ and $ \beta_{k} \le \beta_{l}$ for any $l \le k \le n_1$. Here $c_1 := 2^{ -\left\lceil 2s/c_\alpha \right\rceil - 1}$ with $c_\alpha$ specified in Lemma~\ref{lem:aux:bounded}. This implies \begin{align*} \sum_{k=l+1}^{n_1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \exp \left( - \frac{\mu_1}{2} \sum_{i=l+1}^{k-1} \alpha_{i} \right) & \le \sqrt{\beta_{l}} \sum_{k=l+1}^{n_1} \exp \left[ - (k-1-l) \frac{c_1 \mu_1 \alpha_{l} }{2} \right] \\ & \le \frac{ \sqrt{\beta}_{l} }{1 - \exp(- c_1 \mu_1 \alpha_{l} / 2) }. \end{align*} For $x \in (0,1)$, we have $\exp(-x) \le 1 - x/2$. Therefore, for sufficiently large $n$, we have \begin{align*} \left\| \sum_{k=l+1}^{n_1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \prod_{i=1}^{k-l-1} A_{k-i} \right\| \le \frac{4 }{ c_1 \mu_1 } \cdot \frac{ \sqrt{\beta_{l} } }{ \alpha_{l} } \end{align*} for any $n_0 \le l < n_1$. With $c_1 = 2^{ -\left\lceil 2s/c_\alpha \right\rceil - 1}$, the coefficient is $\frac{4}{c_1 \mu_1} = \frac{ 2^{ \left\lceil 2s/c_\alpha \right\rceil + 3} }{\mu_1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Contract $\|A_j\|\le1-\mu_1\alpha_j/2$, bound the product by an exponential, and sum a geometric series using Lemma B.1.

nodes.name: Contraction bound on $A_j$ and exponential bound on the prod

Since the real parts of the eigenvalues of $B_1$ are no less than $\mu_1$, $\beta_{j} = o(\alpha_{j})$ and $n$ is sufficiently large, we have $\| A_j \| \le \| {I} - \alpha_{j} B_1 \| + \beta_{j} \| H^\star B_2 \| \le 1 - \mu_1 \alpha_{j} / 2$ for any $j > l \ge n$. It follows that \begin{align*} \left\| \sum_{k=l+1}^{n_1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \prod_{i=1}^{k-l-1} A_{k-i} \right\| \le \sum_{k=l+1}^{n_1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \prod_{i=l+1}^{k-1} \left( 1 {-} \frac{ \mu_1 \alpha_{i} }{2} \right) \le \sum_{k=l+1}^{n_1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \exp \left( - \frac{\mu_1}{2} \sum_{i=l+1}^{k-1} \alpha_{i} \right). \end{align*}

Here $c_1 := 2^{ -\left\lceil 2s/c_\alpha \right\rceil - 1}$ with $c_\alpha$ specified in Lemma~\ref{lem:aux:bounded}. This implies \begin{align*} \sum_{k=l+1}^{n_1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \exp \left( - \frac{\mu_1}{2} \sum_{i=l+1}^{k-1} \alpha_{i} \right) & \le \sqrt{\beta_{l}} \sum_{k=l+1}^{n_1} \exp \left[ - (k-1-l) \frac{c_1 \mu_1 \alpha_{l} }{2} \right] \\ & \le \frac{ \sqrt{\beta}_{l} }{1 - \exp(- c_1 \mu_1 \alpha_{l} / 2) }. \end{align*}

Therefore, for sufficiently large $n$, we have \begin{align*} \left\| \sum_{k=l+1}^{n_1} \sqrt{\beta_{k}} \prod_{i=1}^{k-l-1} A_{k-i} \right\| \le \frac{4 }{ c_1 \mu_1 } \cdot \frac{ \sqrt{\beta_{l} } }{ \alpha_{l} } \end{align*} for any $n_0 \le l < n_1$.

nodes.name: Discrete generator approximation
nodes.statement: Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{assump:smooth} -- \ref{assump:stepsize-twotime}, \ref{assump:noise-fclt} and \ref{assump:mart-decouple-rate} hold. Then \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item For any $f \in C^2_c({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$, with ${\mathcal A}^x$ defined in \eqref{eq:generator-twotime:Lx}, we have \begin{align} {\mathbb E} [ f ({\check{x}}_{n+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{n}) | {\mathcal F}_{n} ] = \alpha_{n} {\mathcal A}^x f({\check{x}}_{n}) + R^f_{n}, \end{align} where $\frac{1}{\alpha_{n}} {\mathbb E} | R^f_{n} | \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. \item For any $g \in C^2_c({\mathbb R}^{d_y})$, with ${\mathcal A}^y$ defined in \eqref{eq:generator-twotime:Ly}, we have \begin{align} {\mathbb E} [ g ({\check{z}}_{n+1}) - g({\check{z}}_{n}) | {\mathcal F}_{n} ] = \beta_{n} {\mathcal A}^y g({\check{z}}_{n}) + R^g_{n}, \end{align} where $\frac{1}{\beta_{n}} {\mathbb E} | R^g_{n} | \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Conditional increments of $f(\check x_n)$ and $g(\check z_n)$ equal step size times the generator plus negligible residuals.
nodes.label: lem:generator-twotime

nodes.name: Discrete generator for the fast iterate (58)
nodes.statement: {\mathbb E} [ f ({\check{x}}_{n+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{n}) | {\mathcal F}_{n} ] = \alpha_{n} {\mathcal A}^x f({\check{x}}_{n}) + R^f_{n},
nodes.label: eq:generator-twotime:x

nodes.statement: {\mathbb E} [ g ({\check{z}}_{n+1}) - g({\check{z}}_{n}) | {\mathcal F}_{n} ] = \beta_{n} {\mathcal A}^y g({\check{z}}_{n}) + R^g_{n},

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.4
nodes.statement:
We first prove Part~(i). For convenience, with $\Gamma^\alpha_{n,m}$ introduced in Definition~ef{defn:time-inter}, we define the following notation  egin{align*}  ar{N}^\alpha(n, t) := \min \left\{ m \ge n \colon \Gamma^\alpha_{n, m} \ge t ight\}. \end{align*} Then the filtration defined in \eqref{eq:filtration-main} can be written succinctly as ${\mathcal F}^{ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n,t} = {\mathcal F}_{  ar{N}^\alpha(n, t) }$. We construct ${\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t)$ as  egin{align} {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t) = \ssum{k}{n}{ ar{N}^\alpha(n,t)-1}  ig\{ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) - {\mathbb E}[ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ]  ig\}. \end{align} Clearly, ${\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t)$ is adapted to the filtration $({\mathcal F}^{ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n,t})_{t \ge 0}$. Next we verify that ${\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t)$ is a martingale w.r.t. $({\mathcal F}^{ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n,t})_{t \ge 0}$. For any $t > s \ge 0$, if $k \le  ar{N}^\alpha(n,s)-1$, then ${\check{x}}_{k}, {\check{x}}_{k+1} \in {\mathcal F}^{ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n,s}$ and ${\mathcal F}_k \subset {\mathcal F}^{ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n,s}$, implying \[ {\mathbb E}  ig\{ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) {-} f({\check{x}}_{k}) {-} {\mathbb E}[ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) {-} f({\check{x}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ]  ig| {\mathcal F}^{ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n,s}  ig\} {=} f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) {-} f({\check{x}}_{k}) {-} {\mathbb E}[ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) {-} f({\check{x}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ]. \] Otherwise, $k \ge  ar{N}^\alpha(n,s) $ and ${\mathcal F}^{ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n,s} \subseteq {\mathcal F}_{k}$, implying \[ {\mathbb E}  ig\{ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) - {\mathbb E}[ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ]\,  ig|\, {\mathcal F}^{ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n,s}  ig\} = 0. \] Consequently,  egin{align*} {\mathbb E} [ {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t) | {\mathcal F}^{ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n,s} ] & = \ssum{k}{n}{ ar{N}^\alpha(n,t)-1} {\mathbb E}  ig\{ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) - {\mathbb E}[ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ]\,  ig|\, {\mathcal F}^{ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n,s}  ig\} \ & = \ssum{k}{n}{ ar{N}^\alpha(n,s)-1}  ig\{ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) - {\mathbb E}[ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ]  ig\} = {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(s), \end{align*} which implies that ${\mathcal M}_{n}^f (t)$ is a martingale w.r.t.\ ${\mathcal F}^{ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n,t}$. Now we focus on the residual term ${\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t)$. For notational simplicity, we define $\overline{t}^\alpha_{n} = \Gamma^\alpha_{n,  ar{N}^\alpha(n,t)} $. Then we have $\overline{t}^\alpha_{n} - \alpha_{ ar{N}^\alpha(n,t) - 1} < t \le \overline{t}^\alpha_{n}$. With this notation and $\underline{t}^\alpha_{n}$ introduced in Definition~ef{defn:time-inter}, ootnote{In the notation $\underline{t}^\alpha_{n}$, we view $t$ as a variable.} ${\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t)$ can be expressed as  egin{align} {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t) & = f( { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(t) ) - f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(0) ) - \int_0^t {\mathcal A}^x f( { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) )\, \mathrm{d} s - {\mathcal M}_{n} ^f(t) 
onumber \ & \overset{\eqref{eq:Mnf-def}}{=} f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)) - f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}) ) - \int_0^t {\mathcal A}^x f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) \,\mathrm{d} s + \ssum{k}{n}{ ar{N}^\alpha(n,t)-1} {\mathbb E} [ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ] 
onumber \ & \overset{\eqref{eq:generator-twotime:x}}{=} f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)) - f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}) ) - \int_0^t {\mathcal A}^x f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) \,\mathrm{d} s + \ssum{k}{n}{ ar{N}^\alpha(n,t)-1} \left( \alpha_{k} {\mathcal A}^x f({\check{x}}_{k}) + R^f_k ight) 
onumber \ & \overset{(a)}{=} f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)) - f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}) ) + \int_0^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} \left( {\mathcal A}^x f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(\underline{s}^\alpha_{n}) ) - {\mathcal A}^x f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) ight) \,\mathrm{d} s 
onumber \ & \qquad + \int_t^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} {\mathcal A}^x f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) \,\mathrm{d} s + \ssum{k}{n}{ ar{N}^\alpha(n,t) - 1} R^f_k, \end{align} where for step (a), we used Fact~ef{fact2}~ef{fact2-3} such that $\alpha_{k} {\mathcal A}^x f({\check{x}}_{k}) = \int_{\Gamma^\alpha_{n,k}}^{\Gamma^\alpha_{n,k+1}} {\mathcal A}^x f( { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_n ) ) \,\mathrm{d} s $. Notice that $f \in C_c^2({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$. For a fixed $t$, to control ${\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t)$ in the $L_1$ sense, we need to control the following $L_1$ distances ${\mathbb E} \| { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \| $ and ${\mathbb E} \| { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}( \overline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \|$ for any $s \in [0,\overline{t}_{n}^\alpha]$. From the definition of ${ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ in \eqref{eq:def:xbar}, we have ${ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) = {\check{x}}_{N^\alpha(n,s)}$. Consequently,  egin{align*} { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) = (s - \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \left(- B_1 {\check{x}}_{N^\alpha(n,s) } +  rac{R^x_{N^\alpha (n,s)} }{ \alpha_{N^\alpha (n,s)} } ight) -  rac{s - \underline{s}^\alpha_{n}}{ \sqrt{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)} } } 	ilde{\xi}_{N^\alpha(n,s)}. \end{align*} It follows that for each $s \in [0, \overline{t}_{n}^\alpha] $, the following results hold  egin{align*} {\mathbb E} \| { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \| & \le (s - \underline{t}^\alpha_{n} ) {\mathbb E} \left\| - B_1 {\check{x}}_{N^\alpha(n,s) } +  rac{R^x_{N^\alpha (n,s)} }{ \alpha_{N^\alpha (n,s)} } ight\| +  rac{s - \underline{s}^\alpha_{n}}{ \sqrt{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)} } } {\mathbb E} \| 	ilde{\xi}_{N^\alpha(n,s)} \| \ & \overset{\eqref{eq:lem:tight-twotime:l2bound-x}}{\lesssim} (s - \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) + \sqrt{s - { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \| + {\mathbb E} \| { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}( \overline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) - { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \| \ & \le {\mathbb E} \| { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \| + ( \overline{s}^\alpha_{n} - \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) {\mathbb E} \left\| - B_1 {\check{x}}_{N^\alpha(n,s) } +  rac{R^x_{N^\alpha (n,s)} }{ \alpha_{N^\alpha (n,s)} } ight\| \ & \qquad +  rac{ \overline{s}^\alpha_{n} - \underline{s}^\alpha_{n}}{ \sqrt{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)} } } {\mathbb E} \| 	ilde{\xi}_{N^\alpha(n,s)} \| \ & \lesssim \sqrt{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)} }. \end{align*} Since $f \in C_c^2({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$, it follows that  egin{align}  egin{split} {\mathbb E} | f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)) - f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}^{(n)}_{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}}) | & \lesssim {\mathbb E} \| { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(t) - { ar{	extnormal{X}}}^{(n)}_{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n} } \| \lesssim \sqrt{\alpha_{N^\alpha(n,t)}} = o(1), \ {\mathbb E} \left| \int_t^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} {\mathcal A}^x f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) \,\mathrm{d} s ight| & \lesssim \int_t^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} 1 \,\mathrm{d} s = o(1), \ {\mathbb E} \left| \int_0^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} \left( {\mathcal A}^x f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n} (\underline{s}^\alpha_{n}) ) - {\mathcal A}^x f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) ight) \,\mathrm{d} s ight| & \lesssim \int_0^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} {\mathbb E} \| { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n} (\underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \| \,\mathrm{d} s \ & \lesssim \int_0^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} \sqrt{\alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)} } ds \lesssim \sqrt{\alpha_{n}} = o(1). \end{split} \end{align} Moreover, for a fixed $t$, Lemma~ef{lem:generator-twotime} implies  egin{align} {\mathbb E} \left| \ssum{k}{n}{ ar{N}^\alpha(n,t) -
