nodes.statement_short: Build $\mathcal M^f_n$ from martingale differences of $f(\check x_k)$ and show the residual vanishes in $L_1$ using Lemma C.2 and interpolation error bounds.

nodes.name: Define $\bar N^\alpha$ and rewrite the filtration
nodes.statement: We first prove Part~(i). For convenience, with $\Gamma^\alpha_{n,m}$ introduced in Definition~\ref{defn:time-inter}, we define the following notation \begin{align*} \bar{N}^\alpha(n, t) := \min \left\{ m \ge n \colon \Gamma^\alpha_{n, m} \ge t \right\}. \end{align*} Then the filtration defined in \eqref{eq:filtration-main} can be written succinctly as ${\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,t} = {\mathcal F}_{ \bar{N}^\alpha(n, t) }$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $\bar N^\alpha$ and rewrite the filtration

nodes.name: Construct the martingale part $\mathcal M^f_n$
nodes.statement: We construct ${\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t)$ as \begin{align} {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t) = \ssum{k}{n}{\bar{N}^\alpha(n,t)-1} \big\{ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) - {\mathbb E}[ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ] \big\}. \end{align} Clearly, ${\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t)$ is adapted to the filtration $({\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,t})_{t \ge 0}$.
nodes.statement_short: Construct the martingale part $\mathcal M^f_n$

nodes.name: Verify martingale property by cases on $k$
nodes.statement: Next we verify that ${\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t)$ is a martingale w.r.t. $({\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,t})_{t \ge 0}$. For any $t > s \ge 0$, if $k \le \bar{N}^\alpha(n,s)-1$, then ${\check{x}}_{k}, {\check{x}}_{k+1} \in {\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,s}$ and ${\mathcal F}_k \subset {\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,s}$, implying \[ {\mathbb E} \big\{ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) {-} f({\check{x}}_{k}) {-} {\mathbb E}[ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) {-} f({\check{x}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ] \big| {\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,s} \big\} {=} f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) {-} f({\check{x}}_{k}) {-} {\mathbb E}[ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) {-} f({\check{x}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ]. \] Otherwise, $k \ge \bar{N}^\alpha(n,s) $ and ${\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,s} \subseteq {\mathcal F}_{k}$, implying \[ {\mathbb E} \big\{ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) - {\mathbb E}[ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ]\, \big|\, {\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,s} \big\} = 0. \] Consequently, \begin{align*} {\mathbb E} [ {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t) | {\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,s} ] & = \ssum{k}{n}{\bar{N}^\alpha(n,t)-1} {\mathbb E} \big\{ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) - {\mathbb E}[ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ]\, \big|\, {\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,s} \big\} \\ & = \ssum{k}{n}{\bar{N}^\alpha(n,s)-1} \big\{ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) - {\mathbb E}[ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ] \big\} = {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(s), \end{align*} which implies that ${\mathcal M}_{n}^f (t)$ is a martingale w.r.t.\ ${\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,t}$.
nodes.statement_short: Verify martingale property by cases on $k$

nodes.name: Express the residual via Lemma C.2
nodes.statement:
Now we focus on the residual term ${\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t)$. For notational simplicity, we define $\overline{t}^\alpha_{n} = \Gamma^\alpha_{n,  ar{N}^\alpha(n,t)} $. Then we have $\overline{t}^\alpha_{n} - \alpha_{ ar{N}^\alpha(n,t) - 1} < t \le \overline{t}^\alpha_{n}$. With this notation and $\underline{t}^\alpha_{n}$ introduced in Definition~ef{defn:time-inter}, ootnote{In the notation $\underline{t}^\alpha_{n}$, we view $t$ as a variable.} ${\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t)$ can be expressed as  egin{align} {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t) & = f( { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(t) ) - f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(0) ) - \int_0^t {\mathcal A}^x f( { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) )\, \mathrm{d} s - {\mathcal M}_{n} ^f(t) 
onumber \ & \overset{\eqref{eq:Mnf-def}}{=} f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)) - f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}) ) - \int_0^t {\mathcal A}^x f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) \,\mathrm{d} s + \ssum{k}{n}{ ar{N}^\alpha(n,t)-1} {\mathbb E} [ f({\check{x}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{x}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ] 
onumber \ & \overset{\eqref{eq:generator-twotime:x}}{=} f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)) - f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}) ) - \int_0^t {\mathcal A}^x f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) \,\mathrm{d} s + \ssum{k}{n}{ ar{N}^\alpha(n,t)-1} \left( \alpha_{k} {\mathcal A}^x f({\check{x}}_{k}) + R^f_k ight) 
onumber \ & \overset{(a)}{=} f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)) - f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}) ) + \int_0^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} \left( {\mathcal A}^x f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(\underline{s}^\alpha_{n}) ) - {\mathcal A}^x f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) ight) \,\mathrm{d} s 
onumber \ & \qquad + \int_t^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} {\mathcal A}^x f({ ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) \,\mathrm{d} s + \ssum{k}{n}{ ar{N}^\alpha(n,t) - 1} R^f_k, \end{align} where for step (a), we used Fact~ef{fact2}~ef{fact2-3} such that $\alpha_{k} {\mathcal A}^x f({\check{x}}_{k}) = \int_{\Gamma^\alpha_{n,k}}^{\Gamma^\alpha_{n,k+1}} {\mathcal A}^x f( { ar{	extnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_n ) ) \,\mathrm{d} s $.
nodes.statement_short: Express the residual via Lemma C.2

nodes.name: Bound interpolation errors by $\sqrt{\alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)}}
nodes.statement: Notice that $f \in C_c^2({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$. For a fixed $t$, to control ${\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t)$ in the $L_1$ sense, we need to control the following $L_1$ distances ${\mathbb E} \| {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \| $ and ${\mathbb E} \| {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}( \overline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \|$ for any $s \in [0,\overline{t}_{n}^\alpha]$. From the definition of ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ in \eqref{eq:def:xbar}, we have ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) = {\check{x}}_{N^\alpha(n,s)}$. Consequently, \begin{align*} {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) = (s - \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \left(- B_1 {\check{x}}_{N^\alpha(n,s) } + \frac{R^x_{N^\alpha (n,s)} }{ \alpha_{N^\alpha (n,s)} } \right) - \frac{s - \underline{s}^\alpha_{n}}{ \sqrt{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)} } } \tilde{\xi}_{N^\alpha(n,s)}. \end{align*} It follows that for each $s \in [0, \overline{t}_{n}^\alpha] $, the following results hold \begin{align*} {\mathbb E} \| {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \| & \le (s - \underline{t}^\alpha_{n} ) {\mathbb E} \left\| - B_1 {\check{x}}_{N^\alpha(n,s) } + \frac{R^x_{N^\alpha (n,s)} }{ \alpha_{N^\alpha (n,s)} } \right\| + \frac{s - \underline{s}^\alpha_{n}}{ \sqrt{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)} } } {\mathbb E} \| \tilde{\xi}_{N^\alpha(n,s)} \| \\ & \overset{\eqref{eq:lem:tight-twotime:l2bound-x}}{\lesssim} (s - \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) + \sqrt{s - \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} } \lesssim \sqrt{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)} }, \\ {\mathbb E} \| {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}( \overline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \| & \le {\mathbb E} \| {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \| + {\mathbb E} \| {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}( \overline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \| \\ & \le {\mathbb E} \| {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}( \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \| + ( \overline{s}^\alpha_{n} - \underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) {\mathbb E} \left\| - B_1 {\check{x}}_{N^\alpha(n,s) } + \frac{R^x_{N^\alpha (n,s)} }{ \alpha_{N^\alpha (n,s)} } \right\| \\ & \qquad + \frac{ \overline{s}^\alpha_{n} - \underline{s}^\alpha_{n}}{ \sqrt{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)} } } {\mathbb E} \| \tilde{\xi}_{N^\alpha(n,s)} \| \\ & \lesssim \sqrt{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)} }. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound interpolation errors by $\sqrt{\alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)}}$

nodes.name: Residual vanishes in $L_1$
nodes.statement: Since $f \in C_c^2({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$, it follows that \begin{align} \begin{split} {\mathbb E} | f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)) - f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}^{(n)}_{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}}) | & \lesssim {\mathbb E} \| {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}^{(n)}_{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n} } \| \lesssim \sqrt{\alpha_{N^\alpha(n,t)}} = o(1), \\ {\mathbb E} \left| \int_t^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} {\mathcal A}^x f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) \,\mathrm{d} s \right| & \lesssim \int_t^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} 1 \,\mathrm{d} s = o(1), \\ {\mathbb E} \left| \int_0^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} \left( {\mathcal A}^x f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n} (\underline{s}^\alpha_{n}) ) - {\mathcal A}^x f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) \right) \,\mathrm{d} s \right| & \lesssim \int_0^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} {\mathbb E} \| {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n} (\underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \| \,\mathrm{d} s \\ & \lesssim \int_0^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} \sqrt{\alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)} } ds \lesssim \sqrt{\alpha_{n}} = o(1). \end{split} \end{align} Moreover, for a fixed $t$, Lemma~\ref{lem:generator-twotime} implies \begin{align} {\mathbb E} \left| \ssum{k}{n}{\bar{N}^\alpha(n,t) - 1} R^f_k \right| \le \ssum{k}{n}{\bar{N}^\alpha(n,t) - 1} \alpha_{k} {\mathbb E} \left| \frac{R^f_k}{\alpha_{k}} \right| \le \sup_{k' \ge n} {\mathbb E} \left| \frac{R^f_{k'}}{\alpha_{k'}} \right| \cdot \ssum{k}{n}{\bar{N}^\alpha(n,t) - 1} \alpha_{k} \lesssim o(1). \end{align} Plugging \eqref{eq:thm:fclt-twotime:res1} and \eqref{eq:thm:fclt-twotime:res2} into \eqref{eq:them:fclt-twotime:res} yields that for a fixe $t$, ${\mathbb E} | {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t) | \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Residual vanishes in $L_1$

nodes.name: Part (ii) analogously
nodes.statement: For Part~(ii), we similarly define \begin{align*} \bar{N}^\beta(n, t) := \min \left\{ m \ge n \colon \Gamma^\beta_{n, m} \ge t \right\} \end{align*} and \begin{align*} {\mathcal M}_{n}^g(t) = \ssum{k}{n}{\bar{N}^\beta(n,t)-1} \big\{ f({\check{z}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{z}}_{k}) - {\mathbb E}[ f({\check{z}}_{k+1}) - f({\check{z}}_{k}) | {\mathcal F}_{k} ] \big\}. \end{align*} The remaining proof is similar to that of Part~(i).
nodes.statement_short: Part (ii) analogously

nodes.name: Geometric ergodicity for SDEs
nodes.statement: Under Assumption~\ref{assump:hurwitz}, the SDE in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} has a unique invariant distribution $\pi^\star$. Moreover, suppose ${\textnormal{X}}(t)$ is a solution, for any compact set $K \subset {\mathbb R}^{d_x}$ and function $f \in C_c^2({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$. Then there exist positive numbers $A$ and $b$ such that \begin{align*} \sup_{x \in K} | {\mathbb E}[ f({\textnormal{X}}(t)) | X(0) = x ] - {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star} f({\textnormal{X}}) | \le A e^{-bt}, \ \forall t \ge 0. \end{align*} Similar results also hold for the SDE in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}.
conclusions: the SDE in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} has a unique invariant distribution $\pi^\star$
nodes.label: prop:ergo

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.1 (i)
nodes.statement: The proof is divided into three steps. In the first step, we apply Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx} to establish the convergence of convergent subsequences. In the second step, we verify Condition~\ref{prop:final:condition:initial} in Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx}. Finally, we apply Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx} to establish the convergence of the whole sequence. \vspace{0.2cm} \textbf{Step~1: establishing subsequence convergence}. For the conditions in Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx}, Condition~\ref{prop:final:condition:unique} has been discussed in Section~\ref{sec:fclt:prelim:mart}. Lemma~\ref{lem:tight-twotime} ensures that Condition~\ref{prop:final:condition:tight} holds. To verify Condition~\ref{prop:final:condition:mart-prob}, we apply Lemma~\ref{lem:mart-prob-twotime}, which shows that for any $f \in C^2_c({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$ and $t \ge 0$, one has that \begin{align*} f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)) - f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(0)) - \int_0^{t} {\mathcal A}^x f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) ds = {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t) + {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t), \end{align*} where for each $n$, ${\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t)$ is a martingale w.r.t.\ $({\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,t})_{t \ge 0}$ defined in \eqref{eq:filtration-main} and for each $t$, ${\mathbb E} | {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t) | \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. Then for any $k \ge 0$, $0 \le t_1 < t_2 < \dots < t_k \le t \le t+s $, and $f, h_1, h_2, \dots, h_k \in C_c^2({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$ \begin{align*} & \quad \ \Bigg|\, {\mathbb E} \bigg[ \Big( f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t+s)) - f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)) - \int_t^{t+s} {\mathcal A}^x f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(r)) dr \Big) \prod_{i=1}^k h_i({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t_i)) \bigg]\, \Bigg| \\ & = \Bigg|\, {\mathbb E} \bigg[ \big({\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t+s) - {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t) + {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t+s) - {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t) \big) \prod_{i=1}^k h_i({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t_i)) \bigg] \, \Bigg| \\ & = \Bigg|\, {\mathbb E} \bigg\{ \prod_{i=1}^k h_i({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t_i))\, {\mathbb E} \big[ {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t+s) - {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t) + {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t+s) - {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t) \,\big|\, {\mathcal F}_{n,t}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}} \big] \bigg\} \, \Bigg| \\ & \le {\mathbb E} \bigg\{ \prod_{i=1}^k | h_i({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t_i)) | \, {\mathbb E} \big[ | {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t+s) | + | {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t) | \,\big|\, {\mathcal F}_{n,t}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}} \big] \bigg\} \to 0 \end{align*} as $n \to \infty$. Now we assume $ \{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n_k} (\cdot) \}_{k=1}^\infty $ is a weakly convergent subsequence of $ \{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n} (\cdot) \}_{n=1}^\infty$. Clearly, this subsequence satisfies Condition~\ref{prop:final:condition:initial} in Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx}. Suppose ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n_k} (0) \Rightarrow \tilde{\pi}$. Then Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx} ensures that ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n_k}(\cdot) \Rightarrow {\textnormal{X}}^{\tilde{\pi}}(\cdot)$ as $k \to \infty$, where ${\textnormal{X}}^{\tilde{\pi}}(\cdot)$ is the solution of the SDE in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde} with the initial distribution $\tilde\pi$. \vspace{0.2cm} \textbf{Step~2: verifying initial conditions}. To establish the convergence of ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(0)$, it suffices to prove that all the convergent subsequences have the same limit. In fact, this limit is $\pi^\star$, the unique invariant distribution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}. The uniqueness is guaranteed by Proposition~\ref{prop:ergo}. In the next, we prove that if the subsequence ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n_k}(0) \Rightarrow \tilde{\pi}$, one must have $\tilde{\pi} = \pi^\star$. The proof is divided to the following two parts: (i) for any fixed $T > 0$, we show that there exists a solution ${\textnormal{X}}(t)$ to \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} such that $\tilde{\pi}$ has the same distribution as ${\textnormal{X}}(T)$; (ii) when $T$ is sufficiently large, the geometric ergodicity implies that the distribution of ${\textnormal{X}}(T)$ can be arbitrarily close to $\pi^\star$. \textbf{Part (i)}. We first introduce some additional notation. Recall that $\Gamma^\alpha_{n,n'} = \ssum{k}{n}{n'-1} \alpha_k$. For $n \in {\mathbb N}$ and $t \ge 0$, we define \begin{align*} M^\alpha (n,t) := \min\left\{ m \ge 0 \colon \Gamma^\alpha_{m,n} \le t \right\}\ \text{ and } \ \tilde{t}^\alpha_{n} := \Gamma^\alpha_{M^\alpha(n,t), n}. \end{align*} Since $\alpha_{n} \to 0$, we have $\tilde{t}^\alpha_{n} \uparrow t$. For a fixed $T>0$, we consider the subsequence $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(\cdot) \}_{k=0}^\infty$, which satisfies \begin{align*} {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(0) = {\check{x}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)} \ \text{ and }\ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}( \widetilde{T}^\alpha_{n_k})= {\check{x}}_{n_k}, \end{align*} where $\widetilde{T}^\alpha_{n} := \Gamma^\alpha_{M^\alpha(n,T), n}$ By Lemma~\ref{lem:tight-twotime}, $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t) \}_{n=1}^\infty$ is tight. Then Prokhorov's theorem (i.e., Proposition~\ref{prop:tight}~\ref{prop:tight:prok}) implies that the subsequence $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(\cdot) \}_{k=0}^\infty$ further has a weakly convergent subsequence. Without loss of generality, we assume the subsequence $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(\cdot) \}_{k=0}^\infty$ itself weakly converges. Then its initial distribution sequence also converges weakly, i.e., ${\check{x}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)} \Rightarrow \mu_T$ for some distribution $\mu_T$. Then by Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx}, ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(\cdot) \Rightarrow {\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_T}(\cdot) $, where ${\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_T}(\cdot)$ is a solution to \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde} with initial distribution $\mu_T$. Consequently, we also have ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(T) \Rightarrow {\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_T}(T)$. Moreover, recall that we have verified the second condition of Proposition~\ref{prop:tight-suff-slow} in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:tight-twotime}. Then $|T - \widetilde{T}^\alpha_{n_k}| \to 0$ implies that $\left\| {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(\widetilde{T}^\alpha_{n_k}) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(T) \right\| \overset{p}{\rightarrow} 0$ as $k \to \infty$. By Slutsky's theorem, ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(\widetilde{T}^\alpha_{n_k}) \Rightarrow {\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_T}(T)$, i.e., ${\check{x}}_{n_k} \Rightarrow {\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_T}(T)$. Since ${\check{x}}_{n_k} \Rightarrow \tilde\pi$, this implies that for any $T > 0$, ${\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_T}(T) \sim \tilde{\pi}$. \vspace{0.1cm} \textbf{Part (ii)}. Next, we apply ${\check{x}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)} \Rightarrow \mu_T$ and ${\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_T}(T) \sim \tilde{\pi}$ to prove $\tilde\pi = \pi^\star $. Since $\{ {\check{x}}_{n} \}_{n=1}^\infty$ is tight, for any ${\varepsilon} > 0$, there exists a compact set $K_{\varepsilon} \subset {\mathbb R}^{d_x}$ only depending on ${\varepsilon}$ such that $\sup_{n \ge 0} {\mathbb P}({\check{x}}_{n} \in K_{\varepsilon}) \ge 1 - {\varepsilon}$. It follows that $\mu_T(K_{\varepsilon}) \ge 1-{\varepsilon}$ for any $T > 0$. Moreover, Proposition~\ref{prop:ergo} implies that for a fixed $g \in C_c^2({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$, we can find $T_{\varepsilon}$ such that \begin{equation} \sup_{{x} \in K_{\varepsilon}} \left| {\mathcal P}_{T_{\varepsilon}}\, g({x})- {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star}\, g({\textnormal{X}}) \right| \le {\varepsilon}, \end{equation} where ${\mathcal P}_t$ represents a semigroup induced by the SDE in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}, that is, \begin{align} {\mathcal P}_t f(x) = {\mathbb E} [ f({\textnormal{X}}(t)) \,|\, {\textnormal{X}}(0) = x ], \end{align} where ${\textnormal{X}}(\cdot)$ is the solution to the SDE in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}. Setting $T = T_{\varepsilon}$, we have ${\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}}(T_{\varepsilon}) \sim \tilde{\pi}$. Since ${\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}}(\cdot)$ is a solution to \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} with initial distribution $\mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}$, we have \begin{align*} {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \tilde\pi}\, g({\textnormal{X}}) = {\mathbb E}\, [ g ({\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}}(T_{\varepsilon}) ) \,|\, {\textnormal{X}}(0) \sim \mu_{T_{\varepsilon}} ] \overset{\eqref{eq:semigroup}}{=} \int_{{\mathbb R}^{d_x}} {\mathcal P}_{T_{\varepsilon}}\, g({x}) d \mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}({x}) \end{align*} It follows that \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \left| {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \tilde\pi}\, g({\textnormal{X}}) - {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star}\, g({\textnormal{X}}) \right| & \le \int_{{\mathbb R}^{d_x}} \left| {\mathcal P}_{T_{\varepsilon}} g({x}) -{\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star} g({\textnormal{X}}) \right| d \mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}({x})\\ & = \int_{K_{\varepsilon}} \left| {\mathcal P}_{T_{\varepsilon}} g({x}) - {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star} g({\textnormal{X}}) \right| d \mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}({x}) \\ & \qquad + \int_{K_{\varepsilon}^c} \left| {\mathcal P}_{T_{\varepsilon}} g({x}) - {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star} g({\textnormal{X}}) \right| d \mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}({x}) \\ &\le \int_{K_{\varepsilon}} \left| {\mathcal P}_{T_{\varepsilon}} g({x}) - {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star} g({\textnormal{X}}) \right| d \mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}({x}) + 2 \|g\|_\infty \mu_{T_{\varepsilon}} (K_{\varepsilon}^c) \\ & \overset{(a)}{\le} {\varepsilon} + 2\|g\|_\infty {\varepsilon}, \end{aligned} \end{equation*} where (a) is due to $\mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}(K_{\varepsilon}) \ge 1-{\varepsilon}$ and \eqref{eq:erg_diff}. Letting ${\varepsilon} \to \infty$, we obtain ${\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \tilde\pi}\, g({\textnormal{X}}) = {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star}\, g({\textnormal{X}}) $. For any $g \in C_c^2({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$, we can repeat the above procedure, implying $\tilde\pi = \pi^\star$. \vspace{0.2cm} \textbf{Step~3: concluding whole sequence convergence}. This step is straightforward. In Steps~1 and 2, we have verified the all the conditions in Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx}. Moreover, ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(0) \Rightarrow \pi^\star$, the invariant distribution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde}. Consequently, ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ converges weakly to the solution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} with the initial distribution $\pi^\star$, implying that this solution is a stationary process. Since $B_1$ is a Hurwitz matrix, the invariant distribution $\pi^\star={\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_{x})$ with $\Sigma_x$ satisfying the equation in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-var} \cite[Section~6.5]{risken1996fokker}.
nodes.statement_short: Martingale-problem approach: Prop. 5.2 gives subsequential convergence; ergodicity forces the initial law to be $\pi^\star$; conclude for the whole sequence. Key step: identify subsequential limits of $\check x_n$ as $X^{\mu_T}(T)$ for every $T$.

nodes.name: Three-step plan
nodes.statement: The proof is divided into three steps. In the first step, we apply Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx} to establish the convergence of convergent subsequences. In the second step, we verify Condition~\ref{prop:final:condition:initial} in Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx}. Finally, we apply Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx} to establish the convergence of the whole sequence.
nodes.statement_short: Three-step plan

nodes.name: Step 1: verify Prop. 5.2 conditions via Lemmas 5.3, 5.4
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step~1: establishing subsequence convergence}. For the conditions in Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx}, Condition~\ref{prop:final:condition:unique} has been discussed in Section~\ref{sec:fclt:prelim:mart}. Lemma~\ref{lem:tight-twotime} ensures that Condition~\ref{prop:final:condition:tight} holds. To verify Condition~\ref{prop:final:condition:mart-prob}, we apply Lemma~\ref{lem:mart-prob-twotime}, which shows that for any $f \in C^2_c({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$ and $t \ge 0$, one has that \begin{align*} f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)) - f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(0)) - \int_0^{t} {\mathcal A}^x f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) ds = {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t) + {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t), \end{align*} where for each $n$, ${\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t)$ is a martingale w.r.t.\ $({\mathcal F}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n,t})_{t \ge 0}$ defined in \eqref{eq:filtration-main} and for each $t$, ${\mathbb E} | {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t) | \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. Then for any $k \ge 0$, $0 \le t_1 < t_2 < \dots < t_k \le t \le t+s $, and $f, h_1, h_2, \dots, h_k \in C_c^2({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$ \begin{align*} & \quad \ \Bigg|\, {\mathbb E} \bigg[ \Big( f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t+s)) - f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)) - \int_t^{t+s} {\mathcal A}^x f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(r)) dr \Big) \prod_{i=1}^k h_i({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t_i)) \bigg]\, \Bigg| \\ & = \Bigg|\, {\mathbb E} \bigg[ \big({\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t+s) - {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t) + {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t+s) - {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t) \big) \prod_{i=1}^k h_i({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t_i)) \bigg] \, \Bigg| \\ & = \Bigg|\, {\mathbb E} \bigg\{ \prod_{i=1}^k h_i({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t_i))\, {\mathbb E} \big[ {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t+s) - {\mathcal M}_{n}^f(t) + {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t+s) - {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t) \,\big|\, {\mathcal F}_{n,t}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}} \big] \bigg\} \, \Bigg| \\ & \le {\mathbb E} \bigg\{ \prod_{i=1}^k | h_i({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t_i)) | \, {\mathbb E} \big[ | {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t+s) | + | {\mathcal R}_{n}^f(t) | \,\big|\, {\mathcal F}_{n,t}^{\bar{\textnormal{X}}} \big] \bigg\} \to 0 \end{align*} as $n \to \infty$. Now we assume $ \{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n_k} (\cdot) \}_{k=1}^\infty $ is a weakly convergent subsequence of $ \{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n} (\cdot) \}_{n=1}^\infty$. Clearly, this subsequence satisfies Condition~\ref{prop:final:condition:initial} in Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx}. Suppose ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n_k} (0) \Rightarrow \tilde{\pi}$. Then Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx} ensures that ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n_k}(\cdot) \Rightarrow {\textnormal{X}}^{\tilde{\pi}}(\cdot)$ as $k \to \infty$, where ${\textnormal{X}}^{\tilde{\pi}}(\cdot)$ is the solution of the SDE in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde} with the initial distribution $\tilde\pi$.
nodes.statement_short: Step 1: verify Prop. 5.2 conditions via Lemmas 5.3, 5.4; subsequences converge

nodes.name: Step 2: every subsequential initial limit equals $\pi^\star$
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step~2: verifying initial conditions}. To establish the convergence of ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(0)$, it suffices to prove that all the convergent subsequences have the same limit. In fact, this limit is $\pi^\star$, the unique invariant distribution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}. The uniqueness is guaranteed by Proposition~\ref{prop:ergo}. In the next, we prove that if the subsequence ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n_k}(0) \Rightarrow \tilde{\pi}$, one must have $\tilde{\pi} = \pi^\star$. The proof is divided to the following two parts: (i) for any fixed $T > 0$, we show that there exists a solution ${\textnormal{X}}(t)$ to \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} such that $\tilde{\pi}$ has the same distribution as ${\textnormal{X}}(T)$; (ii) when $T$ is sufficiently large, the geometric ergodicity implies that the distribution of ${\textnormal{X}}(T)$ can be arbitrarily close to $\pi^\star$. \textbf{Part (i)}. We first introduce some additional notation. Recall that $\Gamma^\alpha_{n,n'} = \ssum{k}{n}{n'-1} \alpha_k$. For $n \in {\mathbb N}$ and $t \ge 0$, we define \begin{align*} M^\alpha (n,t) := \min\left\{ m \ge 0 \colon \Gamma^\alpha_{m,n} \le t \right\}\ \text{ and } \ \tilde{t}^\alpha_{n} := \Gamma^\alpha_{M^\alpha(n,t), n}. \end{align*} Since $\alpha_{n} \to 0$, we have $\tilde{t}^\alpha_{n} \uparrow t$. For a fixed $T>0$, we consider the subsequence $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(\cdot) \}_{k=0}^\infty$, which satisfies \begin{align*} {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(0) = {\check{x}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)} \ \text{ and }\ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}( \widetilde{T}^\alpha_{n_k})= {\check{x}}_{n_k}, \end{align*} where $\widetilde{T}^\alpha_{n} := \Gamma^\alpha_{M^\alpha(n,T), n}$ By Lemma~\ref{lem:tight-twotime}, $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t) \}_{n=1}^\infty$ is tight. Then Prokhorov's theorem (i.e., Proposition~\ref{prop:tight}~\ref{prop:tight:prok}) implies that the subsequence $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(\cdot) \}_{k=0}^\infty$ further has a weakly convergent subsequence. Without loss of generality, we assume the subsequence $\{ {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(\cdot) \}_{k=0}^\infty$ itself weakly converges. Then its initial distribution sequence also converges weakly, i.e., ${\check{x}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)} \Rightarrow \mu_T$ for some distribution $\mu_T$. Then by Proposition~\ref{prop:mart-prob-approx}, ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(\cdot) \Rightarrow {\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_T}(\cdot) $, where ${\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_T}(\cdot)$ is a solution to \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde} with initial distribution $\mu_T$. Consequently, we also have ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(T) \Rightarrow {\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_T}(T)$. Moreover, recall that we have verified the second condition of Proposition~\ref{prop:tight-suff-slow} in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:tight-twotime}. Then $|T - \widetilde{T}^\alpha_{n_k}| \to 0$ implies that $\left\| {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(\widetilde{T}^\alpha_{n_k}) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(T) \right\| \overset{p}{\rightarrow} 0$ as $k \to \infty$. By Slutsky's theorem, ${\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)}(\widetilde{T}^\alpha_{n_k}) \Rightarrow {\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_T}(T)$, i.e., ${\check{x}}_{n_k} \Rightarrow {\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_T}(T)$. Since ${\check{x}}_{n_k} \Rightarrow \tilde\pi$, this implies that for any $T > 0$, ${\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_T}(T) \sim \tilde{\pi}$. \vspace{0.1cm} \textbf{Part (ii)}. Next, we apply ${\check{x}}_{M^\alpha(n_k, T)} \Rightarrow \mu_T$ and ${\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_T}(T) \sim \tilde{\pi}$ to prove $\tilde\pi = \pi^\star $. Since $\{ {\check{x}}_{n} \}_{n=1}^\infty$ is tight, for any ${\varepsilon} > 0$, there exists a compact set $K_{\varepsilon} \subset {\mathbb R}^{d_x}$ only depending on ${\varepsilon}$ such that $\sup_{n \ge 0} {\mathbb P}({\check{x}}_{n} \in K_{\varepsilon}) \ge 1 - {\varepsilon}$. It follows that $\mu_T(K_{\varepsilon}) \ge 1-{\varepsilon}$ for any $T > 0$. Moreover, Proposition~\ref{prop:ergo} implies that for a fixed $g \in C_c^2({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$, we can find $T_{\varepsilon}$ such that \begin{equation} \sup_{{x} \in K_{\varepsilon}} \left| {\mathcal P}_{T_{\varepsilon}}\, g({x})- {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star}\, g({\textnormal{X}}) \right| \le {\varepsilon}, \end{equation} where ${\mathcal P}_t$ represents a semigroup induced by the SDE in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}, that is, \begin{align} {\mathcal P}_t f(x) = {\mathbb E} [ f({\textnormal{X}}(t)) \,|\, {\textnormal{X}}(0) = x ], \end{align} where ${\textnormal{X}}(\cdot)$ is the solution to the SDE in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}. Setting $T = T_{\varepsilon}$, we have ${\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}}(T_{\varepsilon}) \sim \tilde{\pi}$. Since ${\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}}(\cdot)$ is a solution to \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:x-sde} with initial distribution $\mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}$, we have \begin{align*} {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \tilde\pi}\, g({\textnormal{X}}) = {\mathbb E}\, [ g ({\textnormal{X}}^{\mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}}(T_{\varepsilon}) ) \,|\, {\textnormal{X}}(0) \sim \mu_{T_{\varepsilon}} ] \overset{\eqref{eq:semigroup}}{=} \int_{{\mathbb R}^{d_x}} {\mathcal P}_{T_{\varepsilon}}\, g({x}) d \mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}({x}) \end{align*} It follows that \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \left| {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \tilde\pi}\, g({\textnormal{X}}) - {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star}\, g({\textnormal{X}}) \right| & \le \int_{{\mathbb R}^{d_x}} \left| {\mathcal P}_{T_{\varepsilon}} g({x}) -{\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star} g({\textnormal{X}}) \right| d \mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}({x})\\ & = \int_{K_{\varepsilon}} \left| {\mathcal P}_{T_{\varepsilon}} g({x}) - {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star} g({\textnormal{X}}) \right| d \mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}({x}) \\ & \qquad + \int_{K_{\varepsilon}^c} \left| {\mathcal P}_{T_{\varepsilon}} g({x}) - {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star} g({\textnormal{X}}) \right| d \mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}({x}) \\ &\le \int_{K_{\varepsilon}} \left| {\mathcal P}_{T_{\varepsilon}} g({x}) - {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star} g({\textnormal{X}}) \right| d \mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}({x}) + 2 \|g\|_\infty \mu_{T_{\varepsilon}} (K_{\varepsilon}^c) \\ & \overset{(a)}{\le} {\varepsilon} + 2\|g\|_\infty {\varepsilon}, \end{aligned} \end{equation*} where (a) is due to $\mu_{T_{\varepsilon}}(K_{\varepsilon}) \ge 1-{\varepsilon}$ and \eqref{eq:erg_diff}. Letting ${\varepsilon} \to \infty$, we obtain ${\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \tilde\pi}\, g({\textnormal{X}}) = {\mathbb E}_{{\textnormal{X}} \sim \pi^\star}\, g({\textnormal{X}}) $. For any $g \in C_c^2({\mathbb R}^{d_x})$, we can repeat the above procedure, implying $\tilde\pi = \pi^\star$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.1 (ii)
nodes.statement: Under the tightness in Lemma~\ref{lem:tight-twotime}, Proposition~\ref{prop:tight} shows that it suffices to examine the finite-dimensional distributions of ${\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(\cdot)$. Recall that ${\check{z}}_{n}$ is defined as ${\check{z}}_{n} = {\check{y}}_{n} - \sqrt{ \kappa_{n-1} } B_2 B_1^{-1} {\check{x}}_{n}$ with $\kappa_{n-1} = \beta_{n-1} / \alpha_{n-1} = o(1)$; Assumption~\ref{assump:mart-decouple-rate} implies ${\mathbb E} \| {\check{x}}_{n} \|^2 = {\mathcal O}(1)$. It follows that ${\check{y}}_{n} - {\check{z}}_{n} \overset{p}{\to} 0$. Meanwhile, from the definition in \eqref{eq:def:ybar} and \eqref{eq:def:zbar}, for each fixed $t$, ${\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(t) - {\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(t)$ is the linear combination of ${\check{y}}_{N^\beta(n,t)} - {\check{z}}_{N^\beta(n,t)}$ and ${\check{y}}_{N^\beta(n,t)+1} - {\check{z}}_{N^\beta(n,t)+1}$, both converging to the zero vector in probability. Consequently, ${\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(t) - {\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(t) \overset{p}{\to} 0$. Similarly, we could prove that for any positive integer $k$ and $t_1, \ldots, t_k$, $({\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(t_1) - {\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n}(t_1), \dots, {\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(t_k) - {\bar{\textnormal{Z}}}_{n} (t_k) ) \overset{p}{\to} 0$. Applying Slutsky's theorem and Theorem~\ref{thm:fclt-twotime}, we obtain that the finite-dimensional distributions of ${\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ converge weakly to the finite-dimensional distributions of the stationary distribution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}. Consequently, ${\bar{\textnormal{Y}}}_{n}(\cdot)$ converges weakly to the stationary distribution of \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde}. Note that Assumption~\ref{assump:hurwitz} implies that $-\left(B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta}}{2} {I} \right)$ is a Hurwitz matrix. The property of the SDE in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde} implies that the invariant distribution is ${\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_{y})$ with $\Sigma_y$ satisfying the equation in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-var} in \cite[Section~6.5]{risken1996fokker}.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\bar Y_n-\bar Z_n\to0$ in probability in fdds, then use tightness, Slutsky and Corollary 5.1.

nodes.statement: Note that Assumption~\ref{assump:hurwitz} implies that $-\left(B_3 - \frac{\tilde{\beta}}{2} {I} \right)$ is a Hurwitz matrix. The property of the SDE in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-sde} implies that the invariant distribution is ${\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_{y})$ with $\Sigma_y$ satisfying the equation in \eqref{eq:fclt-twotime:y-var} in \cite[Section~6.5]{risken1996fokker}.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 4.1
nodes.statement: From the definition of ${\check{x}}_{n}$, we have $\alpha_{n-1}^{-1/2} {\hat{x}}_{n} \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_x)$. Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime} ensures that $\alpha_{n-1} / \alpha_{n} \to 1$. Then Slutsky's theorem implies $\alpha_{n}^{-1/2} {\hat{x}}_{n} \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_x)$. Similarly, we could prove $\beta_{n}^{-1/2} {\hat{y}}_{n} \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_y)$. Moreover, since ${x}^\star = H({y}^\star)$, we have $\alpha_{n}^{-1/2} ({x}_{n} - {x}^\star) = \alpha_{n}^{-1/2} {\hat{x}}_{n} + \alpha_{n}^{-1/2} (H({y}_n) - H({y}^\star))$. Using the delta method, we have $\beta_{n}^{-1/2} (H({y}_{n}) - H({y}^\star)) \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0, H^\star \Sigma_y (H^\star)^\top ) $ with $H^\star = \nabla H({y}^\star) \in {\mathbb R}^{d_x \times d_y}$. Since $\beta_{n} / \alpha_{n} \to 0$, applying Slutsky's theorem yields $\alpha_{n}^{-1/2} (H({y}_n) - H({y}^\star)) \Rightarrow 0 $. Consequently, $\alpha_{n}^{-1/2} ({x}_{n} - {x}^\star) \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_{x})$.
nodes.statement_short: Slutsky's theorem for the rescaled errors and the delta method for $H(y_n)$.

nodes.name: Slutsky for $\hat x_n$ and $\hat y_n$
nodes.statement: From the definition of ${\check{x}}_{n}$, we have $\alpha_{n-1}^{-1/2} {\hat{x}}_{n} \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_x)$. Assumption~\ref{assump:stepsize-twotime} ensures that $\alpha_{n-1} / \alpha_{n} \to 1$. Then Slutsky's theorem implies $\alpha_{n}^{-1/2} {\hat{x}}_{n} \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_x)$. Similarly, we could prove $\beta_{n}^{-1/2} {\hat{y}}_{n} \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_y)$.
nodes.statement_short: Slutsky for $\hat x_n$ and $\hat y_n$

nodes.name: Delta method and Slutsky for $x_n-x^\star$
nodes.statement: Moreover, since ${x}^\star = H({y}^\star)$, we have $\alpha_{n}^{-1/2} ({x}_{n} - {x}^\star) = \alpha_{n}^{-1/2} {\hat{x}}_{n} + \alpha_{n}^{-1/2} (H({y}_n) - H({y}^\star))$. Using the delta method, we have $\beta_{n}^{-1/2} (H({y}_{n}) - H({y}^\star)) \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0, H^\star \Sigma_y (H^\star)^\top ) $ with $H^\star = \nabla H({y}^\star) \in {\mathbb R}^{d_x \times d_y}$. Since $\beta_{n} / \alpha_{n} \to 0$, applying Slutsky's theorem yields $\alpha_{n}^{-1/2} (H({y}_n) - H({y}^\star)) \Rightarrow 0 $. Consequently, $\alpha_{n}^{-1/2} ({x}_{n} - {x}^\star) \Rightarrow {\mathcal N}(0, \Sigma_{x})$.

nodes.name: Fast iterate update
nodes.statement: x_{n+1} &= x_{n} - \alpha_{n}\left(F(x_{n},y_{n}) + \xi_{n}\right),

nodes.name: Slow iterate update
nodes.statement: y_{n+1} &= y_{n} - \beta_{n}\left(G(x_{n},y_{n}) + \psi_{n}\right),

nodes.name: SGD step
nodes.statement: x_{n+1} &= x_{n} - \alpha_n(\nabla f(x_{n}) + \xi_{n})~\text{with}~\alpha_n = \frac{\alpha_0}{ (n+1)^a }~(0 < a < 1) ,

nodes.name: Averaging step
nodes.statement: y_{n+1} &= \frac{1}{n+1}\sum_{\tau=0}^n x_{\tau} = y_n - \beta_n(y_n-x_n)~\text{with}~\beta_n = \frac{1}{n+1}.

nodes.name: Fast auxiliary update
nodes.statement: x_{n+1} &= x_{n} - \alpha_{n} \big( \phi(s_{n})^{\top} x_{n} - \rho_{n} \delta_{n} \big) \phi(s_{n}),

nodes.name: GTD2 slow update
nodes.statement: y_{n+1} &= y_{n} - \beta_{n} \rho_{n} \big( \gamma \phi(s'_{n}) - \phi(s_{n}) \big) \phi(s_{n})^\top x_{n}, \ \qquad \mathrm{ (GTD2) }

nodes.name: TDC slow update
nodes.statement: y_{n+1} &= y_{n} - \beta_{n} \rho_{n} \big( \gamma \phi(s'_n) \phi(s_n)^\top x_{n} - \delta_{n} \phi(s_{n}) \big), \ \quad \, \mathrm{ (TDC) }

nodes.name: Velocity update
nodes.statement: x_{n+1} &= x_{n} - \alpha_n (x_n - \nabla f(y_n) - \xi_n),\\

nodes.name: Update rule of the fast error (38)
nodes.statement: {\hat{x}}_{n+1} & = {\hat{x}}_n - \alpha_n F(x_n, y_n) - \alpha_n \xi_n + H(y_n) - H(y_{n+1}),
nodes.label: eq:xhat

nodes.name: Update rule of the slow error (39)
nodes.statement: {\hat{y}}_{n+1} & = {\hat{y}}_n - \beta_n G(H(y_n), y_n) + \beta_n ( G(H(y_n), y_n) - G(x_n, y_n) ) - \beta_n \psi_n.
nodes.label: eq:yhat

nodes.name: Decomposed slow error recursion (40)
nodes.statement: {\hat{y}}_{n+1} = (I - \beta_{n} B_3) {\hat{y}}_{n} - \beta_{n} B_2 {\hat{x}}_{n} - \beta_n \psi_n - \beta_n R_n^G.
nodes.label: eq:yhat-decom

nodes.name: Rescaled slow recursion (41)
nodes.statement: {\check{y}}_{n+1} & = \sqrt{ \frac{ \beta_{n-1} }{ \beta_{n} } } ({I} - \beta_{n} B_3) {\check{y}}_{n} - \sqrt{ \beta_{n} \alpha_{n-1} } B_2 {\check{x}}_{n} - \sqrt{\beta_{n}} \psi_{n} - \sqrt{\beta_{n}} R_{n}^G \nonumber \\ & = \left( {I} - \beta_{n} B_3 + \frac{ \tilde{\beta} \beta_{n} }{2} {I} \right) {\check{y}}_{n} - \sqrt{\beta_{n} \alpha_{n} } B_2 {\check{x}}_{n} - \sqrt{\beta_n} \psi_{n} + R_{n}^y,
nodes.label: eq:lem:check-twotime:y-update

nodes.name: Slow residual decomposition (42)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} R_{n}^y & = \underbrace{ \left( \sqrt{ \frac{ \beta_{n-1} }{\beta_{n}} } - 1 - \frac{ \tilde{\beta} \beta_{n} }{2} \right) {\check{y}}_{n} }_{=: R_{n,1}^y} + \underbrace{ ( \beta_{n} - \sqrt{ \beta_{n} \beta_{n-1} } ) B_3 {\check{y}}_{n} \vphantom{ \left( \sqrt{ \frac{ \beta_{n-1} }{\beta_{n}} } \right) } }_{ =:R_{n,2}^y } \\ & \quad \ + \underbrace{ ( \sqrt{ \beta_{n} \alpha_{n} } - \sqrt{ \beta_{n} \alpha_{n-1} } ) B_2 {\check{x}}_{n} \vphantom{ \left( \sqrt{ \frac{ \beta_{n-1} }{\beta_{n}} } \right) } }_{=: R_{n,3}^y } - \underbrace{ \sqrt{\beta_{n}} R_{n}^G \vphantom{ \left( \sqrt{ \frac{ \beta_{n-1} }{\beta_{n}} } \right) } }_{ =: R_{n,4}^y }. \end{split}
nodes.label: eq:lem:check-twotime:Ry

nodes.name: Step-size ratio expansions (43)
nodes.statement: \sqrt{ \frac{ \beta_{n-1} }{ \beta_{n} } } & = \sqrt{ 1 + \beta_{n-1} ( \beta_{n}^{-1} - \beta_{n-1}^{-1} ) } = \sqrt{1 + \tilde{\beta} \beta_{n-1} + o(\beta_{n-1}) } \nonumber \\ & = \sqrt{1 + \tilde{\beta} \beta_{n} + o(\beta_{n}) } = 1 + \frac{ \tilde{\beta} \beta_{n} }{2} + o(\beta_{n}), \nonumber \\ \sqrt{ \frac{ \alpha_{n-1} }{\alpha_{n}} } & = 1 + {\mathcal O}(\beta_n), \qquad \sqrt{ \frac{ \kappa_{n-1} }{\kappa_{n}} } = 1 + {\mathcal O}(\beta_n).
nodes.label: eq:lem:check-twotime:sqrtalpha

nodes.name: Decomposed fast error recursion (45)
nodes.label: eq:xhat-decom

nodes.name: Rescaled fast recursion (46)
nodes.label: eq:lem:check-twotime:x-update

nodes.name: Fast residual decomposition (47)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} R_{n}^x & = \underbrace{ \left( \sqrt{ \frac{\alpha_{n-1}}{\alpha_{n}} } - 1 \right) {\check{x}}_{n} }_{=: R_{n,1}^x} + \underbrace{ (\alpha_{n} - \sqrt{ \alpha_{n} \alpha_{n-1} }) B_1 {\check{x}}_{n} \vphantom{\left( \sqrt{ \frac{\alpha_{n-1}}{\alpha_{n}} } \right) } }_{=: R_{n,2}^x} + \underbrace{ \sqrt{\frac{ \alpha_{n-1} }{ \alpha_{n} } } \beta_{n} H^\star B_2 {\check{x}}_{n} \vphantom{\left( \sqrt{ \frac{\alpha_{n-1}}{\alpha_{n}} } \right) }}_{=: R_{n,3}^x} \\ & \qquad + \underbrace{ \sqrt{ \frac{\beta_{n-1}}{\alpha_{n}} } \beta_{n} H^\star B_3 {\check{y}}_{n} \vphantom{\left( \sqrt{ \frac{\alpha_{n-1}}{\alpha_{n}} } \right) } }_{=: R_{n,4}^x} - \underbrace{ \frac{1}{ \sqrt{\alpha_{n}} } R_{n}^{\nabla H} }_{=: R_{n,5}^x} - \underbrace{ \frac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_{n}}} R_{n}^{H} }_{=: R_{n,6}^x} - \underbrace{ \sqrt{\alpha_{n}} R_{n}^F \vphantom{\frac{\beta_{n}}{\sqrt{ \alpha_{n} } } } }_{=:R_{n,7}^x } + \underbrace{ \frac{\beta_{n}}{\sqrt{ \alpha_{n} } } H^\star R_{n}^G }_{=:R_{n,8}^x}. \end{split}
nodes.label: eq:lem:check-twotime:Rx

nodes.name: Fast residual upper bounds (48)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \| {\mathbb E} [ R_{n}^x | {\mathcal F}_n ] \| & = {\mathcal O}( \beta_{n} \alpha_{n}^{-1/2}) (\| {\hat{x}}_{n} \| + \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \| ) + {\mathcal O} (\beta_{n} \alpha_{n}^{-1/2}) ( \| {\hat{x}}_{n} \|^{1+{\delta_H}} + \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \|^{1+{\delta_H}} ) \\ & \quad \ + {\mathcal O} (\beta_{n}^{1+{\delta_H}} \alpha_{n}^{-1/2}) \| \psi_{n} \|^{1+{\delta_H}} + {\mathcal O}(\alpha_{n}^{1/2}) ( \| {\hat{x}}_{n} \|^{1+{\delta_F}} + \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \|^{1+{\delta_F}} ) \\ & \quad \ + {\mathcal O} (\beta_{n} \alpha_{n}^{-1/2}) ( \| {\hat{x}}_{n} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} + \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \|^{1+{\delta_G}} ), \\ \| R_{n}^x \| & = {\mathcal O}( \| {\mathbb E} [ R_{n}^x | {\mathcal F}_n ] \| ) + {\mathcal O} (\beta_{n} \alpha_{n}^{-1/2}) \| {\hat{y}}_{n} \|^{\delta_H} \| \psi_{n} \|. \end{split}
nodes.label: eq:lem:check-twotime:Rx-upper

nodes.name: Drift term bound (49)
nodes.statement: \| {\bf B}^{(1x,n)}_{t,s} \| & \le \ssum{k}{N^\alpha(n,t)}{N^\alpha(n,s) - 1} \alpha_{k} \left\| B_1 {\check{x}}_{k} - \frac{R_{k}^x}{\alpha_{k}} \right\| + (s - \underline{s}^\alpha_{n}) \left\| B_1 {\check{x}}_{N^\alpha(n,s)} - \frac{ R_{N^\alpha(n,s)}^x }{ \alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)} } \right\| \nonumber \\ & \le \ssum{k}{N^\alpha(n,t)}{N^\alpha(n,s)} \alpha_{k} \left\| B_1 {\check{x}}_{k} - \frac{R_{k}^x}{\alpha_{k}} \right\|.

nodes.name: Uniform L2 bound for the fast drift (50)
nodes.statement: \sup_{n} {\mathbb E} \left\| B_1 {\check{x}}_{n} - \frac{R_{n}^x }{ \alpha_{n}} \right\|^2 \le 2 \| B_1 \|^2 \sup_{n} {\mathbb E} \| {\check{x}}_{n} \|^2 + 2 \sup_{n} \frac{ {\mathbb E} \| R_{n}^x \|^2}{\alpha_{n}^2} \le C^{ti}_x

nodes.name: Second-moment bound of the drift term (51)
nodes.statement: {\mathbb E} \| {\bf B}^{(1x,n)}_{t,s} \|^2 & \overset{\eqref{eq:lem:tight-twotime:B1x-1}}{\le} {\mathbb E} \left( \ssum{k}{N^\alpha(n,t)}{N^\alpha(n,s)} \alpha_{k} \left\| B_1 {\check{x}}_{k} - \frac{R_{k}^x}{\alpha_{k}} \right\|\right)^2 \nonumber \\ & \le \left( \ssum{k}{N^\alpha(n,t)}{N^\alpha(n,s)} \alpha_{k} \right) \left( \ssum{k}{N^\alpha(n,t)}{N^\alpha(n,s)} \alpha_{k} {\mathbb E} \left\| B_1 {\check{x}}_{k} - \frac{R_{k}^x}{\alpha_{k}} \right\|^2 \right) \nonumber \\ & \overset{ \eqref{eq:lem:tight-twotime:l2bound-x} }{\le} C^{ti}_x \left( \ssum{k}{N^\alpha(n,t)}{N^\alpha(n,s)} \alpha_{k} \right)^2 \le C^{ti}_x ( s-t + 2 \alpha_{n} )^2 \overset{(a)}{\le} K_1(s-t)^2,
nodes.label: eq:lem:tight-twotime:B1x

nodes.name: p-th moment bound of the noise term (53)
nodes.statement: {\mathbb E} \| \mbox{\boldmath$\Xi$\unboldmath}^{(n)}_{t,s} \|^p & \le C^{ti}_p C^{ti}_\xi \left( \frac{ s-t + 2\alpha_{n} }{ \alpha_{ N^\alpha(n, s) } } + 1 \right)^{\frac{p}{2}-1} \alpha_{n}^{ \frac{p}{2} - 1 } \ssum{k}{ N^\alpha(n,t) }{N^\alpha(n,s) } \alpha_{k} \nonumber \\ & \le C^{ti}_p C^{ti}_\xi ( s-t + 3 \alpha_{n} )^\frac{p}{2} \left( \frac{ \alpha_{n} }{ \alpha_{ N^\alpha(n, s) } } \right)^{\frac{p}{2}-1 } \nonumber \\ & \overset{ (a) }{\le} C^{ti}_p C^{ti}_\xi C^{ti}_\alpha ( s-t + 3 \alpha_{n} )^\frac{p}{2} \overset{ (b) }{\le} K_2 ( s-t )^\frac{p}{2},
nodes.label: eq:lem:tight-twotime:xii

nodes.name: Bounds for slow drift and noise terms (54)
nodes.statement: {\mathbb E} \| {\bf B}^{(3y,n)}_{t,s} \|^2 \le K_3 (s-t)^2 \quad \text{ and } \quad {\mathbb E} \| \mbox{\boldmath$\Psi$\unboldmath}^{(n)}_{t,s} \|^p \le K_4 (s-t)^\frac{p}{2}.

nodes.name: Interpolation error bounds (68)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} {\mathbb E} | f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t)) - f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}^{(n)}_{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}}) | & \lesssim {\mathbb E} \| {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(t) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}^{(n)}_{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n} } \| \lesssim \sqrt{\alpha_{N^\alpha(n,t)}} = o(1), \\ {\mathbb E} \left| \int_t^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} {\mathcal A}^x f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) \,\mathrm{d} s \right| & \lesssim \int_t^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} 1 \,\mathrm{d} s = o(1), \\ {\mathbb E} \left| \int_0^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} \left( {\mathcal A}^x f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n} (\underline{s}^\alpha_{n}) ) - {\mathcal A}^x f({\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s)) \right) \,\mathrm{d} s \right| & \lesssim \int_0^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} {\mathbb E} \| {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n}(s) - {\bar{\textnormal{X}}}_{n} (\underline{s}^\alpha_{n} ) \| \,\mathrm{d} s \\ & \lesssim \int_0^{\overline{t}^\alpha_{n}} \sqrt{\alpha_{N^\alpha(n,s)} } ds \lesssim \sqrt{\alpha_{n}} = o(1). \end{split}
nodes.label: eq:thm:fclt-twotime:res1

nodes.name: Accumulated generator residual bound (69)
nodes.statement: {\mathbb E} \left| \ssum{k}{n}{\bar{N}^\alpha(n,t) - 1} R^f_k \right| \le \ssum{k}{n}{\bar{N}^\alpha(n,t) - 1} \alpha_{k} {\mathbb E} \left| \frac{R^f_k}{\alpha_{k}} \right| \le \sup_{k' \ge n} {\mathbb E} \left| \frac{R^f_{k'}}{\alpha_{k'}} \right| \cdot \ssum{k}{n}{\bar{N}^\alpha(n,t) - 1} \alpha_{k} \lesssim o(1).
nodes.label: eq:thm:fclt-twotime:res2
